animation_physics.analyze_animation.summary: Analyze an Animation Sequence's motion from its own frames: how far and fast the root travels and turns, when each foot is planted and how fast a planted foot still moves, how closely the last frame meets the first, and the bones with the sharpest rotation spikes.

animation_physics.auto_blend_space.summary: Lay out a locomotion blend space from its clips' own motion: each Animation Sequence in animationPaths is read from its frames (a root that travels is the clip's motion; a root that stays is an in-place clip, read from its planted feet, which slide backward at the ground speed) and placed by its speed and direction in the character's frame. forwardAxis is the way the character faces in its clips (+Y for the UE mannequin). axes picks what each axis holds: speed (cm/s), direction (degrees: 0 forward, +90 right, 180 back), forwardSpeed or rightSpeed (signed cm/s); default speed for a Blend Space 1D, direction and speed for a Blend Space. The axes are set to hold every sample: speed from 0 to the top speed rounded up to 50, signed speeds symmetric, direction -180 to 180 with wrapping input. A clip within 10 degrees of backward takes both direction edges, an idle (under 10 cm/s) takes every direction used, at speed 0, and a position another clip or a kept sample already holds is refused (refused in that clip's row). The listed clips replace the samples, or with keepSamples join them, in one undo step, saved unless save is false; dryRun answers the same and changes nothing. Refused, changing nothing: BLENDSPACE_NOT_FOUND, ANIMATION_NOT_FOUND, ANIMATION_INCOMPATIBLE (another skeleton, or an additive type the blend space or the other clips do not share), EMPTY_ANIMATION, BONE_NOT_FOUND (a bone named in feet), INVALID_ARGUMENT (an Aim Offset, an unknown axis, axes that do not fit the blend space).

animation_physics.bind_cloth_to_skeletal.summary: Bind a cloth asset to a skeletal mesh section so that section simulates as cloth, chosen by clothOp. bind takes a cloth asset already on the mesh (clothAssetName, as availableClothAssets lists them); assign also takes clothAssetPath and adds that asset to the mesh first. meshLodIndex, sectionIndex and assetLodIndex (default 0 each) pick where; a LOD or section that does not exist is BIND_FAILED, and naming no asset lists the candidates (CLOTH_ASSET_REQUIRED). Saved unless save is false (saved).

animation_physics.cleanup.summary: Delete animation assets by path (artifacts), each closed in any editor and garbage collected first. Paths that do not exist are listed under missing; when none of them existed the call still succeeds, saying nothing needed removing. No undo and no reference check: an asset others still use leaves them pointing at nothing.

animation_physics.configure_anim_graph_n.summary: Change an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph, chosen by edit. add_layered_blend_per_bone adds a Layered Blend Per Bone node that layers each blend pose over the bones its branch filters name (a bone not on the skeleton is BONE_NOT_FOUND) and names the node for wiring. set_value sets a node setting (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, NodeComment) or the animation an asset player plays, by node name or nodeId, and reads it back; NODE_NOT_FOUND lists the nodes and AMBIGUOUS_NODE the matches. Both save unless save is false.

animation_physics.configure_socket.summary: Sockets on a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), chosen by socketOp; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create (add) puts socketName on attachBoneName, which both require, at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one); a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a taken name SOCKET_EXISTS. configure (modify) changes an existing socket: attachBoneName moves it, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given; a missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND and a call naming nothing to change is refused. Each change is one undo step.

animation_physics.configure_vehicle.summary: Make a placed skeletal-mesh actor drive as a wheeled vehicle (Chaos Vehicles): adds an MCP_VehicleMovement4W movement component when it has none, then sets the wheels (replacing them), engine, transmission, mass and drag. Each value is set by name, so one an engine version lacks is skipped without a word; only that actor changes, and nothing is saved until its level is.

animation_physics.create_animation_asset.summary: Create an animation asset: a sequence, montage, blend space (1D/2D), aim offset, pose asset from a sequence, or procedural animation.

animation_physics.create_animation_bluep.summary: Create an Animation Blueprint named name in path (default /Game/Blueprints) for the skeleton at skeletonPath, or the one skeletalMeshPath is built on (SKELETON_NOT_FOUND when that does not load; without either it has no skeleton), from parentClass (default AnimInstance; a class that is no AnimInstance is INVALID_PARENT_CLASS). An Animation Blueprint already there is kept and answered with existingAsset; any other asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH and is left alone. It is compiled and saved unless save is false (saved).

animation_physics.create_control_rig.summary: Create a Control Rig Blueprint at path/name (path default /Game/ControlRigs), from skeletalMeshPath or skeletonPath when given, saved unless save is false. UE 5.5 and later build the rig for that mesh (modularRig makes a Modular Rig); 5.1 to 5.4 only set the preview mesh and ignore modularRig; UE 5.0 answers NOT_SUPPORTED. The reply's assetPath is where the asset landed.

animation_physics.create_physical_materi.summary: Create or tune a physical material: friction (an icy or slippery floor, a grippy one), bounce (restitution), density and how two touching surfaces combine them. A mesh takes it through control_actor edit_component property PhysMaterialOverride (edit_scs set_property on a class template).
terms: make a ball, a cube or a box bounce

animation_physics.create_skeleton.summary: Create a Skeleton asset holding one root bone (rootBoneName, default Root) at path, or path/name when name is given (without name the last part of path names it), under /Game, /Engine or /Temp. Saved unless save is false; the reply's saved says whether it reached disk (a /Temp skeleton never does).

animation_physics.edit_anim_graph.summary: Edit an Animation Blueprint graph: blend, cached-pose and slot nodes, state machines, states, transitions and transition rules, blend trees. Any other AnimGraph node (Two Bone IK, Modify Bone, Blend Space Player) is created by class with manage_blueprint edit_graph create_node.

animation_physics.edit_animation.summary: Edit an animation sequence: bone tracks and keys, curve keys, notifies, footstep sounds, sync markers, additive and root-motion settings, length, play rate, aim-offset samples.
terms: make an animation play faster or slower
slow down or speed up an animation

animation_physics.edit_blend_space.summary: Edit a Blend Space or Aim Offset (assetPath), chosen by edit. add_sample places animationPath at sampleValue (a number on a 1D blend space, {x, y} on a 2D one; the axis range grows to fit) and returns sampleIndex; a position another sample holds, or an animation of another skeleton or additive type, is refused (SAMPLE_REJECTED). set_axis_settings changes one axis (Horizontal, the default, or Vertical; a 1D blend space has Horizontal only): only the axisName, minValue, maxValue and gridDivisions sent change, minValue stays below maxValue, and the reply gives the axis as it now is. set_interpolation_settings sets input smoothing on every axis and the sample weight speed, only the fields sent. rebuild drops invalid samples, rebuilds the grid and recompiles the Animation Blueprints that use it (compileReferencers, default true), listing any that fail. Saved unless save is false (saved); add_sample, set_axis_settings and set_interpolation_settings are one undo step each.

animation_physics.edit_control_rig.summary: Edit a Control Rig: add a unit node (list_rig_units finds them), connect or disconnect pins, set a pin value, remove a node, import the skeleton's bones, add a bone, null or control, or remove an element; one edit or many steps, then one compile and save. The reply lists what each edit made (a new node with its pins).

animation_physics.edit_montage.summary: Edit an animation montage, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). add_montage_section adds a section at startTime (a name already there is SECTION_EXISTS) and set_section_timing moves one; link_sections makes fromSection play into toSection (SECTION_NOT_FOUND lists the sections); add_montage_slot adds an animation of a skeleton the montage takes as a segment of a slot, refused where it would overlap one already there, and grows the montage to fit; add_montage_notify adds a notify of notifyClass, or a named notify event, at a time within the montage; set_blend_in and set_blend_out set blendTime and blendOption, refusing a call with neither. Each edit is one undo step.

animation_physics.edit_morph_target.summary: Create a morph target from vertex deltas, replace its deltas, import morph targets from another mesh, or set a morph target value on an actor. create, set_deltas and import write the mesh's source data, so the morph targets last through every rebuild.

animation_physics.edit_physics_asset.summary: Create a physics asset or edit it, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create builds bodies and joints from skeletalMeshPath as the editor's Create Physics Asset does, at outputPath (or name in path; default <mesh>_PhysicsAsset beside the mesh): geomType Capsule (default), Box, Sphere, TaperedCapsule (cloth only), SingleConvexHull or MultiConvexHull, any other name refused; bones shorter than minBoneSize get no body unless bodyForAll; createConstraints joins the bodies; assignToMesh (default false) makes the mesh use it; a build that makes no body is refused (BODY_GENERATION_FAILED). add_body gives boneName a Capsule (default), Sphere or Box shape sized by radius and length or width, depth and height, placed by center and rotation; a bone that already has a body gets the shape added to it (created false), and a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND. configure_body (modify_body) sets mass (kg, above 0, as the body's mass override), linearDamping, angularDamping, collisionEnabled and simulatePhysics (true simulates with the ragdoll, false is Kinematic and follows the animation), and refuses a call that sets none of them. add_constraint joins bodyA and bodyB with a joint Limited to 45 degrees on every axis (both bodies must exist, BODY_NOT_FOUND; a second joint on the pair is CONSTRAINT_EXISTS); set_constraint changes the pair's joint or makes one; configure_constraint_limits sets swing1, swing2 and twist angles and motions from limits. assign makes skeletalMeshPath (or meshPath) use physicsAssetPath, saving the mesh. Every edit but create is one undo step.

animation_physics.edit_skeleton.summary: Edit a skeleton (skeletonPath), chosen by edit. add_bone adds boneName under parentBoneName (needed once the skeleton has bones; a taken name is BONE_EXISTS) at location, rotation and scale relative to the parent. set_bone_parent moves boneName, with its children, under parentBoneName, where it keeps its place in the reference pose: its own descendants are refused, and the parent it already has changes nothing (changed false). Both change the skeleton asset only; the skeletal meshes on it keep their own bones. set_bone_transform rewrites boneName in the reference pose of the skeletal mesh (skeletalMeshPath, or the skeleton's preview mesh), only the location, rotation or scale sent, in one undo step. create_virtual_bone adds a virtual bone from sourceBoneName to targetBoneName named boneName, or VB <source>_<target>; the engine's VB prefix is added when missing. rename_bone renames virtual bones only; a real bone takes a reimport of the mesh (OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED). Saved unless save is false (saved).

animation_physics.edit_skin_weights.summary: Edit skeletal-mesh skin weights: auto-skin, set vertex weights, copy them from another skinned mesh, mirror one side onto the other, or prune tiny influences. Weights are always normalized on write.

animation_physics.get_animation_info.summary: Read an animation asset: sequence or montage length, frame rate, notifies, curves, root motion and additive flags, and the bone tracks of a sequence; montage sections and slots; blend space axes; anim Blueprint skeleton and parent class.

animation_physics.get_control_rig.summary: Read a Control Rig: each node of its graph with its unit and pins (path, direction, type, default, linked), the links between pins, its hierarchy (bones, nulls, controls with their parents) and whether it compiled; node names one node with every struct member pin.

animation_physics.get_skeleton_info.summary: Read a skeleton, skeletal mesh or Physics Asset, chosen by info (a skeletal mesh path reads its skeleton, or its assigned Physics Asset). skeleton gives counts of bones, virtual bones and sockets; bones lists every bone in hierarchy order with index, parent and reference-pose location, the names other calls take (layer filters, sockets, IK, physics bodies); sockets lists each socket with its bone and offset; virtual_bones lists virtual bones with source and target; bone_transform reads one bone's reference-pose transform and parent; morph_targets lists a mesh's morph targets and their delta counts; physics_asset reads a Physics Asset's bodies (the shapes in each) and constraints; physics_bodies lists only the body names. A path that does not load is SKELETON_NOT_FOUND or MESH_NOT_FOUND, a bone the skeleton lacks BONE_NOT_FOUND.

animation_physics.list_rig_units.summary: Find the units a Control Rig graph can hold (Get Transform, Two Bone IK, Aim, math and more): each unit's object path, name and category, for edit_control_rig add_unit.

animation_physics.play_montage.summary: Play an animation montage on a placed skeletal actor (the playing one while Play In Editor runs): Montage_Play through its Anim Instance at playRate, or the montage as a single-node animation when the mesh has none, which switches that component's animation mode. The reply gives playMode and montageLength; outside play the actor does not tick, so nothing moves, playing is false and a warning says so.
terms: play an animation on a character

animation_physics.remove_skeleton_elemen.summary: Remove part of a skeleton or physics asset, chosen by element. bone removes boneName from the skeleton: with removeChildren its whole branch goes, otherwise its children move up to its parent and keep their place in the reference pose; the only root a skeleton has is refused. socket removes socketName from the skeleton (a socket defined on a mesh is not found here). physics_body removes the body of boneName from physicsAssetPath together with every constraint that uses it. A missing bone, socket or body is refused; each removal is one undo step. Saved unless save is false (saved).

animation_physics.setup_ik.summary: Set up IK: create an IK rig or IK retargeter, a Control Rig for IK solvers, or set which source chain drives each target chain of a retargeter.

animation_physics.setup_physics_simulati.summary: Make an actor simulate physics: a placed prop (actorName) falls, tumbles and can be pushed while the game plays, weighing massKg when given (the reply gives its mass either way), or a skeletal mesh gets a Physics Asset with bodies made for its bones.
terms: a cube or a crate that falls with gravity
make a crate heavier or lighter
set the mass of a crate or a prop in kg
add a box the player can push

animation_physics.setup_ragdoll.summary: Make a skeletal actor go limp in the running game (Play or Simulate), chosen by ragdoll. setup switches every physics body of its skeletal mesh to simulate, assigning physicsAssetPath first when given; activate turns that on or off (activate, default true). A mesh with no physics asset is refused (NO_PHYSICS_ASSET), and ragdollActive reads back whether it now simulates. A Character keeps its capsule and movement running, so stop those as well for a body that falls.

animation_physics.setup_retargeting.summary: Retarget animation onto another skeleton through an IK Retargeter, baking new AnimSequences.

animation_physics.skin_mesh_to_skeleton.summary: Skin a static mesh to a skeleton so it deforms with the animation, producing a SkeletalMesh.

asset.bulk_delete.summary: Delete every asset under folderPath (subfolders included; the folders stay) or the listed assetPaths, then resolve old redirectors there. An asset something outside the delete still uses is kept and listed in referenced with what uses it; deleted lists the paths actually gone.

asset.caption_assets.summary: Keep captions and tags for assets, as the calling agent writes them after looking at thumbnail_sheet: each {assetPath, caption (what it shows, up to 300 characters), tags (up to 12 words or short phrases)} replaces that asset's caption; an entry with an empty caption and no tags takes the caption away (also for an asset since deleted). They are kept in the project's caption file (Saved/EngineWire/AssetCaptions.json), never in the assets, which stay untouched; find_assets_like searches them. All or nothing: ASSET_NOT_FOUND (missing lists the paths), INVALID_PATH or WRITE_FAILED (the file could not be written) keeps none.

asset.create_folder.summary: Create a Content Browser folder at path (under /Game or another allowed root); one that exists already answers success with alreadyExisted true. An empty folder may be gone after an editor restart until an asset is saved in it.

asset.create_render_target.summary: Create a Texture Render Target 2D asset for a scene capture or a Blueprint to draw into: width and height (default 1024, at most 8192), format (default RGBA8), saved unless save is false (saved says whether it was written). A render target already at that path is kept as it is and answered with alreadyExists and its own size; another asset there is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.

asset.delete.summary: Delete one or more assets, or whole folders. A folder of thousands of assets can take minutes and reports how far it has got as it goes; when the call answers before the delete is done (task.state running), the delete carries on, so check the folder with asset.list instead of deleting again.

asset.duplicate.summary: Copy an asset, or a whole folder with its sub-folders, and save the copies. destinationPath is a folder (the copy keeps the source name, or takes newName), a full asset path, or a bare name beside the source; newName alone copies beside the source. A taken destination is refused (DESTINATION_EXISTS) and a missing source answers ASSET_NOT_FOUND; a folder copy skips assets whose destination is taken (duplicatedCount under assetCount). Each asset is copied on its own: what referred to the original, placed actors and the other copies included, still does. A copied Blueprint gets its Math Expressions rebound and a copied Niagara system is compiled, so both work at once.

asset.edit_material_instance.summary: Add a parameter expression to a material or material function, reset every parameter override on a material instance, or give an instance another parent material (reparent: its own shaders are compiled again for it). To override a parameter value on an instance, use set_material_parameter.

asset.export_mesh.summary: Export a static or skeletal mesh asset (or an animation sequence, on its preview mesh) to a file through the editor's own exporters: glb (default: one self-contained glTF binary), gltf (JSON with its buffers and textures beside it), fbx or obj. It is written under Saved/Exports unless outputPath says otherwise; the reply gives the path, the size, the files written beside it and any exporter warnings.

asset.find_assets_like.summary: Find assets by what they are and what they look like, best first: query words are matched (BM25) against each asset's name and folders, class, and the captions and tags caption_assets kept; likeAsset finds assets like an example: by its own name and folder words (its pack), by the look of its stored thumbnail (colours, edge directions, outline) and by its size, among assets of its class unless class says otherwise; colour (#RRGGBB or a name: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink, brown, black, white, grey) ranks assets by how much of their thumbnail is that colour; sizeCm by how near their largest dimension is (meshes). Every criterion given ranks the assets it can judge and the rankings are fused (Reciprocal Rank Fusion); each row's why names the criteria that ranked it and its place there. The index of the assets (Saved/EngineWire/AssetIndex.json) is brought up to date first, reading thumbnails from the packages without loading the assets, for up to 10 s a call: pending counts those not read yet (call again). Refused with ASSET_NOT_FOUND (likeAsset), INVALID_PATH, INVALID_ARGUMENT (a colour it cannot read; a query with no word of two letters or more and nothing else asked).

asset.import.summary: Import a file inside the project folder (sourcePath, relative to the project or absolute under it; a path outside is SECURITY_VIOLATION, a missing file SOURCE_NOT_FOUND) as an asset at destinationPath: a folder keeps the file name, an object path names it. An asset already there is replaced only with overwrite (DESTINATION_OCCUPIED otherwise): a plain file replaces it in place, keeping what points at it, while an FBX with skeleton or animation options deletes it first (REPLACE_FAILED while something still uses it). skeletonPath imports an FBX animation take onto that skeleton, or with importMesh binds the imported skeletal mesh to it. The reply names assetPath (the mesh when the file holds one), alsoImported (its takes, materials and textures) and saved (default true); a static or skeletal mesh it made with closed parts wound inside out (up to 1 million triangles are checked) gets a warning naming it, the count and the inspect.check_mesh call that lists them.

asset.import_marketplace_asset.summary: Bring a marketplace asset into the project: add a Fab listing (it returns at once with an operationId; poll query_marketplace lookup=fab_import_status), cancel a Fab import that is queued or downloading, download a Fab asset, or import a Megascans asset.

asset.inspect_asset.summary: Inspect an asset: metadata, what it uses or what uses it (referencers), its dependency graph, an exists-and-loads check, a directory report (every asset under a folder, or with reportType unreferenced only those nothing uses), or a diff: its unsaved changes against the saved file, or a compare with another asset.

asset.list.summary: List the assets and subfolders in a folder (path), the registered content sources, or the instances of a material.

asset.maintain_content.summary: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.

asset.move.summary: Move an asset to a new path, or a whole folder: every asset under it moves (sub-folders kept) and references, redirectors and project settings follow.

asset.nanite_rebuild_mesh.summary: Turn Nanite on for a static mesh asset, or several in one call (assetPaths), and set the share of its triangles Nanite keeps; each mesh is rebuilt and saved, and the reply reads naniteEnabled and trianglePercent back from it.

asset.process_asset.summary: Process an asset, chosen by process. thumbnail renders its preview at width by height (default 512, 1 to 4096) and stores it in the asset, which is left unsaved (thumbnailCached; engine content keeps its own), writing it as a PNG as well when outputPath names a project-relative file. lods gives static meshes lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each half the triangles of the one before), replacing LODs past the count and hand-tuned settings, then rebuilds and saves each. mesh_materials sets the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or name, so every placement shows them; an engine mesh changes for this session only and is never saved (saveSkippedReason). mesh_collision sets the collision of a static mesh asset (a fitted box, sphere or capsule, its render triangles, or none), rebuilds every placed copy and saves it. lods and mesh_collision refuse engine meshes (ENGINE_CONTENT): duplicate one into /Game first.
terms: assign materials to a static mesh

asset.query_asset.summary: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets (graph nodes by title too, so every call of a function), the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.

asset.query_marketplace.summary: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library, and the status of a Fab import that is running.

asset.reimport.summary: Bring assets up to date with their source files, as the Content Browser's Reimport does but with no dialog: each from the file it was imported from (its import data), or, for one asset, from sourceFile (a file inside the project, as import takes it). Every asset is checked before any is reimported: ASSET_NOT_FOUND, ENGINE_CONTENT, NOT_REIMPORTABLE (no source file recorded: made in the editor, or a kind never imported) SOURCE_FILE_MISSING (sourceFile not there) and SECURITY_VIOLATION (sourceFile outside the project) change nothing. An asset whose recorded file is gone is listed under missingSources and left as it is; when that leaves none, SOURCE_FILE_MISSING. Saved after (save, default true); editor undo does not take a reimport back. REIMPORT_FAILED names the ones the importer refused (the editor log says why). A reimported static or skeletal mesh with closed parts wound inside out gets a warning, as import gives.

asset.rename.summary: Rename an asset or a folder in place (newName), or move it (destinationPath); a folder takes every asset under it along. Several unrelated assets in one call: maintain_content bulk_rename with renames.

asset.set_metadata.summary: Write package metadata on an asset (kind metadata: key/value pairs, numbers and booleans as text, objects and arrays as JSON text, null skipped; updatedKeys counts them) or tag it (tags: each tag becomes a metadata key set to true; appliedTags). The asset is marked unsaved, not saved (save_all keeps it). Package metadata is editor-only: cooking strips it, so the running game cannot read it.

asset.source_control.summary: Revision control for the project, chosen by sourceControlOp: init makes a Git repository at the project root with an Unreal .gitignore and a first commit and turns the Git provider on; commit_all stages and commits every change (alreadyClean when there is none); enable turns a provider on or switches to it (Git, Perforce, Subversion); checkout and submit check assets out and in through the provider that is on, listing paths that name no asset (skipped). Git runs on a worker and every step comes back with its output.

asset.thumbnail_sheet.summary: Show a page of a folder's assets as one numbered picture: each tile is the thumbnail the editor keeps for the asset (stored in its package when it was saved from the editor, or made this session), labelled with its number and name, three across; an asset with none shows a plain grey tile and thumbnail false in its row (none is rendered: that would load the asset; asset.process_asset process=thumbnail makes one). By default only assets without a caption are shown (uncaptionedOnly), so captioning a page with caption_assets and asking again brings the next ones. Rows give each number its assetPath and class; nextOffset is the next page. The picture is returned as an image and saved under Saved/Captures (file), unless keepFile is false.

blueprint.add_behaviour.summary: Write gameplay logic into an Actor Blueprint in one call: health that takes damage and dies, damage on touch, a pickup that heals or counts (coins, keys), a sprint key for a Character, a key that shoots projectiles for a pawn, a pawn that chases the player or patrols a route, a turret that turns to the player and fires at them, an enemy the player defeats by jumping on it, a barrel that explodes when it dies, a moving platform or elevator, walk, look and jump controls for a Character, a pawn that respawns when it falls or dies (with checkpoints), a goal that ends the level when the player reaches it, a pad that launches a Character, a teleporter, a platform that falls when a pawn lands on it, a time limit, a spawner that keeps spawning an actor class, a dash key for a Character, a sound or a cutscene that plays when the player walks into an area, the health of the player or a count such as coins or score on screen, a hint on screen while the player is in an area, or a game over screen that restarts the level when the player dies. Logic none of these covers is written with edit_graph.
terms: make an npc talk when the player comes close
show how many coins or gems are left
make a bouncy mushroom or trampoline
health of a castle, a base or a building
make the enemy die when shot or hit
push back whoever touches or hits it
add a health potion or a health pack
faster while a key is held
make bullets or projectiles hurt enemies
make the enemy attack the player
cannon that fires at the player
jump on enemies to kill them
platform that moves back and forth
platform that moves up and down

blueprint.add_content_widget.summary: Add a content widget to a Widget Blueprint: text, rich text, image, button, check box, combo box, slider, spin box, progress bar, text input, list/tree view, or any widget class.

blueprint.add_function.summary: Add a function or an event to a Blueprint; an event can be bound to a component's or a Widget Blueprint widget's delegate (OnClicked), and a function named after one the parent lets a Blueprint override (a widget's OnKeyDown) is made as that override.

blueprint.add_game_widget.summary: Add a ready-made HUD piece to a Widget Blueprint: health bar, ammo counter, crosshair, minimap, compass, damage indicator, interaction prompt, objective or quest tracker.
terms: a hit marker on the crosshair

blueprint.add_panel_widget.summary: Add a panel widget to a Widget Blueprint: canvas, overlay, boxes, grids, border, scroll/size/scale box, spacer, safe zone, switcher, wrap box, or a whole layout of panels, text and images with their looks in one call (widget_tree).

blueprint.add_widget_viewmodel.summary: Add a viewmodel to a Widget Blueprint, as the widget editor's Viewmodels panel does: viewModelClass is a viewmodel class or Blueprint (list_viewmodels lists them), name its name in the widget (default the editor's, from the class), creation create_instance (the widget makes its own, default; an abstract class is manual) or manual (the game hands one over with the widget's setter). One undo step; compiled and saved. Refusals change nothing: NOT_A_VIEWMODEL (the class sends no field notifications), NAME_TAKEN, CLASS_NOT_FOUND, NOT_FOUND (no Widget Blueprint there), MVVM_DISABLED.
terms: use a viewmodel in a widget

blueprint.arrange_widgets.summary: Place the children of a Canvas Panel by how they relate instead of by coordinates: one left of, right of, above or below another (gap: exactly that far apart, else at least 0), edges or centre lines lined up (alignLeft, alignRight, alignTop, alignBottom, alignCenterX, alignCenterY over widgets), the same width or height, a width or height, an inset from an edge of the panel, or centred in it. Each relation is required, or preferred with a strength (strong, medium, weak) and kept as far as the required ones allow (Cassowary); besides them every widget stays inside the panel and no narrower than its text (strong), and otherwise as large as it is and then where it is (weak): set in from an edge, it moves there rather than stretching. The boxes are solved at the reference resolution (default 1920x1080, the project's DPI scaling applied) and each widget's anchors follow what holds it (an inset from the right anchors it right, centred anchors it at the centre, insets from both sides stretch it, a widget tied to another follows that one), so the layout holds at other sizes; every relation is then measured again at each of resolutions (default 1920x1080, 1280x720 and 3440x1440) and the reply says where it holds. One undo step; compiled and saved; dryRun reports the boxes and anchors and changes nothing. A required relation that cannot hold with the required ones before it is UNSATISFIABLE (which one) and nothing changes; a widget not in a Canvas Panel, or in another one than the rest, is NOT_A_CANVAS.
terms: place widgets relative to each other

blueprint.audit_widget.summary: Check a Widget Blueprint the way a UI reviewer would, at several screen sizes: it is laid out offscreen as the game creates it (as preview_widget draws it) at each of resolutions, and every visible widget is judged. Findings: off_screen (part or all of a widget past the screen edge), clipped_text (a text needing more room than its box gives, without wrapping), overlap (buttons on buttons, text on text, text across a button it is not part of; images are backdrops and not judged), unsafe (text or a button inside the margin outside the title-safe area, safeZone), small_target (with touch: a button, check box, slider or text box under 44 Slate units on its short side), low_contrast (the WCAG 2.x ratio of a text's colour to what is drawn behind it, under 4.5:1, or 3:1 for text of 18 pt or 14 pt bold; where nothing is drawn behind it, the preview's dark backdrop stands in for the game), misaligned (two neighbouring widgets whose edges miss each other by 1-4 px, unless another edge or the centre of that direction lines them up exactly). Each finding names its widget (and the other one), the sizes it shows at, its rect at the first of them and what is wrong; the most severe come first, 100 at most. Reads only.

blueprint.bind_widget.summary: Bind a widget property to a variable or pure function (text, color, enabled, visibility, progress bar percent or slider value; the converting getter is generated), wire an event to a function (on-clicked, hovered, value-changed; the function is created when missing), or bind localized text or a localization key.

blueprint.bind_widget_viewmodel.summary: Bind a widget property to a viewmodel field (MVVM), as the View Bindings panel does: source and destination are paths, Head.Field...: the head is a viewmodel of the widget (by its name), a widget of its tree, or Self (the Widget Blueprint), then the fields one after another (Health.Current, HealthBar.Percent, Player.Stats.Armor). A field is a property or a getter function. mode one_way (the destination follows the source whenever it changes, default), two_way, one_time or to_source (the source follows the destination: a slider writing a viewmodel). The Widget Blueprint is compiled with the binding and saved; a binding the MVVM compiler rejects (types that do not match without a conversion function, a source field that is not FieldNotify) is taken out again, leaving no undo step, and answers BINDING_INVALID with the compiler's message. A path naming nothing that is there is PATH_NOT_FOUND (with the viewmodels and widgets that are), a widget that does not compile beforehand WIDGET_DOES_NOT_COMPILE; refusals change nothing. Conversion functions are not made here.

blueprint.compile.summary: Compile a Blueprint asset, optionally saving after compile, or every Blueprint under a folder at once, answered with the ones the compiler or the graph checks flag.

blueprint.convert_actors_to_blueprint.summary: Turn placed actors into a Blueprint class named name in savePath, as the editor's Convert Selection to Blueprint Class does (a prefab): mode harvest (default) copies every component of every actor into one Blueprint, child_actors keeps each actor whole as a Child Actor component, subclass makes a Blueprint subclass of one actor's class that keeps its property values. With replace (default true) the actors give way to one instance of the new Blueprint where they stood (replacedWith), one undo step; the Blueprint itself stays (delete it to take it back). Every name and the path are checked before anything is made; the Blueprint is compiled and saved.
terms: create or make a prefab from actors
turn placed actors into a blueprint

blueprint.create.summary: Create a Blueprint asset, chosen by createMode (ensure checks first), named name in savePath (default /Game) and save it (saved). parentClass is a native class as /Script/Module.Class or a short name (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController), or a Blueprint class path ending in _C; blueprintType Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary stands in for a missing parentClass, and Interface without one makes a Blueprint Interface. A parent that resolves to nothing is CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming classes of that name. properties sets class defaults, Component.Property and struct members by dotted path, reported as appliedProperties and failedProperties (the create stands either way). A Blueprint already at the path is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged; one with another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS. A new Blueprint gets its components from edit_scs.
terms: static mesh component in a new blueprint
blueprint actor with a cube or sphere mesh

blueprint.create_widget_template.summary: Create a new Widget Blueprint holding a ready-made screen: main menu, pause menu, settings menu, loading screen, HUD, dialog box, inventory, radial menu, credits or shop.
terms: add a settings menu with volume and graphics

blueprint.delete_animation.summary: Delete a named animation (matched in any case) from a Widget Blueprint, its tracks with it, and save the Blueprint; saved says whether the save worked.

blueprint.delete_node.summary: Delete Blueprint graph nodes (deleteScope node, the default), or disconnect every wire of one pin (pin_links). node deletes nodeId, or every node in nodeIds (up to 500), all or nothing: an id that matches no node is NODE_NOT_FOUND and a function entry or result node is PROTECTED_NODE, with nothing deleted; their wires go with them, and the reply lists the removed guids. pin_links breaks the links of pinName on nodeId (PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the pins the node has) and names the pins it was wired to under disconnectedFrom; a pin with no links changes nothing. Either is one undo step, then the Blueprint compiles (diagnostics when it no longer compiles) and is saved. A pinName sent with deleteScope node is refused (CONTRADICTORY_SCOPE) rather than deleting the whole node.

blueprint.duplicate_widget.summary: Copy a widget and everything under it (a list row with its label, icon and button) inside a Widget Blueprint: same properties, slot layout and children, placed right after the original or under another panel.

blueprint.edit_graph.summary: Write Blueprint logic of any kind, or edit a graph: add or create nodes (including reroute and struct make/break nodes), connect pins, set node properties and pin defaults, add a construction script, arrange nodes beside what they are wired to, or run many of those edits, variables included, in one batch.
terms: print a message when the game starts
move nodes next to each other

blueprint.edit_scs.summary: Change the components a Blueprint adds (its Simple Construction Script), chosen by edit; each edit saves the Blueprint unless save is false. add_scs_component (add_component is the same) adds componentName of componentClass under parentComponent (its own part, a parent Blueprint's, or the native root; by default the root), with meshPath and materialPath (refused when they do not load or the class shows no mesh or material), location, rotation, scale and properties, and compiles; a taken name is refused, as is an add during Play. modify applies operations in order (each {type: add_component, modify_component or attach_component, ...}) or edits one component, naming each failed one in warnings (the call fails when none applied), and compiles only with compile or applyAndSave true; reparent moves a component under another; set_property and set_transform change one template and compile, and placed copies that kept the old value follow (instancesUpdated).
terms: make a component a child of another

blueprint.edit_timeline.summary: Make or change a Blueprint timeline, what a Timeline node plays: its length, autoplay and loop, and its float, vector, color and event tracks with their keys. The Timeline node gets a pin per track, and its Update pin fires every frame while it plays.

blueprint.edit_variable.summary: Change a Blueprint's variables, chosen by edit. add_variable adds variableName of variableType with defaultValue, category and the isPublic, isReplicated, exposeOnSpawn and exposeToCinematics flags (a taken name is VARIABLE_NAME_CONFLICT, a type that resolves to nothing TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED, a default the type refuses DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED; nothing is added then); rename_variable renames a variable or a component and its graph nodes follow; set_variable_metadata sets a variable's tooltip, category or replication; set_metadata sets metadata pairs on the class or one variable; set_default writes a class default value, an inherited property included.

blueprint.edit_widget_animation.summary: Build a widget animation, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes a named animation of a given length (a taken name is refused), add_track gives one widget an opacity, color or render-transform track, add_keyframe keys a value at a time on a widget (adding the track and binding when missing) or a whole animation across several widgets in one call (keys, all checked before any is written). get_widget_animation reads it back.
terms: animate a button or a title

blueprint.edit_widget_blueprint.summary: Create or restructure a Widget Blueprint, chosen by edit. create makes one named name in path (default /Game/UI), or at widgetPath, from parentClass (default UserWidget; a native widget class or a Widget Blueprint class path, anything else INVALID_PARENT_CLASS), with an empty widget tree, then compiles and saves it (compileSucceeded, saveSucceeded); a taken path is ALREADY_EXISTS. set_parent_class reparents it to a UserWidget class or Widget Blueprint, refreshes, compiles and saves (INVALID_CLASS, CYCLIC_PARENT). rename_widget renames slotName to newName and carries graph references, bindings, animations and navigation along (ALREADY_EXISTS, NAME_CONFLICT). reparent_widget moves slotName under the panel newParent at index (default last; the same parent reorders), keeping its slot layout; a move under its own child is INVALID_PARENT.

blueprint.get_blueprint.summary: Read a Blueprint, chosen by info. blueprint returns its parent class, type, compile status (hasCompileErrors), variables (name, type, category, replication, default), functions with their parameters, events, graphs with node counts, components (name, class, parent, root) and class defaults; property reads one value from its class defaults: propertyName is a variable or inherited property, or Component.Property for a component it adds, and a name found nowhere is PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing its variables.

blueprint.get_scs.summary: List a Blueprint's own components (SCS nodes) with class, parent, root flag and relative transform, plus the components it inherits from parent Blueprints and its native parent class; or, given a folder (path) and componentClass, every Blueprint under it that has such a component, owned or inherited.
terms: search blueprints for a component class

blueprint.get_widget_animation.summary: Read a Widget Blueprint's animations: without animationName, each one's length and track count; with it, every widget the animation drives and each track's keys per channel (translation.x, angle, scale.x, r, value ...) as [seconds, value] pairs, the names add_animation_keyframe takes.

blueprint.get_widget_info.summary: Read a Widget Blueprint: its widget tree (each widget with its class and parent, so a panel's children), or one slot layout (padding, alignment, size rule).

blueprint.implement_interface.summary: Make a Blueprint implement an interface (a Blueprint Interface asset or a native interface class), or drop it with remove. The reply lists the interface functions that became graphs to fill and the ones that are events to handle.

blueprint.inspect_graph.summary: Inspect a Blueprint graph: its nodes (every one, those whose title, pin default, text or object path matches a filter, or the unused ones), node details, pin details, the available node types, or the functions a node can call found by what they do in plain words (game time, random number in range), with the memberName, memberClass and pins create_node takes.

blueprint.lint_blueprint.summary: Read every graph of a Blueprint for the mistakes that show in Play, each with the node to fix: tick_heavy (Event Tick reaches a level search such as Get All Actors Of Class, or a spawn, every frame), unreachable (no event or function leads to a node, so it never runs), random_fanout (one pure Random node read by several nodes rolls once per read), infinite_while (a While Loop whose Condition is always true), never_assigned (an object variable read but never set, neither Instance Editable nor Expose on Spawn, with no default: every read is None), unguarded_read (an object variable set from a cast, a call or nothing, used as the target of a call or property where not every path to it checks it first with Is Valid, a validated get or a cast: a None there is an Accessed None). Then, from the values each variable can hold where each node runs (followed through Sets, Branches, Sequences and loops): divide_by_zero (a Divide or % whose divisor can be 0 there, nothing checking it first), index_out_of_range (an array Get, Set or Remove whose index can be negative or reach the array's length, as a ForLoop to Length instead of Last Index does), out_of_range (a Set that can store a value outside the variable's Value Range, which clamps only the Details panel), float_equality (== or != on a float worked out by arithmetic), constant_condition (a Branch already decided where it runs, so one exit never runs), endless_loop (a While Loop nothing in its body can end). A value only something outside the graph decides (a public variable, an unknown function's result) is not judged; checks that compare two variables (Health >= Damage) are followed. Nothing compiles or changes, and a function library is read too. The same rules run in the editor's Data Validation (Validate Assets, saves, validate_assets dataValidation): infinite_while, a divisor that is always 0 and an index always outside its array fail the asset, the rest warn; a write's reply passes on only those errors, so a graph built one node at a time is not told its newest node

blueprint.list_viewmodels.summary: List the viewmodel classes a widget can bind to (MVVM): Blueprints whose class derives from MVVMViewModelBase under folder (default /Game, the first 200) and native (C++) ones, each with the fields it notifies through: properties and getter functions marked FieldNotify, which are what a binding reads changes from (set_field_notify marks a Blueprint's variables). A viewmodel Blueprint is made with create_blueprint, parent class /Script/ModelViewViewModel.MVVMViewModelBase. Needs the ModelViewViewModel plugin (MVVM_DISABLED otherwise; enable_plugin and a restart turn it on). Reads only.

blueprint.preview_widget.summary: Look at a Widget Blueprint without running the game: it is drawn offscreen for a screen size and returned as a PNG image, as the game creates it: Construct graphs do not run, so texts are the designer defaults, and widgets set Collapsed or Hidden stay hidden.

blueprint.probe_handle.summary: Probe a Blueprint handle for reachability without loading the asset; reports its asset class.

blueprint.read_graph_as_code.summary: Read a Blueprint's event graphs and functions as text, in the S-expression grammar of Epic's UE 5.8 Blueprint DSL (read_graph_dsl / write_graph_dsl), on every UE 5.x: one (event Name (Params) ...) or (fn Name (Params) ...) per event or function; a statement per node that runs, (Category|Title args...) named by the node's action-menu id (Development|PrintString, Variables|Default|SetHealth), with trailing arguments still at their defaults left out (a call on the Blueprint itself leaves its unwired Target out; a Target that is wired comes first, every argument after it kept); (bind var (Call ...)) where an output is read later (by output position, _ for one not read); (if cond ... (elif cond ...) (else ...)), (for i (range n) ...), (for elem array ...), (while cond ...), (break), (switch Type value (:Case ...)), (return ...); pure nodes inline: (+ a b), (== a b), (and a b), (not x), (select cond a b), (.x vector), (.yaw rotator), (.location transform), self, literals ("text", 5, true); a node with named exec outputs takes (:Pin ...) continuations (pin names with spaces quoted). Every statement ends with a ; comment naming its node by id: n and the first hex digits of the node's GUID (6, more where two nodes read together share them), so ids do not change between reads; nodes gives each id its nodeId (the full GUID other graph actions take) and type, links every wire as "id.Pin -> id.Pin" (codeOnly leaves both out). Where a path runs on into a node already printed, (goto id) says so (Epic's own reader leaves that path out); a pure value two statements read is bound once at the top, tagged "pure, runs at each read" (Blueprint works it out again at each read). Reads only: nothing is created, compiled or changed. The first read after the editor starts takes several seconds while the editor builds its node menu.

blueprint.read_widget_viewmodels.summary: Read a Widget Blueprint's viewmodels (name, class, id, how the widget gets it) and its viewmodel bindings (id, source and destination as Head.Field paths, mode, enabled, whether it runs a conversion function). Empty lists for a widget with no viewmodel yet. Needs the ModelViewViewModel plugin (MVVM_DISABLED otherwise). Reads only.
terms: what a widget binds to viewmodels

blueprint.remove_function.summary: Remove a function the Blueprint defines (kind function: functionName), recompiled and saved; one still called is refused with FUNCTION_IN_USE naming each call node to delete first, and inherited or engine functions are NOT_FOUND. Or remove an event (event: a custom event by eventName, or any event node by nodeId, on graphName or the first event graph page), recompiled and saved; a custom event still called is refused with EVENT_IN_USE naming the call nodes.

blueprint.remove_scs_component.summary: Remove one or several SCS-owned component template nodes from the Blueprint. As the editor deletes, the children move up to the removed node's parent, and removing a root makes its first scene child the root (DefaultSceneRoot gives way to the mesh under it).

blueprint.remove_variable.summary: Permanently remove one or more member variables from a Blueprint, then compile and save it. Every get and set node of the variable is deleted with it, as the editor does once you confirm, leaving what they were wired to unwired; removedNodes names them. A name the Blueprint lacks removes nothing (NOT_FOUND, listing its variables).

blueprint.remove_widget.summary: Remove a widget and everything inside it from a Widget Blueprint, then save and recompile it, so Blueprints bound to it refresh too (except while Play In Editor runs). The reply echoes the name sent.

blueprint.remove_widget_viewmodel.summary: Remove one viewmodel binding (bindingId, from read_widget_viewmodels) or one viewmodel (viewModel, by name) from a Widget Blueprint. A viewmodel bindings still use is VIEWMODEL_IN_USE (their ids: remove them first); a binding that runs a conversion function is BINDING_HAS_CONVERSION (the editor removes its graph with it: the View Bindings panel). One undo step; compiled and saved. Refusals change nothing: BINDING_NOT_FOUND, VIEWMODEL_NOT_FOUND, VIEWMODEL_LOCKED, NOT_FOUND, MVVM_DISABLED.

blueprint.set_field_notify.summary: Turn FieldNotify on (default) or off for Blueprint variables, as the variable's FieldNotify box does: a FieldNotify variable tells its listeners each time a Set node changes it, which is what a viewmodel binding reads. Works on a viewmodel Blueprint (parent class MVVMViewModelBase) and on a Widget Blueprint; any other Blueprint is NOT_NOTIFYING. A name that is no variable of it is VARIABLE_NOT_FOUND (with the variables it has). One undo step; compiled and saved.

blueprint.set_font.summary: Style one widget of a Widget Blueprint (widgetPath; slotName is the widget name), chosen by textStyle. font sets the font asset (font, a Font asset path) and the fontSize of a Text Block, Rich Text Block (its default text), Editable Text or Editable Text Box; what is left out keeps its current value, and another widget type is UNSUPPORTED_WIDGET. margin sets left, top, right and bottom (each 0 when left out) as the padding of a widget in a Horizontal Box, Vertical Box or Overlay slot, or of a Border; any other slot, such as a Canvas Panel one, is INVALID_SLOT. The Blueprint is compiled and saved (saved says whether it was written).

blueprint.set_widget_layout.summary: Set a widget slot layout property (anchor, position, size (canvas {x,y}; box child sizeRule Auto/Fill and fillValue weight), alignment, padding, z-order, visibility, clipping, render transform) or its style: the text of a text block or button label, text justification, color, font size, font face, family and letter spacing (or the look of another text block), image texture, opacity, rounded corners, button hover/press sounds.

blueprint.write_graph_from_code.summary: Write a Blueprint's logic from text, on every UE 5.x: each (event Name ...) or (fn Name (Params) ...) form replaces that event's or function's body with nodes made from its statements, in the grammar read_graph_as_code prints (Epic's UE 5.8 Blueprint DSL), so the way to edit is read, change the text, write it back. A statement is (Category|Title args... :Pin value (:ExecPin stmts...)), the node named by its action-menu id as read_graph_as_code prints it (positional arguments fill the data inputs in order, :Pin names one, a (:Pin ...) continuation runs from that exec output and sees the node's outputs as _pin_name; a call that may run on the Blueprint itself leaves its Target, the self input, unwired unless it has an argument for every input, the Target's first, or names :self); (bind name (Call ...)) or (bind (first _ third) (Call ...)) names outputs for later statements (a name is bound once); (if cond ... (elif cond ...) (else ...)), (for i (range n) ...), (for i (range a b) ...), (for item array ...), (while cond ...), (break), (switch int|string|name value (:Case ...) (:Default ...)), (return values...), (goto id [Pin]) on to the node with that id (a statement of this code by its ; comment, or a node the write leaves in the graph, so one event can be rewritten alone). Values: names, literals ("text", 5, 1.5, true), (+ - * / % == != < <= > >= and or xor a b), (not x), (- x), (select cond a b), (.x .y .z .pitch .yaw .roll .location .rotation .scale value), self, and an event id alone, (AddEvent|Custom|OnDone), for an event input: that event of the graph bound to the delegate (a Bind Event to ... node), made when no event has that id; % is the integer modulo, the float one when an operand is a float, and == and != on text compare the strings exactly (Equal Exactly). A call used as a value takes the menu entry that gives one (IsValid as a condition is the pure function, not the macro of the same id), and one that gives none is refused there; an id whose title differs from the menu's only in spaces, underscores or

build_environment.add_foliage.summary: Place foliage (trees, grass, bushes, rocks): create or update a foliage type asset, place explicit instances/transforms, or paint instances over a brush disc or a box area, dropped onto the ground. Placing and painting are one undo step each.
terms: add trees, grass or flowers to the level
scatter rocks or trees around an area
plant trees around a building, a castle or a lake
place rocks randomly on the landscape
spread rocks or trees around the level
add grass to the landscape or the ground

build_environment.assemble_modules.summary: Lay a modular kit out over a grid of cells so that every face where two pieces meet fits, by wave function collapse, and spawn the layout as one actor (an instanced static mesh component per piece, one undo step). Each piece is a static mesh made to fill one cell of cellSize; pivot says where its own origin sits in the cell (corner: the cell's lowest corner; center; bottom_center: the middle of its floor), and a piece reaching outside that box is refused. Each face of each piece, at each quarter turn about Z when rotations is on (half turns when the cell is not square), is read from the mesh's source geometry as 16 x 16 squares (each read by 4 x 4 rays cast in from just outside, so a wall as thin as 1/40 of the cell shows): two cells sit side by side only where the faces between them match, both empty or covering the same squares to 90% (a corridor 3 squares wide never meets one 4 wide). emptyWeight adds an empty cell (0 forbids it). The grid's outer faces must be empty except on openSides (default -Z: the pieces stand on the ground). A piece whose face nothing in the kit can meet is never placed and unmatchedFaces names it: a wall reaching the top of its cell needs +Z open or a piece to stack on it, and an outer wall needs a piece to stand back to back with or that side open. Instances collide where the piece's mesh has collision. dryRun lays the kit out and spawns nothing. Refused, placing nothing: NO_SOLUTION (no layout: why, and the faces nothing meets), MESH_NOT_FOUND (not a static mesh with source geometry), INVALID_ARGUMENT (a piece outside its cell box, more than 4096 cells, or pieces whose faces take more than 10 s to read).
terms: make a dungeon or a maze
build a house or a castle from a kit

build_environment.bake_lightmap.summary: Build the level's static lighting (Lightmass) at quality (default Preview; Medium, High, Production): the same build as build_lighting, which defaults to Production. Reflection captures are not rebuilt, and a level that forces no precomputed lighting answers skipped. Can take minutes; nothing is saved.

build_environment.build_lighting.summary: Build the level's static lighting (Lightmass) at quality (default Production; Preview, Medium, High). Reflection captures are not rebuilt, a level whose World Settings force no precomputed lighting is refused (PRECOMPUTED_LIGHTING_DISABLED), an unknown quality is UNKNOWN_QUALITY, and a failed build lists its reasons (no static lights, no Lightmass importance volume). Can take minutes; nothing is saved.

build_environment.configure_atmosphere.summary: Configure the sky and atmosphere: sky atmosphere, sky light, sun position, directional light, height fog, volumetric clouds, time of day, sky/light color curves.
terms: add fog to the level or the map
make the fog thicker or thinner
move the sun or change the time of day
make it daytime, morning or evening
longer shadows from a lower sun
add stars to the night sky

build_environment.configure_foliage.summary: Change a foliage type asset (foliageTypePath, or foliageType), chosen by setting: mesh (meshPath; previousMesh, placedInstances and instancesShowingNewMesh tell how the placed instances followed), placement (density, minScale, maxScale, alignToNormal, randomYaw), collision (collisionEnabled), culling (cullDistance; the fade start moves in when it was further) or lod (settings: UFoliageType properties by name). Only the fields sent are written, and configuredProperties names them; a call that sets nothing is refused, as is a value a property will not take (CONFIGURATION_FAILED). Saved (SAVE_FAILED otherwise; engine content is never saved).

build_environment.configure_lighting.summary: Change scene lighting, chosen by setting. global_illumination sets the dynamic GI method (LumenGI, ScreenSpace, None, Lightmass) for this editor session, or in DefaultEngine.ini as well with saveToProject; shadows sets engine-wide shadow quality, distance and features for the session, or the shadow settings of the actor actorName names; exposure and ambient_occlusion write overrides on a post-process volume (actorName, else the level's one unbound volume, spawned when there is none); volumetric_fog enables or disables volumetric fog on the level's height fog. exposure, ambient_occlusion and volumetric_fog refuse a call that sets nothing (NO_SETTING_SUPPLIED).
terms: turn the shadows off or on
add god rays or light shafts

build_environment.configure_lightmass.summary: Static (baked) lighting, chosen by setting. settings writes the level's Lightmass settings (World Settings) from settings, keyed by engine field name (NumIndirectLightingBounces, IndirectLightingQuality, StaticLightingLevelScale, bUseAmbientOcclusion), which the next build uses; build_quality bakes the lighting at quality (default Production; Preview, Medium, High, or 0 to 3) and answers when the bake ends, refused when the level forces no precomputed lighting; indirect_lighting_cache sets how an actor's primitive components sample the indirect lighting cache (enabled: point sampling or off) or other primitive fields (settings). A key the target lacks is listed in unsupportedSettings and a call where none applies is refused; settings and indirect_lighting_cache are one undo step, and nothing is saved.

build_environment.configure_post_process.summary: Set post-process values on a PostProcessVolume, chosen by setting: bloom, exposure, depth of field, motion blur, tonemapper, color grading, LUT, white balance, vignette, grain, chromatic aberration, lens flare, SSAO/GTAO, screen-space and Lumen reflections, blend (screen_percentage sets r.ScreenPercentage instead). The volume is actorName, else the level's unbound (whole level) volume, the persistent level's first; a level with none gets one, named actorName when given. A name no volume has is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND listing the volumes, several unbound volumes AMBIGUOUS. Each value is the FPostProcessSettings field it names and turns that field's override on; settings takes any field by engine name. A value outside the engine's limits, an unknown name and a call that sets nothing are refused, and nothing is written unless every value is taken. One undo step; the level is left unsaved. blendWeight (0-1) and infiniteUnbound set the volume itself with any variant.
terms: add bloom or depth of field
make the room, the scene or the level darker or brighter
make the game look like a film
add a blur effect to the screen
make the hallway or the corridor dark

build_environment.configure_ray_tracing.summary: Turn a ray-tracing feature on or off and tune it through its console variables for this editor session: shadows, global illumination, reflections, ambient occlusion, path tracing. settings takes only the keys that feature reads (another is refused); with hardware ray tracing off for the project the values draw nothing and the reply warns.

build_environment.configure_scene_captur.summary: Configure a capture actor: render target, capture source, resolution, offset, planar-reflection settings, reflection capture resolution, or trigger a (re)capture.

build_environment.configure_spline_meshe.summary: Configure meshes along a spline: mesh asset, material, forward axis, spacing, randomization, or scatter meshes along it.

build_environment.configure_water.summary: Change a water body, chosen by setting: the one named by waterBodyName, targetActor or actorName, else the level's first. waves gives it Gerstner waves (waveHeight, waveLength, steepness, direction) that its surface and anything floating on it follow, and fails when the body does not keep them; material sets the material that draws its surface (its WaterMaterial, read back as waterMaterial; a material without the Used with Water usage gains it and is left unsaved); collision turns collision on its components on or off (collisionEnabled); settings writes water body actor properties by engine name. material and collision are one undo step; a call with nothing to set, or whose settings name nothing the body has, is refused, and a material that does not load fails the call.
terms: make the water calmer or the waves bigger

build_environment.configure_weather.summary: Configure a weather actor: rain, snow or lightning set a Cascade particle system (particleSystemPath) on an Emitter labelled WeatherEmitter, SnowEmitter or LightningEmitter; wind spawns or tunes a WindDirectionalSource (direction as its rotation, speed and other settings by property name). Nothing is simulated beyond what those actors do; not saved.
terms: add rain, snow, wind or lightning
make a storm with rain and lightning
make the trees sway in the wind
make the grass and the trees move in the wind

build_environment.create_atmosphere_acto.summary: Create the sky lighting rig (kind sky_sphere: a Sky Atmosphere, a sun and a Sky Light), an Exponential Height Fog (fog_volume), or one actor carrying its own sun, sky light and atmosphere at noon (time_of_day_system; nothing animates it, set_time_of_day moves the sun). Each reuses an actor already carrying its label, but one labelled otherwise is not seen, so mixing sky_sphere and time_of_day_system, or a sun of another label, doubles the sun.

build_environment.create_buoyancy_compon.summary: Make an actor float: add a buoyancy component (pontoons in settings.BuoyancyData) to an actor whose root is a physics-simulating mesh, and let it take the water body's overlap at level load, so one placed already in the water floats instead of sinking. In a Blueprint, add /Script/Water.BuoyancyComponent with edit_scs and set the class default bGenerateOverlapEventsDuringLevelStreaming to true.

build_environment.create_capture_actor.summary: Place a capture actor labelled name at location and rotation, chosen by kind: scene_capture_2d or scene_capture_cube (renders the view into a render target, assigned with configure_scene_capture setting=render_target), or a sphere_reflection, box_reflection or planar_reflection capture (settings: properties of its capture component). A capture of the same kind already labelled name is kept (alreadyExists); an actor of another class under that label is refused (NAME_TAKEN).

build_environment.create_foliage_type.summary: Create foliage assets, chosen by kind. type makes a static mesh foliage type named name in path (default /Game/Foliage) that places meshPath, with density (instances per 1000 x 1000 units, default 100), minScale and maxScale (default 1), alignToNormal and randomYaw (default true) and cullDistance. A foliage type already there is updated instead, keeping the settings not sent (created false); another kind of asset under the name is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). procedural places a procedural foliage volume and a spawner asset named <name>_Spawner (refused when it exists) with one foliage type per foliageTypes entry ({meshPath, density}), simulated with seed over bounds; a simulation that places nothing fails.

build_environment.create_landscape.summary: Create a new landscape in the world (its current level), or a grass type for one, chosen by kind. landscape spawns a flat Landscape actor labelled name (or landscapeName; an actor already under it is refused, NAME_TAKEN), its corner at location: componentCount {x, y} components (default 8 x 8), or the fewest that cover sizeX and sizeY (vertices like the editor Overall Resolution, or quads). Each component holds sectionsPerComponent (1 or 2) squared sections of quadsPerSection quads (7, 15, 31, 63 by default, 127 or 255). materialPath goes on it (default the engine grid material; one that does not load is refused, ASSET_NOT_FOUND). builtComponents, resolutionX/resolutionY and extentX/extentY (half the built size; a quad is 100 units) are measured from what was built, a build that makes no components fails (LANDSCAPE_BUILD_FAILED), and the level is left unsaved. grass_type saves a landscape grass type asset named name in path (default /Game/Landscape) that grows meshPath at density 1 per 10 square metres, scaled 0.8 to 1.2, randomly turned and aligned to the surface; a grass type already there is kept unchanged (alreadyExists) and another asset there is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).

build_environment.create_landscape_asset.summary: Create a landscape asset, chosen by kind. layer_info makes a landscape layer info asset (the layer a landscape material paints) named layerName or name in path (default /Game/Landscape), with hardness, physicalMaterialPath (refused when it does not load) and noWeightBlend; an asset already at that path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS). streaming_proxy places a World Partition streaming proxy linked to the landscape, at location and rotation (default the landscape's), reusing a proxy already labelled actorName.

build_environment.create_light.summary: Create a light actor in the level being edited: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (or any light class), at location (default 0, 0, 300), made Movable, with intensity, color and, in properties, shadow, radius and cone settings. The reply lists what was applied, refused (a setting this kind of light lacks) or adjusted; the spawn is one undo step and the level is left unsaved. During Play it still goes into the edited level, not the running game.
terms: add lights to a dungeon or a room
light up the stage with a spotlight
a red or warm coloured light
add a spotlight on the player

build_environment.create_lighting_setup.summary: Create lighting scaffolding, chosen by kind: level makes, saves and opens a new level lit by a sun, a SkyAtmosphere and a real-time sky light (refused over unsaved levels and during Play); lightmass_volume places a Lightmass Importance Volume box in the editor level, inside which baked lighting gets full quality.

build_environment.create_procedural_terr.summary: Create a procedural-mesh terrain actor (not a Landscape, so no sculpting or painting applies): a grid of sizeX by sizeY cells of spacing units each (default 100 x 100 of 100), subdivisions per side (2-200, default 50), raised by a fixed wave pattern whose peaks reach about 0.7 of heightScale (default 500), with collision and an optional material. Placed in the editor level, unsaved.

build_environment.create_sky_light.summary: Create a sky light (skyLightOp create, the default), or make sure the edited level has exactly one (ensure_single). create spawns one at location (default 0,0,500) as one undo step, lit by the captured scene or by cubemapPath (refused before anything spawns when that path holds no cube texture), at intensity; recapture captures the sky again now. During Play it spawns into the running game and is gone when play stops. ensure_single spawns a sky light labelled name (default SkyLight) when the level has none and relabels the only one to name; with several it refuses with MULTIPLE_SKY_LIGHTS, naming the one to keep (keep) and the ones to delete with control_actor delete (remove), and deletes nothing itself. It refuses during Play (PIE_ACTIVE), and its reply says spawned and relabelled.

build_environment.create_spline.summary: Create a spline actor, a spline mesh component, or in one call a typed spline with a mesh drawn along its route: road and river (a flat slab, 400 wide), wall and fence (standing on the route, 20x300 and 10x100), pipe and cable (round, 50 and 4 across). meshPath swaps in a mesh fitted to width (and height for a wall or fence); every span collides.
terms: add a fence along a path
add a wall around the level or an area
add a rope or a cable
make a race track or a road loop

build_environment.create_water_body.summary: Create a water body (ocean, lake, river or custom) with the Water plugin: real water that takes the editor's default materials and, for an ocean or lake, its default waves, as placing one in the editor does (listed under defaultsApplied).
terms: water the player can swim in
add water to the level or a map

build_environment.create_weather_system.summary: Find or spawn an Emitter actor (default label WeatherEmitter, the one configure_weather rain uses) and give it the Cascade particle system particleSystemPath. It is one emitter, not a weather simulation; a path that does not load is reported in particleSystemError while the call still succeeds.

build_environment.delete.summary: Delete actors from the editor level by label, name or path (names, or one of actorPath, name, actorName, targetActor): any actor, not only environment ones. Every name must match exactly one actor or nothing is deleted (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND; AMBIGUOUS_ACTOR for a label several actors share), and a failed delete is rolled back. Not saved.
terms: delete water, ocean, lake, river or landscape

build_environment.edit_landscape.summary: Edit a landscape (landscapeName or landscapePath, else the first in the level), chosen by edit. paint_landscape paints a layer over a brush disc, a vertex region or the whole landscape, and paint_landscape_layer at one weight over a region; import_heightmap writes a raw 16-bit heightmap into its heights. Those three go into the edit layer being edited (else the first), are one undo step and are merged before the reply, so the drawn landscape and its collision show them. configure_landscape_lod sets LOD properties by name and reads them back; configure_landscape_material assigns its material; configure_landscape_splines replaces its splines with one through points that raises and lowers the ground to it and can paint a layer, through the landscape's Splines edit layer (added when missing; terrainShaped and terrainNote say whether it did and why not); generate_lods gives static meshes simplified LODs.

build_environment.edit_spline.summary: Change the points of an actor's first spline component, chosen by edit; positions, rotations and tangents are in the spline actor's local space (subtract its location from a world point), and each edit is one undo step. add_point appends position, or inserts it at index, with pointType (default Curve) and optional tangents; set_point_position, set_point_rotation, set_point_scale and set_point_tangents change the point at pointIndex, which they require with their value (a lone arriveTangent sets both tangents); set_type sets splineType on pointIndex, or on every point when it is left out. An index past the last point is INVALID_INDEX and an unknown point type is refused.

build_environment.erode_landscape.summary: Wear a landscape down the way water wears ground, so that every cell drains: fillDepressions (default true) raises each pit to where it would spill (its basin becomes a flat lake bed), valleys cuts valleys by stream power, droplets wash gullies into the slopes, talusAngle slumps what is steeper, and the pits that leaves are filled again. region limits it to some of the landscape's vertices (default all), its border held so the result joins the ground around it. Written into the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited, else the first, as sculpt writes) as one undo step and merged before the reply; dryRun computes all of it and writes nothing. The reply gives drains (every cell has a path to the border that never climbs, judged on the heights written; undrainedCells when not), depressionsFilled, maxLoweredCm, maxRaisedCm, changedCells, dropletsRun (the same seed and droplets give the same ground), editLayers (with more than one, the others still add on top of this one) and rivers: up to 20, largest catchment first, each {catchmentM2, lengthM, points} with its course in world cm from source to mouth (at most 64 points; a river crossing a filled lake runs straight over it), for water bodies, splines and roads. Refused, changing nothing: LANDSCAPE_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_REGION (outside the landscape, or under 5 vertices a side), INVALID_ARGUMENT (more than 4,194,304 vertices at once: name a region).

build_environment.export_heightmap.summary: Write a landscape's heights (the level's first landscape when none is named) to a raw file: 16-bit samples, no header, machine byte order, for its whole extent or region (clamped to it). The path is relative to the project folder (Saved/Heightmaps/terrain.raw); the reply gives width, height and sampleCount, which reading it back with import_heightmap needs.

build_environment.export_snapshot.summary: Write the sun's rotation and intensity and the sky light's intensity (time of day included) to a snapshot file, for import_snapshot to apply again.

build_environment.get_foliage_instances.summary: Count foliage instances in the level, across every foliage actor (each loaded sublevel and World Partition cell keeps its own; foliageActors counts them), in total and per foliage type (byType), and list their positions; one type also returns rotation and scale ({x, y, z}: the whole scale, so a non-uniform one shows). The summary flag drops the list; limit caps it.

build_environment.get_splines_info.summary: List the spline actors in the level with each one's point count, length and world points (first 64); with actorName, one spline's points (location relative to the actor, the space spline edits take, and worldLocation), types, length and closed-loop flag.

build_environment.import_snapshot.summary: Apply a snapshot file export_snapshot wrote: the sun's rotation and intensity and the sky light's intensity, on the lights the file names. The file lives under Saved/unreal-mcp (or tmp/unreal-mcp) in the project and must end .json; one that is not there still answers success, applying nothing, so check the path.

build_environment.list_light_types.summary: List the light classes known to the editor: DirectionalLight, PointLight, SpotLight, RectLight and any other loaded light class, with a count.

build_environment.paint_foliage_instance.summary: Paint foliage instances with brush-based placement: a disc or a box area, dropped onto the ground.

build_environment.place_decals.summary: Lay deferred decals onto the surfaces under points, as a level artist drops stains, cracks, moss, puddles or posters: each point is traced along direction (default straight down) to the first surface with collision, and a decal actor is placed flat on what that actor draws there (where the line meets the triangles of its mesh, which can lie well inside a box used as its collision; a mesh that draws nothing along the line, as at the holes of a grate, is passed through), projecting into the surface, its texture upright as seen from outside (its top up a wall, toward world +X on a floor) and turned by angle. points places one per point; area scatters count of them over a disc facing the trace, on a floor or up a wall (spaced half a decal apart, each turned at random unless angle is given, the same for the same seed).
