The texture covers width x height cm of the surface (default 200 x 200; scaleJitter varies the size by up to that share) and projects depth cm through it (default half its smaller side, at least 20), so keep depth small on thin or curved surfaces or it spills onto what is behind; the box is centred where the line met the surface, so surface under the decal further than half the depth from that spot (behind a bump the line hit, as a fender on a quay wall) gets none of it. Each decal is labelled label_01, label_02 ... (default Decal) in the outliner folder (default Decals) and tagged mcp.decal; all of them are one undo step. onActors limits the surfaces a decal may land on (a point whose surface is another actor is listed in missed, not_listed); a point that hits nothing within traceCm (default 1000) is missed no_surface. dryRun traces and reports without placing. Refused, placing nothing: DECAL_MATERIAL_REQUIRED (the material's domain is not Deferred Decal: material.create_material kind decal makes one), MATERIAL_NOT_FOUND, NOTHING_PLACED (every point missed), INVALID_ARGUMENT.

build_environment.plan_road.summary: Find a road between from and to that a vehicle could drive: no grade over maxGradePercent anywhere along it (default 10), every obstacle and gap kept half its width away (width, default 600 cm), and no corner tighter than turnRadius (default 1500 cm), so a slope too steep to take straight is climbed in turns and switchbacks (up a cone-shaped hill whose sides pass about three times the limit its straight runs may find no way to the top: NO_ROUTE then says how steep a route would be). The ground under a grid turned so both ends sit on its points (a margin of half their distance, or of half the road their difference in height needs at that grade, at least 50 m; cells of about half the turn radius, at most 400 a side) is read by vertical traces: a landscape is ground, or the actors in groundActors (with neither, the actor under from); anything else solid standing anywhere in a cell up to 3.3 m above the ground is an obstacle (a post or a thin wall included), and a place with no collision at all is a gap (a create_primitive mesh has none until configure_mesh_collision). The route is searched over every cell and the heading it is entered by (16 headings), then straightened wherever grade, clearance and radius still hold and the straight road stays within 25 cm of the ground. Reads only. The reply gives points (world cm, the first at from and the last at to, each 10 cm above the ground and higher where the ground between it and a neighbour rises above the straight road joining them or where a lifted neighbour would leave the road between them steeper than the limit, so the middle of the road laid on them never dips in; across its width a level road still cuts into a side slope), lengthM, climbM, maxGradePercent (the steeper of the ground under the road and the road between the lifted points) and minTurnRadiusM measured on those points, maxLiftCm, switchbacks, groundGapCm (the farthest the straight road between two points strays from the ground), and two ready calls: nextCall lays the road with create_road_spline (a road
terms: add a path or a road on the terrain

build_environment.remove_foliage.summary: Remove foliage from every foliage actor in the level (each loaded sublevel and World Partition cell keeps its own): every instance of foliageType, every type (removeAll true), or only the instances inside an area box or several (areas, each {min, max}; with foliageType, that type only). A whole type also leaves the level's foliage list. One undo step; instancesRemoved counts what went (0 when nothing matched), an unknown type is FOLIAGE_TYPE_NOT_FOUND, and a box without min and max removes nothing.

build_environment.remove_spline_point.summary: Remove the point at pointIndex from an actor's first spline component, in one undo step; the points after it move down one index. Not saved.

build_environment.sculpt.summary: Shape a landscape, chosen by sculptOp: sculpt raises, lowers or flattens the ground under a round brush at a world location; heightmap sets, raises, lowers, flattens or smooths a region of its vertices (raw heights or centimetres); material sets the material it renders with. sculpt and heightmap count the vertices that changed, write the landscape's edit layer (the one being edited, else the first) as one undo step, and merge the layers before the reply so rendering and collision follow; an unknown tool or operation is refused.
terms: raise or flatten the terrain or ground
make a mountain or a hill

build_environment.set_light_channel.summary: Turn lighting channels 0-2 (channels, or one channel) on or off (enabled, default true): on a light, which then lights only primitives sharing a channel with it, or on every primitive of an actor. One undo step; the playing actor while Play In Editor runs.

control_actor.add_tag.summary: Add a tag to an actor (tagOp add, the default; with actorNames to many in one undo step) or remove one (remove), leaving its level unsaved. A tag is kept once and wasPresent says whether it was there; actorNames that match nothing come back in missing, and ACTOR_NOT_FOUND answers when none matched. Tags drive find_by_tag, delete_by_tag and the Actor Has Tag node; mcp.placement.ok makes the placement checks skip the actor.

control_actor.align_actors.summary: Line actors up on one axis, as a level designer squares up a row of crates, the tops of shelves or the fronts of buildings: each actor moves along axis only, so the edge it is aligned by (the min, max or center of its bounds, or its pivot) lands on the first actor's, or on value. Every name is found before anything moves (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND changes nothing); the moves are one undo step (none when nothing moves), dryRun reports them without moving, and where an actor lands is checked like any move.
terms: align the tops of the shelves
square up a row of crates
line up fence posts or pillars in a row

control_actor.apply_force.summary: Push a physics object in the running game with one impulse; the reply gives the mass it moved and the speed the push gave it.

control_actor.arrange_by_relations.summary: Move actors until the relations stated hold, overlapping nothing, in one undo step: say where things go (["Lamp on Table", "Chair_1 nextTo Table", "Chair_1 facing Table", "Shelf against Wall"]) instead of computing coordinates. The relations are those execute's expect judges: A on B (resting on its top), A inside B, A nextTo B (side by side, touching), A against B (touching, its back to B, its front away), A facing B (the line ahead of its front, its X axis, meets B or points within 20 degrees of the centre of B; beside a side of B it turns square to it) and A near B within d (cm, default 100). A solver plans from where the actors stand now, keeping a rough placement wherever it already fits: each actor is a box turned about Z (what it draws), and their places and turns are annealed over how far each relation misses, how deep they overlap each other or the scene around them, and how far they wander; then each contact is snapped exact. What rests on a moved actor moves with it. Each relation is then judged by the engine as expect judges it.
terms: put the lamp on the table
make the chair face the table
push the shelf against the wall
turn a chair to face a desk
stack boxes, crates or cubes on top of each other

control_actor.attach.summary: Attach childActor to parentActor, in one undo step: to its root, or to componentName (the mesh that owns a bone) at socketName (a bone or socket, SOCKET_NOT_FOUND when missing). It keeps its world placement, or with snapToTarget moves onto the socket (scale kept) and then takes relativeLocation and relativeRotation in the socket space, which is how a grip is tuned. The parent becomes its owner. ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND, CYCLE_DETECTED for itself, ATTACH_FAILED when the engine refuses (a parent already under the child, or a Static child under a moving parent: make it Movable).

control_actor.audit_placement.summary: Sweep every actor in the level and report the ones that interpenetrate another actor, sit sunk below the surface under them, float above it, lean off vertical, or have a face in the same plane as another surface (z-fighting flicker), and the unfinished content they show (a slot on the engine's default grid material, a text still reading "Text", a copy pasted onto the original); or, with blueprintPath, the mesh parts of one actor Blueprint that are buried in each other or sunk below its capsule (a part the Blueprint hides when it is built, such as a rider its construction script shows only while riding, is not judged: warnings names it). What an actor stands on can be part of a room built as one mesh, walls and all; one resting on a mesh with no collision reads floating, and the warning names that mesh.
terms: find which actors overlap each other
two copies in the same place
find actors stacked on top of each other
find actors sunk below the floor

control_actor.call_actor_function.summary: Call a named function on an actor, or while Play In Editor runs on the game's GameInstance, GameMode or another framework object, with optional arguments; normalizes to call_function.

control_actor.create_snapshot.summary: Remember an actor's transform (location, rotation and scale only) under snapshotName, in editor memory, to put back later (inspect create_snapshot with snapshotOp restore). A name used again replaces the old snapshot; snapshots last until the editor closes.

control_actor.delete.summary: Delete actors (deleteScope actors, the default: actorName or actorNames, exact names only, so TestActor never takes TestActor_Copy) or every actor carrying tag or any of tags (by_tag), in one undo step; every actor of a kind (all the cubes) goes by the names find lists. While Play runs they leave the running game, which nothing saves or undoes. Replies deletedCount and deleted; names not found refuse with NOT_FOUND, or DELETE_PARTIAL when some went, both carrying the deleted and missing lists.
terms: delete all cubes or all lights
remove the fog, the sky or the clouds
remove all the enemies or the props

control_actor.describe_relations.summary: Read the level back as relations between its actors, the way one describes a room: what rests on what (on), what hangs on a wall (mounted), what stands inside what (inside), what touches what side by side (nextTo) and what each actor's front points at (faces); which actors stand together (groups), which copies of one prop line up in rows or grids or stand in a ring; and the scene's roles: the ground, the sun's elevation and azimuth, the sky actors, player starts, cameras and the navigation area. Read only.
terms: which props stand in a row
is the shelf against the wall
find actors arranged in a row, a grid or a ring

control_actor.detach.summary: Detach an actor from its parent, keeping where it stands in the world (KeepWorldTransform) and clearing its owner, in one undo step. An actor attached to nothing answers success with detached false. While Play In Editor runs it detaches the playing copy, not the editor actor.

control_actor.distribute_actors.summary: Space actors evenly along one axis, as a level designer lines up pillars, crates or lamps: in their order along axis (default the one their centres spread across most) the first and last stay put and the ones between move so their centres are evenly spaced (stepCm), or with gapCm each sits gapCm past the one before it, measured between their bounds, from the first. Only that coordinate changes. Every name is found before anything moves (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND changes nothing); the moves are one undo step (none when nothing moves), dryRun reports them without moving, and where an actor lands is checked like any move.

control_actor.duplicate.summary: Duplicate a placed actor: a copy with its components, properties, materials and tags at the original's transform moved by offset, labelled newName or numbered after the original, in one undo step.
terms: duplicate a wall, a door or a prop
make a copy of an actor or a house
duplicate a tree or a rock several times

control_actor.edit_component.summary: Add a component to a placed actor (edit add creates it from componentType, componentName, meshPath and properties, attached under its root, a light made Movable), remove one (remove), or set one or more of its properties (set_property, set_properties: a placed mesh's StaticMesh or OverrideMaterials, a light's Intensity or LightColor to turn on a light, dim it or make it brighter, a TextRender's Text), or make its lights flicker (flicker: speed and depth, enabled false stops it). remove takes the exact name, refused with COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND naming the nearest, and only a component added to this actor: one from its class or Blueprint, or its root, is COMPONENT_NOT_REMOVABLE (a Blueprint component comes out with edit_scs). Each is one undo step and leaves the level unsaved; while Play runs they change the playing copy.
terms: make a spinning coin or platform
make an actor movable or static
a flickering torch, candle or lamp
a broken light flickering or stop it flickering
turn off the sun or a lamp
a blue or warmer light colour
a light made smaller or reaching further
make the cube spin or rotate
create a component on an actor
change the color of a light

control_actor.find.summary: Find actors by class, by name, by the static mesh they draw (mesh) or by a material in any of their slots (material), each with its class and location; the mesh and material finds name the matching components.
terms: find all the lights or cameras in the level
actors with a material in a slot

control_actor.find_by_tag.summary: Find the actors in the level whose Tags list holds a tag (the whole tag, case-insensitive), each with name, path and class: the first limit of them (default 200), with truncated and totalCount when more match. The Play-In-Editor world is searched while a session runs.

control_actor.fix_coplanar.summary: Fix z-fighting in one call: every actor with a face in the same plane as another surface moves a unit, so one surface is clearly in front. A piece lying wholly inside the other face (a door on a wall) comes forward; one only partly inside (a ramp sunk into the floor) goes back so the other shows. Every move is checked against the moves before it: one that would leave the moved piece in the plane of another face it touches (a wall nudged off one corner into the next) is not made, and the other way, the other piece, then twice the distance are tried instead. Two parts of one Blueprint actor are parted in the Blueprint itself, so every placed copy is fixed at once. A pair still left is named under skipped with why.

control_actor.fix_placement.summary: Fix what audit_placement reports, judged by its own rules: a sunk actor moves up and a floating one down onto the surface under it (not one resting on a mesh with no collision: dropped there it would sink into that mesh, so it is listed under skipped), and intersecting actors are pushed apart the shortest way out of each other, measured on their collision (the smaller moves further; floors, landscapes, locked and attached actors never move). kinds names which of sunk, floating and overlapping to fix, since each can be deliberate. Every move is one undo step; a run checks what it moved again, up to three rounds, and dryRun lists the moves without making them.
terms: floating above the floor or ground
snap an actor down to the surface below it
put the actor on the floor

control_actor.get_component_property.summary: Read one property's value and type from a named component on a live actor, or from a Blueprint's own component (blueprintPath, no instance needed); dotted paths reach into structs.

control_actor.get_components.summary: List an actor's components (info components, the default): each with name, class, path, relative location, rotation and scale (and worldScale when a parent scales it), attach parent and visibility; componentNames keeps only those, naming the others in missingComponents. A Blueprint asset path lists its class default, which holds only the native components, not the ones the Blueprint adds (read those with edit_scs). Or read its bounds (bounds): origin and half-size extent of every component, colliding or not. The running game copy while Play runs.

control_actor.get_transform.summary: Read where an actor is (the player's pawn too): its transform now, or watch it over game time in PIE (motion): location, velocity, rotation, chosen properties and points on it (bones, sockets, components, with their height over the ground) at every interval, to prove a jump, launch, patrol, fall, foot plant or a rocking hull in one call.
terms: copy an actor's transform or position

control_actor.group_actors.summary: Group actors as the editor's Group (Ctrl+G) does, so they select and move as one while the level is built (a locked group actor holds them, in their shared outliner folder), or with op ungroup break up the outermost groups they belong to. Each is the engine's own undo step. The actors must share a level (DIFFERENT_LEVELS) and the editor's grouping must be on (GROUPING_OFF); every name is found first, so a refusal changes nothing. Groups are an editor aid: in the game the actors are not attached.
terms: group the table and the chairs
make actors move together in the editor

control_actor.list.summary: List actors in the current level with their label, class, location, rotation and scale, plus any propertyNames values and, with bounds, each world bounding box, narrowed by name filter, tag, class or outliner folder; page on with offset. near (a world point) with radius is how to find what is near a point, nearest first, each with its distance. summary counts the level by class, tag and folder instead.

control_actor.lock_actors.summary: Lock or unlock actors in the editor, as Lock Actor Movement in the Transform menu does: a locked actor cannot be dragged in the viewport, and fix_placement, arrange_by_relations and settle_physics leave it where it is (listed under skipped); set_transform still moves it. Every name is found before anything changes (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND changes nothing); the actors whose lock changes are one undo step, none when every one already is as asked. Saved with the level.
terms: lock the floor and the walls

control_actor.randomize_transforms.summary: Give placed actors seeded random turns, tilts, sizes and nudges around where they stand, so scattered rocks, trees and props do not look set by hand: yaw turned by up to yaw degrees either way, pitch and roll by up to tilt, scale multiplied by a factor between scale[0] and scale[1], location moved by up to offset cm along X and Y. The same seed and the same actors in the same order give the same result. Every name is found before anything is touched; one undo step, and where each actor ends up is checked like any move.
terms: randomize the rotation of the trees
vary the rocks so no two look the same

control_actor.rename.summary: Rename an actor: its label (the name the Outliner and every other call use), and with renameObject its object name too, which is the name a cooked level ships. actorNames relabels several actors in one undo step, numbered in the order given by a {n} in newName (Crate_{n} -> Crate_01, Crate_02, ...).
terms: rename the cube or the wall
rename all the trees or the lights

control_actor.replace_actors.summary: Replace placed actors with a static mesh, a Blueprint or an actor class where they stand, as the editor's Replace Selected Actors with does: each new actor keeps the old one's transform, scale, mobility, label, tags, outliner folder, layers, attachments and the level's references to it, and a Blueprint whose class shares a native parent with the old actor's takes its property values. Every name and the asset are checked, and that the editor has an actor for it, before anything is replaced; one undo step brings the old actors back, and where each new actor stands is checked like any move.
terms: swap actors for another mesh or blueprint
replace placeholder cubes with the real mesh

control_actor.set_actor_collision.summary: Turn collision on or off for an actor, give its components a collision preset (BlockAll, OverlapAllDynamic, NoCollision...), or set how they answer one channel (Pawn Ignore lets a character walk through, Pawn Block stops it); many actors at once with actorNames, as one undoable step.

control_actor.set_blueprint_variables.summary: Set Blueprint variables on one placed actor (actorName, the playing copy during Play) from variables {name: value}, or on many actors with actors, each with its own; an actor reference takes an actor's name. Every name is checked first: one the class lacks refuses the call (PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing its variables) and nothing is set. The construction script reruns, as a Details panel edit does, and the call is one undo step (a batch too). A value a variable will not take fails with VARIABLE_NOT_SET naming it (VARIABLE_BATCH_INCOMPLETE for actors); updated lists what was set.

control_actor.set_folder.summary: Move placed actors into an outliner folder path such as Level/Signs (made when missing), or back to the root with folder "": one actor by actorName, or many with actorNames, as one undo step. Names that match no actor are listed under missing while the rest move; none matching is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND.

control_actor.set_material.summary: Put a material on an actor, or a flat colour with color ("#rrggbb", "#rgb" or a name such as red or white: a material instance of the engine's BasicShapeMaterial, made once under /Game/Materials/Colors and reused, which replaces the slot's material, textures and all), or a glowing one with glow (that colour, white without color, lit from within at that strength: an instance of M_ColorGlow in the same folder): slot materialSlot (default 0) of its first mesh component that has that slot, of componentName, or of every one with allComponents; materials sets slot i from entry i ("" skips one), and actorNames gives many actors the same material. One undo step. Refusals: MATERIAL_NOT_FOUND, ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND, MATERIAL_SLOT_NOT_FOUND (no component has the slot), INVALID_ARGUMENT (a colour it cannot read, or color or glow with materialPath); a list that partly failed answers MATERIAL_BATCH_INCOMPLETE naming each failure. While Play runs it changes the playing copy, gone when play stops.
terms: make the cube or the wall red
color an actor red, blue or green
white, black, yellow, orange, purple, pink, brown or gray
change the color of an actor
paint or tint a mesh a colour
make the cube or the sign glow
make a lamp, crystal or sword glow
make the character red or change its color
the player or an enemy glowing
make the enemies or the props different colors
make the wall look like brick, wood or stone

control_actor.set_transform.summary: Move, rotate or scale placed actors (the playing copy during Play), chosen by transformMode; every member writes alike. location, rotation ([pitch, yaw, roll] degrees) and scale are world values, a part left out keeps its current value, and offset moves by [dx, dy, dz] instead of to a location (both together are refused). actors gives several actors their own values and actorNames gives many the same change in one call. A single move is one undo step and teleports, without sweeping. The reply reads the transform back off the actor; one that did not end up as asked (attached, simulating physics, constrained, or moved by game logic) fails with TRANSFORM_MISMATCH carrying where it is, and TRANSFORM_BATCH_INCOMPLETE names batch items that did not move. The placement is checked: groundZ, groundClearance, and placementWarning with suggestedLocation when it is sunk, floating or intersecting.
terms: scale up a tree or a rock
rotate a door or a wall by 90 degrees
move the box, the crate, the barrel or the statue
move or rotate the chair, the table or the lamp
make an actor twice as big or half the size
make an actor bigger or smaller
make the sword or the enemy bigger
make the player taller or smaller
turn or rotate the cube around

control_actor.set_visibility.summary: Show or hide an actor in the editor and in play (visible, default true), or many actors at once with actorNames, as one undo step. Collision follows visibility: hiding turns its collision off, and showing turns it back on, even where set_actor_collision had turned it off. Showing also shows every primitive component, including one hidden on purpose. The single form replies visible as read back plus actorName; the many form replies updatedActors, affectedActors and the names not found under missing. A name that matches nothing is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND; an actor that does not read back as asked is VISIBILITY_MISMATCH.
terms: hide or show all the trees
hide the wall or the door

control_actor.settle_physics.summary: Let actors fall under physics and keep where they come to rest, in one undo step: a pile of crates, rocks scattered on a slope, a toppled chair, a stack whose stability is in doubt. The editor's own Simulate runs for up to the seconds asked (of physics time), each named actor's root body simulating; it stops early once every body sleeps. The reply says, for each actor, where it ended up, how far it moved and turned, whether it came to rest or was still moving, whether it fell (more than fallCm below where it started, or out of the world), and its peak speed (a body launched by starting inside another reads high). With dryRun nothing is kept: a stability check. Answers after Simulate has ended, in about 2-10 s. A run that cannot finish keeps nothing: SIMULATE_STOPPED (Simulate stopped in the editor mid-run), SIMULATE_TIMEOUT, SETTLE_RUNNING (another settle is simulating), NO_LEVEL_VIEWPORT.

control_actor.snap_to_grid.summary: Move actors onto a grid, as the editor's grid snapping places a dragged actor: each location axis in axes (default xyz; xy keeps heights) rounded to the nearest multiple of gridCm (default the editor's own position grid size), and with rotationDeg each rotation axis to a multiple of that. Every name is found before anything moves (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND changes nothing); the moves are one undo step, dryRun reports them without moving, and where an actor lands is checked like any move (sunk, floating, overlapping).

control_actor.spawn.summary: Place actors in the level, or in the running game during Play (gone when Play stops), chosen by spawnKind; each call is one undo step. class spawns classPath (or actorClass), such as /Script/Engine.PointLight or a Blueprint class, or with meshPath alone a Movable static or skeletal mesh actor showing that mesh; blueprint spawns blueprintPath; batch places up to 500 items (1000 once repeat rows are unrolled) in one call, each a spawn payload that can also take materialPath, variables, properties, folder and tags, with shared defaults. location and rotation default to zero and scale to 1; folder files the actor in the outliner and tags tag it. The actor is labelled actorName, else after its mesh or class; when another actor has the same label, the reply's actorName is the actor's unique object name, which later calls must use. An unknown class or mesh is refused (CLASS_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_FOUND), and an actor that destroys itself at once is SPAWNED_THEN_DESTROYED. The reply checks the placement: groundZ and groundClearance, and placementWarning with suggestedLocation for an actor sunk, floating or intersecting (tag mcp.placement.ok to mark one deliberate).
terms: a row of trees, lamps or posts
fill a room with props or furniture
place lamps or posts along a road or a path
add an actor to the level
add a cube to the level
place a cube on the floor
add a sphere to the level
place a sphere in the level
build a wall or a tower of cubes
add a floor or add a ceiling
add a bridge over a gap or a river

control_editor.call_editor_tool.summary: Run one tool of Epic's editor toolsets (Unreal Engine 5.8 Toolset Registry) with a JSON input matching the inputSchema list_editor_toolsets returned, and answer with its output once it finishes. A tool whose name starts with a destructive verb (Delete, Remove, Destroy, Clear, Reset ...) is refused with DESTRUCTIVE_EDITOR_TOOL: run it with call_editor_tool_destructive. A tool that would run scripts or console code, and every ConfigSettingsToolset tool (it reaches this plugin's own settings; use system_control project settings), is never called (EDITOR_TOOL_BLOCKED).

control_editor.call_editor_tool_destruct.summary: Run one tool of Epic's editor toolsets that deletes or resets editor state (its name starts with Delete, Remove, Destroy, Clear, Reset or a similar verb), under the destructive scope and elevated consent; any other tool runs here too. A tool that would run scripts or console code is never called.

control_editor.close_asset.summary: Close every editor open on an asset, by asset path. Fails with EDITOR_NOT_OPEN when none is open; the asset is never loaded to do this.

control_editor.configure_editor.summary: Open or close an editor tab, set editor preferences, or restore or minimize the main editor window without focus (restoring unthrottles Play In Editor).

control_editor.configure_viewport.summary: Change what the editor viewport shows, chosen by setting: view_mode (any engine view mode by name: Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, LightingOnly, ShaderComplexity, CollisionPawn, PathTracing and the rest; the running game's view while Play runs), editor_mode (activate a mode such as EM_Landscape, EM_Foliage or EM_Default, checked active), game_view (hide editor icons), immersive_mode (the viewport fills its window), realtime (keep effects and animated materials moving), show_stats or hide_stats (stat overlays: FPS and Unit by default; hide_stats with no stat hides them all), show_flags (the Show menu by name: flags {"Grid": false, "Collision": true}, every name checked before any is set, each read back). Each answers with the state it reads back; with no level viewport open, NO_VIEWPORT.
terms: turn the grid on or off
show bounds or the navigation mesh in the viewport
hide fog or editor icons in the viewport

control_editor.console_command.summary: Run one console command against the editor world, or through the first player while Play In Editor runs, and return what it printed (output) and what the engine logged meanwhile (log), each kept short: the first 30 lines and any Error: or Warning: line after them, at most three lines that open with the same two words, and (+N more lines) where lines were left out; at most 4096 characters. A command the engine does not recognise fails (EXEC_FAILED); one holding ;, |, &&, a backtick or several lines, or a blocked name (quit, exit, py, crash and the like), is refused (COMMAND_BLOCKED). Success means the engine ran it, not that it had the effect wanted.

control_editor.create_bookmark.summary: Store the level viewport camera (location and rotation) in bookmark slot id, from 0 to the editor bookmark count less one (usually 9; another id is refused); a view already in the slot is replaced. The bookmark is kept in the level, which is left unsaved; jump_to_bookmark returns to it.

control_editor.describe_reflected_api.summary: List a class's reflected functions (a plugin's live bridge object such as FabBrowserApi, or any engine class): each with its parameters, C++ types and return or out flags, read from the installed build; filter narrows by function name.

control_editor.explore_level.summary: Explore the running level with a pawn the way a tester would, to find what a model cannot see by reading it: places the pawn falls out of the level (below its kill height) or leaves the playable area, traps it cannot get out of, parts of the nav mesh no path from the start reaches (islands: a sealed room), and Blueprint errors raised on the way. In a Play session started through this server (others are refused with PLAY_NOT_STARTED_BY_MCP). Go-Explore's first phase, without learning: an archive of cells (the grid cell, the height band and the truth of the track assertions), each kept with the moves that first reached it; every round walks the pawn back to a cell (along the nav mesh, else teleported) and explores from there with sticky random moves (the last one repeated 19 times in 20, jumps included), through the pawn's own movement: no OS input. op start begins a session for the player's pawn or actorName's and explores for seconds; continue explores more (cell picks where the next round starts, else cells chosen less often are preferred); read answers with what was found; stop ends the session. Each call answers after its seconds (at most 22); the window is held on screen without focus meanwhile.
terms: find where the player can fall out
find holes the player falls through
find places the player gets stuck

control_editor.focus_actor.summary: Focus the viewport camera on a specific actor by name: the level viewport, or the free view of an ejected player.
terms: zoom to an actor or the player start

control_editor.fuzz_blueprint.summary: Call a Blueprint's functions in the running game with edge-case inputs and catch the errors they raise, before a player does. Each function and custom event is called once with every input at a plain value (numbers 1, false, text "A", for an object the actor itself or another actor of that class from the game, an array of 3), then once per edge value of one input at a time with the others kept plain: numbers 0, -1 and the int limits (or +-1e9 for floats), empty and 256-character text, None, an empty array, each enum value (up to 8), a zero and a huge vector. A failing call is so already the smallest change from one that works. A call fails when it raises a Blueprint runtime error: an Accessed None, an endless loop, a divide or modulo by zero, an array index out of range; each comes back with the node it came from (node title and nodeId, the node's GUID; a pure node such as a divide runs inside the node its value feeds, which is the one named, and the message names the function). Only in a Play session started through this server (others are refused with PLAY_NOT_STARTED_BY_MCP), on actorName or the first instance of blueprintPath placed in the game. By default the Blueprint's own functions and custom events that take inputs (functions names any, a parent's included; one without inputs is called once). The calls run one after another inside this call, at most maxCalls (default 200) and 20 s; a function stops after its third failing call. They run the game's own logic: what they change stays changed in the running game (never in the level), and what runs after a Delay or a timer runs later, outside the call it belongs to. Break on Exceptions is held off during the calls. Refused with BREAKPOINTS_SET (the Blueprint has breakpoints: a call reaching one would stop the game in the debugger), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, BLUEPRINT_NOT_FOUND, NOT_A_BLUEPRINT (a native actor), FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND (lists the Blueprint's own), NOTHING_TO_FUZZ (no function of its own takes inputs).
terms: call blueprint functions with bad inputs
try edge cases on a blueprint function

control_editor.invoke_reflected_function.summary: Call one reflected UFunction on a plugin's live object, marshalling arguments through the function's own property chain. No signature is hardcoded: whatever describe_reflected_api reports for the installed build is what this accepts, so an integration stays correct across plugin updates instead of silently passing a stale parameter list. Return and out parameters come back in `outputs`. Refuses when only the class default object exists, because invoking on the CDO mutates shared defaults and never reaches the running instance. This is arbitrary in-process invocation — it can reach any reflected function on any resolvable object — so it demands elevated consent.

control_editor.jump_to_bookmark.summary: Move the level viewport camera to a bookmark slot (id); fails with BOOKMARK_NOT_FOUND when that slot is empty.

control_editor.list_editor_toolsets.summary: List the tools of Epic's editor toolsets (the Toolset Registry that ships with Unreal Engine 5.8: StateTree, PCG, GAS, Niagara, UMG, MVVM, physics and more, as their plugins are enabled), each with a description and an effect (read, write, destructive) judged from its name; query narrows them, and toolName returns one tool's input schema for call_editor_tool.

control_editor.open_asset.summary: Open an asset's editor (a Blueprint, a material, a widget, a sequence, a skeletal mesh in Persona) by asset path, loading the asset first; it must be known to the asset registry (ASSET_NOT_FOUND). Under -NullRHI it loads the asset and opens no window, and says so.

control_editor.open_level.summary: Open a level from disk by its path (/Game/Maps/Demo; an object path such as /Game/Maps/Demo.Demo, or a bare name read as /Game/<name>, works too), replacing the open level: Play In Editor is stopped and asset editors close. Unsaved levels are refused, never saved (DIRTY_PACKAGES); the reply waits for the level to settle (settledSeconds).
terms: open the menu level or another map

control_editor.play.summary: Control Play In Editor with control: play (starts it, answering once play has begun), pause, resume, stop (answers once play has ended), eject (leave the pawn for a free camera) or possess (control another pawn by actorName, such as a character to test, or back to the player pawn).
terms: play the level or the game

control_editor.playtest.summary: Walk a pawn of the running game to a goal along the nav mesh and judge the leg, in a Play session started through this server (control_editor play; a session started in the editor is refused with PLAY_NOT_STARTED_BY_MCP, since someone may be playing it). The player's pawn by default, or actorName's; goal is a point, or goalActor where that actor is. The verdict: pass only with evidence (the goal reached within acceptRadius, every check held, no script error), fail with what went wrong (stuck: no progress for stuckSeconds; fell: below its start by fallCm or out of the world; a script error during the leg; a check that did not hold), inconclusive (the nav mesh gives no full path, so the leg was not tried; still on the way at maxSeconds; or the game paused itself during the leg), error (the game left the level: Play stopped or the level changed). A paused game (a title screen, a pause menu) is refused with GAME_PAUSED: resume it with control_editor play, control resume, unpauseGame true. checks are assertions in execute's expect language, judged in the running game when the leg ends. The editor window is held on screen without focus for the leg, so the game runs at speed. The reply: verdict, ended (reached, stuck, fell, timeout, pawn_lost), checks, scriptErrors, timeline (where the pawn was, at most 50 samples), last, bestDistance, traveled, frames.

control_editor.read_editor_ui.summary: Read the editor's own UI: its windows (windows: index, title, ref; menus and popups are windows too) and an outline of their widgets, one a line, indented by nesting: e12 SButton "Save All" [disabled]. A widget is listed when it says something (its text, or an icon-only control's tooltip), takes keyboard focus or is a control (buttons, check boxes [checked]/[unchecked], combo boxes, spin boxes, sliders, text fields, tabs); layout-only widgets fold away. Each ref names its widget for the rest of the editor session. Narrow a big outline with window (an index or part of a title, WINDOW_NOT_FOUND otherwise), from (a ref: only that branch; WIDGET_GONE once its widget is closed), text (only branches holding those words, with the widgets above them) and depth (nesting levels, 1-40, default 12); maxWidgets (1-1000, default 300) caps the lines, truncated says more were left out. It only reads: to change something, search for the capability that does it.
terms: find a button in the editor

control_editor.restart_editor.summary: Restart the editor process, relaunching the same project, or close it (relaunch false). validateOnly lists the unsaved packages without doing either.

control_editor.save_all.summary: Save every level and asset with unsaved changes, or only the packages named in assetPaths (the other dirty ones stay unsaved and are listed in leftDirtyPackages). Temporary packages are skipped; one that fails to save (read-only, not checked out) is listed in failedPackages and fails the call with SAVE_FAILED while the rest stay written. Refused during a Movie Render Queue render (RENDER_IN_PROGRESS). Not undoable.

control_editor.screenshot.summary: Capture a screenshot of the level viewport (optionally from a camera location and rotation given in the same call, or through a camera actor: a cutscene shot at a held sequence moment), of the running game view, or of the whole editor window with the game UI; pathTraced renders the level viewport with the path tracer to a denoised review image.
terms: show me the level from above
take a picture of the level

control_editor.set_camera.summary: Set the viewport camera transform, its field of view, or the view target actor. While Play In Editor runs, the transform moves the free camera of an ejected player and is refused until the player is ejected.

control_editor.set_game_speed.summary: Control the clock of the running game during Play In Editor: game speed (slow motion), a fixed delta time, or step frames.

control_editor.set_selected_actors.summary: Set which actors the editor has selected, as clicking them in the viewport or the Outliner does (the Details panel shows them): mode replace (the default) makes actorNames the selection, add adds them, remove takes them off; replace with no actorNames clears it. Names are labels, object names or paths, matched exactly; one that matches nothing refuses with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND and the selection stays as it was. A change is one undo step; a call that leaves the selection as it was makes none. The reply lists the selection after the call by label (get_selected_actors lists object names).
terms: select all cubes or all lights

control_editor.set_viewport_resolution.summary: Set the game window resolution through the console (r.SetRes <width>x<height>, fractions dropped); it does not resize an editor viewport. The reply is the console command's: command and output.

control_editor.simulate_input.summary: Simulate a keyboard or mouse input event (key_down, key_up, key_tap, mouse_click, mouse_move), or list and press the live UMG widgets of a PIE session (widget_list, widget_click).
terms: check or toggle a checkbox in running game

control_editor.start_recording.summary: Record the running Play In Editor game as a replay (control start, the default: DemoRec, written by default under Saved/Demos; frameRate and durationSeconds), or stop it (stop; NOT_RECORDING when nothing records). Refused without a running game (NO_ACTIVE_SESSION). For playback, seeking or a killcam, use the sequence demo actions.

control_editor.undo.summary: Undo or redo the last editor transaction (the reply names it, or says there was none), or roll back to a restore point, undoing only what this server changed since.

datatable.create_data_registry.summary: Make a data registry over data tables: the asset at assetPath with registryType (the name the game looks items up by, one registry each) and one DataTable source per table, in the order given (the first holding an item serves it), its item struct the tables' shared row struct; saved. The game sets up only registries under the DataRegistry settings' DirectoriesToScan, so scanned says whether this one is (the project settings stay as they are). Nothing is made on a refusal: INVALID_ARGUMENT, ASSET_EXISTS, DATA_REGISTRY_EXISTS (the type is another registry's), DATA_TABLE_NOT_FOUND, ROW_STRUCT_MISMATCH; DATA_REGISTRY_DISABLED when the project leaves the DataRegistry plugin off.

datatable.delete_data_table_row.summary: Delete one data table row by rowName (deleteScope row, the default; ROW_NOT_FOUND names a missing one) or every row (all; rowsCleared counts them), and save the table unless save is false (saved says whether it was written). Logic that looks a row up by name gets nothing back for a deleted one.

datatable.edit_data_table.summary: Write a data table, chosen by edit. create makes a table (name and path, default /Game/DataTables, or dataTablePath) bound to the row struct at rowStructPath; create_row_struct makes a struct for its rows (name and path, default /Game/Structs, or rowStructPath) from members. add_row adds rowName with rowData, the columns it leaves out taking the struct defaults, and refuses a name already there (ROW_ALREADY_EXISTS); update_row changes only the columns rowData names in an existing row; import_rows loads rows of {rowName, rowData} in one call, each named row replaced whole (clearExisting drops every row first), and lists the rows that do not fit under invalidRows. set_row_struct (set_struct_as_row_struct is the same) binds another row struct and carries the rows over (migrateExistingRows, default true): a row whose values do not convert is dropped and listed under invalidRows, and a filled table is refused unless the rows are migrated or cleared. rowData keys are the struct property names, as inspect_data_table reads them back. Every edit saves the asset unless save is false (saved).

datatable.get_data_registry.summary: Read one data registry, by asset path or by its registryType: its item struct and schema (each field's name and type), id format tag, sources (each source's class and the table it reads), whether the game sets it up (scanned) and whether the registry has set up its runtime sources (initialized: then meta sources show the tables they found), every item name in lookup order (the first source holding a name serves it; up to 500 named, itemCount counts all), and the values of up to 50 items asked for by name (items: a curve table's row is named, not read; names no source holds are in itemsNotFound). DATA_REGISTRY_NOT_FOUND names nothing found; DATA_REGISTRY_DISABLED when the project leaves the DataRegistry plugin off.

datatable.inspect_data_table.summary: Read a data table at dataTablePath (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when none is there). info row, the default, reads one row by rowName: found, and its rowData, each column under its property name in the form edit_data_table writes; a missing row answers found false rather than an error. rows lists every row with its values (rows of rowName and rowData), with rowCount the table total and rowStructPath; a listing too large for one reply comes a page at a time (send page.nextCall for the next), and past 10,000 rows truncated is true. row_struct answers hasRowStruct and rowStructPath (struct.get_struct reads the columns).

datatable.list_data_registries.summary: List the project's data registries (DataRegistry assets, found through the asset registry without loading them), each with its registryType (the name the game looks its items up by), itemStruct and scanned: the game sets up only registries under the DataRegistry settings' directoriesToScan (in the reply, with initializeAllLoaded). A project that leaves the DataRegistry plugin off answers DATA_REGISTRY_DISABLED.

enum.delete_enum.summary: Delete an enum asset (deleteScope enum, the default; refused with DELETE_FAILED, naming referencedBy, while anything still uses it) or remove one of its values (value: the later values move up one while loaded Blueprints and assets holding them keep their entries, remapped by name as the enum editor does, and pins set to the removed one are reset to the first entry; one undo step). Saved unless save is false.

enum.edit_enum.summary: Create a user enum or edit its values, chosen by edit. create makes it (name and path, default /Game/Enums, or enumPath) with values in order; a name given twice is refused and nothing is made. add_value appends valueName (index and valueCount answer where). rename_value changes the name the editor shows and keeps the internal name every stored value (defaults, pins, table cells) holds, answered as internalName. reorder_values takes order, every value once, and moves them as the enum editor does, so stored values keep their entries (the order it already has changes nothing). set_value_metadata sets key to value on one entry, such as its ToolTip. split copies the named values, or every value from index on, into a new enum newEnumName (in path, default /Game/Enums) and leaves the source as it is. A value is named by its internal or its shown name; a name the enum already has is VALUE_EXISTS and one it lacks NOT_FOUND. add_value, rename_value and reorder_values are one undo step each. Every edit saves unless save is false.

enum.get_enum.summary: Read a Blueprint enum (UserDefinedEnum): every entry with its name and numeric value, plus the value count.

inspect.add_tag.summary: Add a tag to an actor named by actorName, name or objectPath, or to several with actorNames: control_actor.add_tag runs it, with the same reply (wasPresent; taggedCount, affectedActors and missing for several) and the same ACTOR_NOT_FOUND when nothing matched.

inspect.analyze_view.summary: Judge the level viewport's picture as a reviewer would, in numbers: saliency (where the eye goes: how strongly each actor draws it, the focus point, and a named subject's rank), palette (five colours with their shares, the hue template of Cohen-Or et al. they fit best and how far the rest stray from it, and the colour cast of surfaces that should be grey), light (a lightness histogram, clipped and crushed shares, contrast, exposure, flat lighting and, on a subject lit by the sun, its key to fill ratio in stops) and cost (how much of the frame, and of each actor, the shader complexity view draws at a high cost). Read only: the camera moves only when location, rotation or fov is given, and cost puts the viewport's view mode back after one frame in the shader complexity view.
terms: which actors are expensive to shade
is the level or the scene too dark

inspect.audit_materials.summary: Check the materials in the level viewport's view the way a technical artist would. pbr: the viewport is drawn in the Buffer Visualization view mode for base colour, metallic and roughness (the values the G-buffer holds, so tints and constants in the material count) and each lit, opaque actor in view is judged: too_dark (base colour under sRGB 30, darker than charcoal, on a quarter of it), too_bright (a non-metal over sRGB 240, whiter than snow; a metal's base colour is its reflectance, silver near 250), dark_metal (a metal's base colour under sRGB 155: metals reflect at least about a third of light), partial_metallic (metallic between 0.1 and 0.9 on a quarter: a surface is metal or not), mirror_roughness (roughness under 0.05 on half); an actor with an unlit or translucent material is listed under skipped with why. texel_density: each material slot of the static meshes in view at its sharpest 2D texture, as the texture streamer reckons it (texture size times the material's UV tiling for it over the mesh's UV density times the actor's scale), against the view's median: too_sharp (four times or more: memory spent on detail nobody sees) or too_blurry (a quarter or less). Only a slot whose material holds texture streaming data for the texture is judged, and the median is theirs when there are any; one without (a world-aligned material such as the engine's grid, or data never built) is listed with approximate and its ratio. instancing: static mesh actors of the level drawing one mesh with the same materials, groups of 8 or more, worth turning into one instanced mesh. Read only: the camera moves only when location, rotation or fov is given, and the viewport's view mode and buffer are put back.

inspect.capture_passes.summary: Capture the level viewport's view as machine-readable passes, aligned pixel for pixel: id (a PNG with one colour per actor, and the legend naming each colour's actor), depth (an EXR of the distance in cm) and normal (a PNG of the world normal, RGB = normal x 0.5 + 0.5), with a summary of each. location, rotation and fov place the camera first, as describe_view and control_editor screenshot take them.

inspect.changes_since.summary: List what changed in the editor since a cursor: level actors added, deleted, moved or modified (with the properties edited and their values) and assets or levels created, removed, renamed, modified, saved or opened, each marked by who changed it: mcp (a call through this server), user (an edit made in the editor, and its undo and redo) or editor (anything else, such as saving, importing or opening a level by hand). The engine's own work on actors and objects (loading a level, compiling) is not kept. The reply hands back the cursor to send next time; without one it lists the most recent changes kept. Changes merge per object; 4096 objects are kept, and a cursor from before an editor restart or older than what is kept answers CHANGE_CURSOR_EXPIRED.

inspect.check_mesh.summary: Check whether a static or skeletal mesh's geometry is sound, from its source triangles: closed (watertight) or open with how many holes, edges shared by three or more faces, faces turned inside out, closed parts wound inside out, faces with no area, seams where faces do not share their corners, and how many separate parts it is made of, with its size, surface area and (when closed) volume.

inspect.contact_sheet.summary: One image of an actor from several sides: front, back, left, right and top as true elevations (orthographic, in the actor's own turned frame, with a grid every round number of centimetres) and a three-quarter view, each tile labelled, the actor's size in the title. Shaded as clay from the geometry, the same whatever lights the level: the actor orange, everything else grey, and the parts of the actor hidden behind something (a foot sunk in the floor, a back against a wall) showing through it. Only the actor and the actors within reach of it are drawn, so a wall farther off never hides it while the floor it stands in stays. Each elevation is taken from outside what it draws, except something reaching more than 250 m past the actor (a water zone, a landscape), which it is taken from inside, so the sides of that one may not show. Returned as an image and written as a PNG under Saved/Captures (keepFile false leaves no file); the level viewport is not moved.
terms: show a prop or actor from every side
front back side and top views
check an actor from all sides
look at a cube or a prop from the side

inspect.create_snapshot.summary: Remember or put back an actor's transform (location, rotation and scale only) under a snapshot name, in editor memory: create stores it, restore sets it again (transformChanged says whether anything moved). A name used again replaces the old snapshot; snapshots last until the editor closes.

inspect.delete_object.summary: Delete placed actors by exact name, as control_actor delete does: actorName (or name, or objectPath), or several with actorNames, in one undo step. Names not found refuse with NOT_FOUND, or DELETE_PARTIAL when some went, both listing what was deleted and what was missing.

inspect.describe_view.summary: Describe what the level viewport's camera sees, as text: each actor in view with its share of the frame, its box on screen, how bright it is drawn and its distance, the share that is background (sky, void), and the frame's brightness; or only the actors named, with what hides each one that is not seen. points names what is under spots of the frame and where they are in the world; labels returns the frame with each listed actor boxed and numbered; saveAs keeps the frame under a name and compareWith says what changed in the picture since, region by region, with the actors drawn there before and after. location, rotation and fov place the camera first, as control_editor screenshot takes them.
terms: what is at this point on screen
compare the view before and after
did the edit change the picture

inspect.explain.summary: Explain why something does not happen, chosen by what: two actors that do not overlap or hit (collision), an actor that is not seen (visible), a key that does nothing (input), a widget not on screen (widget), a sound not heard (audible), a light that lights nothing (lit). Each walks an ordered fault tree over what the engine holds and answers the first cause with the call that fixes it, plus every check made.

inspect.find_by_class.summary: Find the actors of a class in the level, by class name or /Script path: returns each match's name, path and class plus a count. Searches the PIE world while a game runs.

inspect.get_blueprint_details.summary: Read a Blueprint asset without spawning it: parent class, type, compile status, variables with defaults, functions, events, graph node counts, and components with transforms, meshes and materials.

inspect.get_component_details.summary: Read one component of an actor or Blueprint: class, relative and world transform, mobility, visibility, attachment, bounds, collision, mesh and chosen property values; info=property returns a single property's value.

inspect.get_components.summary: List the components of a level actor (actorName, name or objectPath) or of a Blueprint (blueprintPath, or an objectPath that is a Blueprint asset: its construction-script components and class defaults), each with its name, class, parent and where it comes from. A mesh component adds its static mesh and the material drawn in each slot, overrides included; a Blueprint component adds its relative transform and visibility. componentNames narrows the list, naming the ones not found under missingComponents.

inspect.get_console_variables.summary: Read console variables by name (r.ScreenPercentage, sg.ShadowQuality, r.Lumen.DiffuseIndirect.Allow): each one's value, type (bool, int, float, string), the layer that set it last (Constructor, Scalability, ProjectSetting, SystemSettingsIni, DeviceProfile, ConsoleVariablesIni, Commandline, Code, Console and the like) and the first line of its help, without running a command. Names it does not know come back in notFound; a name that is not one (letters, digits, dots and underscores) is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT. A variable whose name has a credential word in it (key, token, secret, password, auth or credential, as in net.EncryptionKey) keeps its value back (withheld).

inspect.get_editor_state.summary: Read editor state: selected actors, viewport, world settings (with whether the game is playing or paused), project settings, editor settings, or focus: what the user is working on (open editors, a Blueprint's selected nodes, recent errors).
terms: what is this actor or this asset
what the user is looking at

inspect.get_property.summary: Read a property value from a world actor, asset, or Blueprint class defaults (blueprintPath, or the Blueprint asset's own path), several at once (propertyNames), or the same ones from several objects (objectPaths).

inspect.get_stats.summary: Read performance (FPS, frame rate and time, thread and GPU ms), memory usage (used, available, peak), scene statistics (actors by category, components, hidden actors), or frame cost: the thread that bounds the frame and what in view weighs on it (movable shadow-casting lights, heavy meshes, translucency, ticking actors).

inspect.inspect_class.summary: Read reflection data, chosen by kind. class (className or classPath) gives the class path, parent and ancestors, module, flags (abstract, blueprintable, actor, component and more), every property it declares or inherits (name, type, category, where declared, editable, Blueprint-visible; at most 200 listed, propertyCount the total), the default value of each on its class default object, and its function count. cdo reads a Blueprint class default object without spawning anything (blueprintPath): its default values (propertyNames picks some) and its default components (componentName or componentNames narrows them). struct reads the members of a user struct (structPath): name, type, default and tooltip.

inspect.inspect_object.summary: Deep-inspect an actor or asset, or read a typed detail view of an actor, level, material, texture or mesh (its size, bounds, pivot, LODs and material slots, each with the triangles and bounds of the geometry it covers).

inspect.query_object.summary: Read placed actors, chosen by lookup. list pages through the actors of the level (the running game during Play): filter narrows by name, limit (default 100) and offset page through them, with totalCount and isPieWorld; control_actor list adds class, tag, folder, near and property filters. by_tag lists the actors carrying tag (name, path, class), stopping at limit (default 200) with the total. metadata gives one actor name, label, path, class, tags and location. bounding_box gives its world bounds as origin and extent (half the size on each axis), every component counted. export writes it as T3D text (exportedText), and also to outputPath inside the project when given.

inspect.raycast_mesh.summary: Cast rays at a static mesh asset in its own local space and read where each one meets the surface: the point, the surface normal and the material slot. Places a part, a print or a decal on a curved surface without a placed actor or collision.

inspect.raycast_world.summary: Trace lines through the level against collision and read what each one hits first: the point, the surface normal, the distance, the actor and the component. Finds the ground under a point, checks a line of sight, and proves a wall, floor or volume really blocks. Traces the running game while Play In Editor runs.
terms: what is under or in front of the player or an actor

inspect.read_logpoints.summary: Logpoints: mark Blueprint nodes (set) to record their pin values each time they run in Play without pausing it, read what they recorded (read), or remove marks (clear).
terms: print a blueprint value during play
what values did the node get

inspect.runtime_report.summary: Report the live state of a running PIE game: the player controller, pawn, view target and camera, plus up to 25 matching actors with class, transform, tags, components and the live values of the variables or properties named in propertyNames; actors are reported only while PIE runs.

inspect.set_component_property.summary: Write one or more properties of a component on a placed actor, as control_actor edit_component set_property does: propertyName or a dotted propertyPath with value, or properties for several. One undo step, the level left unsaved; while Play runs it changes the playing copy. The actor is named by actorName, name or objectPath.

inspect.set_property.summary: Write a property value on a world actor, asset, or Blueprint CDO; several at once (properties), or the same on several objects (objectPaths).

manage_ai.analyze_level_layout.summary: Read the editor level's nav mesh as a map of spaces and how routes run through it: rooms (areas at least roomWidthCm wide), corridors (the narrower passages and alcoves between them), the doors joining them, the chokes (the spaces most routes between the other spaces pass through, highest first, each with its passThroughShare), dead ends (a space with one neighbour), loops (independent ways around), and how far one sees from each space (sightlineCm). From a start (startActor, else the first PlayerStart when it stands in the area read) it also lists the spaces that cannot be walked to, and with goalActor or goal the walk there (its length and the spaces it crosses). The reply's message says it in a few sentences; spaces[] (the 100 largest), doors[] (the 100 most used) and the name lists (50 each) hold the details. Reads the whole navigable area, or the navigable part of the box center + extent; samples every cellCm (default 100) up to maxNodes (default 6000: past it the cell widens and the message says so), leaving out islands of fewer than 4 samples (the top of a crate). image writes a top-down PNG of the spaces (imagePath). Reads only. Refused with NAV_DATA_MISSING when the level has no nav mesh, NAV_BUILD_IN_PROGRESS while it builds, NO_WALKABLE_AREA when the box holds none, ACTOR_NOT_FOUND for a startActor or goalActor not in the level, INVALID_ARGUMENT for a start or goal away from the nav mesh read or an area over 600 m tall.

manage_ai.configure_navigation.summary: Configure navigation: nav mesh settings, agent properties, area cost or class, nav links, smart links, or rebuild the nav mesh. A level with no nav mesh yet gets one from a NavMeshBoundsVolume (manage_level_structure create_volume).

manage_ai.create_ai_controller.summary: Create an AI Controller Blueprint (parent AIController) at path/name (path default /Game/AI/Controllers) and save it; an asset already there is refused. A pawn uses it through its AIControllerClass with Auto Possess AI; saved in the reply says whether it reached disk.

manage_ai.create_behavior_tree.summary: Create an AI asset named name, chosen by kind, each saved (saved): behavior_tree a Behavior Tree in path (default /Game/AI/BehaviorTrees), graph_route the same in savePath (default /Game), blackboard a Blackboard in path (default /Game/AI/Blackboards), where a Blackboard already there is kept (alreadyExisted). Any other asset already at the path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS).

manage_ai.create_nav_actor.summary: Create navigation helpers, chosen by kind: link_proxy places a NavLinkProxy whose point link joins startPoint and endPoint (relative to it) so agents cross a gap the navmesh does not connect; smart_link places one whose smart link alone does, switchable on and off; modifier places a NavModifierVolume marking the navmesh under it with areaClass (default NavArea_Obstacle) or, with blueprintPath, adds a NavModifier component to a Blueprint; modifier_component adds that component to a Blueprint or a placed actor. A label or component name already taken is refused.

manage_ai.edit_behavior_tree.summary: Edit a Behavior Tree graph: add composite, task, decorator, service or generic nodes and subnodes, connect or break connections, configure or remove nodes. Each edit is one undo step.

manage_ai.edit_blackboard.summary: Edit a Blackboard asset (blackboardPath), chosen by edit, each saved: add_key adds keyName of keyType (an Object key a MoveTo target uses wants baseObjectClass /Script/Engine.Actor; an Enum key takes enumType), set_value sets the default a key starts with (UE 5.4+, Enum, Object and Class keys 5.5+), set_key_instance_synced shares one value across every AI. A taken name (NAME_TAKEN), a value of the wrong kind, a key of a parent Blackboard (KEY_IN_PARENT) and engine content are refused. Each edit is one undo step.

manage_ai.edit_eqs_query.summary: Create an Environment Query or edit it, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes the asset, add_generator gives an option its items (ActorsOfClass, CurrentLocation, Donut, OnCircle, PathingGrid, SimpleGrid, Composite), add_test adds a test (Distance, Dot, GameplayTags, Overlap, Pathfinding, PathfindingBatch, Project, Random, Trace), add_context points a generator or test at the querier, the items or a context class, configure_test_scoring sets the equation, clamps and filter of a test. A Behavior Tree runs it with a Run EQS Query task.

manage_ai.edit_mass_entity.summary: Build Mass entities, chosen by edit: create_config makes an empty Mass entity config asset and configure adds a trait to it or sets trait properties or a parent config, each saved; add_spawner places a Mass Spawner actor that spawns the config's entities at the items of an Environment Query when play begins. A configure call that sets nothing is refused.

manage_ai.edit_smart_object.summary: Build Smart Objects, chosen by edit, each saved: create_definition makes a definition asset, add_slot adds a slot at an offset, configure_slot enables a slot or adds registered activity tags, add_component puts a Smart Object component (with its definition) on an actor Blueprint. A taken path or component name, an unregistered tag and a definition that does not load are refused.

manage_ai.edit_state_tree.summary: Create a State Tree or edit it, chosen by edit, each compiled and saved: create makes the asset with a Root state and a schema (component or ai, from the GameplayStateTree plugin), add_state adds a named state, add_transition links two states on a trigger, configure_task sets the properties of a task or the selection behavior of a state. compiled says whether the tree compiled (an uncompiled tree does not run), with compileMessages.

manage_ai.get_ai_info.summary: Read an AI asset: a pawn or AI controller Blueprint (each perception sense with its settings under the names the configure actions take, the engine teamId and the teamIdVariable set_perception_team stores, movement), a Behavior Tree summary, Blackboard keys, State Tree states or EQS query options; info=navigation returns NavMesh and agent settings; info=path says whether a pawn could walk between two points on the nav mesh, and why not.

manage_ai.get_tree.summary: Read a Behavior Tree as a nested node tree: root composite with its tasks, decorators and services, node counts and assigned Blackboard; info=blackboard_value reads a Blackboard key's type and default value.

manage_ai.run_behavior_tree.summary: Make an AIController Blueprint run a Behavior Tree whenever it possesses a pawn (control run, the default: On Possess calls Run Behavior Tree with its BehaviorTree variable), take that out again (stop), only set the variable that holds the tree (assign_tree), or bind a Blackboard to a controller or tree (assign_blackboard). The run logic is engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game; a Blueprint that is not an AIController is refused (NOT_AI_CONTROLLER).

manage_ai.set_ai_movement.summary: Set the movement limits on the CharacterMovement component of a Character Blueprint (an AI pawn) and save it: maxWalkSpeed, maxAcceleration, brakingDeceleration (walking), rotationRate (yaw, degrees per second), maxFlySpeed, jumpZVelocity and avoidanceWeight, plus useAccelerationForPaths (path following speeds up and slows down like a player instead of moving at full speed at once), orientRotationToMovement (turn to face where it goes) and useRVOAvoidance (steer around other agents). Only what is sent changes, 0 included; a negative number or a call that sets nothing is refused, as is a Blueprint with no CharacterMovement component (COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND). propertiesSet names what changed and currentValues reads the main values back.

manage_ai.set_focus.summary: Make an AIController Blueprint keep its focus on the player 0 pawn (focusPlayer) or the first actor carrying focusTag, finding it again each frame it has none (focusOp set, the default), or take that logic out (clear). Written into the Blueprint as engine nodes, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game.
terms: rotate the enemy to face the player or look at it

manage_ai.setup_perception.summary: Set up AI perception on an AI controller or pawn Blueprint, chosen by setting, each saved: setup adds the component and several senses at once, add_component only the component (kept when present), sight, hearing and damage tune one sense and keep what is not sent, team stores a team id variable (the engine team itself needs C++), controller is setup for an AIController path. An actor with no team is neutral, so a sense must detect neutrals to notice the player.
terms: make the enemy see or hear the player

manage_audio.analyze_acoustics.summary: Hear how a space sounds where a listener stands: 256 rays cast evenly in every direction from location (or actorName's location; the rays pass through that actor) give the room as heard from there: its volume and surface, mean free path, length, width and height along its own walls (proportion: the largest over the smallest), the share of rays that meet nothing within maxDistance (default 5000 cm: open sky, a large doorway), the delay of the first reflection, and its reverberation time rt60, the seconds sound takes to fall 60 dB. rt60 comes from a traced decay (each ray reflected on, 30% of the reflections scattered, losing absorption of its energy at each, read off its Schroeder curve), so it holds in corridors, flat halls and rooms with openings; eyringRt60 gives Eyring's formula beside it only for a closed room no more than 3 times as long as its smallest side, where that formula holds. absorption (default 0.1) is the share of sound the surfaces soak up: bare concrete or tile about 0.02-0.05, plaster or wood about 0.1, a furnished room 0.2-0.3, a treated studio 0.5 and up. Rays trace the visibility channel against complex collision, as the engine's sound occlusion does. When half the rays escape or more, it is outdoors or very open and no reverb is suggested; otherwise nextCall makes a Reverb Effect with that decay (RE_Room in /Game/Audio/Effects) and zoneCall places it as a reverb zone over the room's box (roomCenter, roomSize; rename both together). Reads only. Refused with POINT_IN_SOLID (the listener is inside geometry), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT (neither location nor actorName).

manage_audio.configure_sound_attenuation.summary: Configure sound attenuation: distance falloff and air absorption, spatialization, occlusion, reverb send, or a named attenuation preset.
terms: make a sound quieter far away

manage_audio.configure_sound_class.summary: Change a Sound Class or Sound Mix, chosen by setting, each saved: parent sets or clears a class's parent (a loop is refused), properties sets its volume, pitch, low-pass, LFE bleed and center-channel volume, mix_modifier adds or edits the adjuster a mix applies to a class (and the mix fades), mix_eq sets the mix's four EQ bands. A call that sets nothing is refused.
terms: change the volume in the menu or the game
the music or the sounds louder or quieter
change the volume in the settings or the menu

manage_audio.control_sound_mix.summary: Change the mix of the sound being heard (the running game while one plays, else the editor; inGame says which), chosen by control: push and pop put a Sound Mix on the mix stack and take it off, set_base sets the base mix beneath them, and set_class_override and clear_class_override change how a mix adjusts the volume and pitch of one Sound Class, which applies while that mix is pushed or base. Mixes and classes are named by asset path or bare name (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when one does not load). Runtime state only: nothing is saved.

manage_audio.create_audio_actor.summary: Place sound in the level being edited, chosen by kind. ambient_sound spawns an Ambient Sound actor playing soundPath at location (default 0,0,0), labelled name, at volume and pitch, with attenuationPath and concurrencyPath when given; it plays in the editor now and when the game starts. audio_component adds an audio component with soundPath to actorName, or to a new actor at location when actorName is left out (the reply names the actor), playing at once unless autoPlay is false. reverb_zone spawns an Audio Volume named name (DUPLICATE_NAME when taken) as a box of size (default 500 on each axis) around location, applying reverbEffect at volume (default 1) with fadeTime (default 2 s). A sound, attenuation, concurrency or reverb path that does not load is ASSET_NOT_FOUND before anything spawns; the ambient sound and the reverb zone are one undo step each.
terms: add a sound or music to the level or a room
add echo to a cave or a hall
add rain, wind or bird sounds
play music when the game starts

manage_audio.create_audio_asset.summary: Create an audio asset named name in path, chosen by kind: sound_cue (playing wavePath when given), sound_class, sound_mix, attenuation_settings, reverb_effect, dialogue_voice, dialogue_wave, source_effect_chain or submix_effect. An asset already at that path is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS) rather than rebuilt over, and a reference that does not load is refused before anything is made. Saved unless save is false.

manage_audio.edit_metasound.summary: Create a MetaSound or edit it: add inputs, outputs and nodes, connect or disconnect nodes, remove nodes, set input and node literals, or run many edits in one batch.

manage_audio.edit_sound_cue.summary: Edit a sound cue graph (assetPath): add or connect nodes, set attenuation or concurrency, add a Doppler pitch shift at the root. add_source_effect works on a Source Effect Chain at assetPath instead: it appends effectPresetPath, or a new preset of effectType saved as its own asset beside the chain (<chain>_<effectType>, numbered when taken).

manage_audio.fade_sound.summary: Fade a sound an actor or audio component plays. soundName is an actor label or name, or an audio component name; componentName picks one of that actor's audio components (refused, listing the ones it has, when it names none), else the first. in (re)starts the sound from its beginning, rising from silence to targetVolume (default 1) over fadeInTime; out lowers it to targetVolume (default 0) over fadeOutTime and then stops it, whatever the level, and changes nothing when it was not playing; to_volume changes the volume of the sound playing to targetVolume over fadeTime (default 1 s), stopping it at 0 (the default), and is refused with SOUND_NOT_PLAYING when nothing plays. The engine ignores a fade out to a level at or above the current one. While a game runs in the editor, the name resolves in the game first. The reply names the actor and component, the fade time and volume used, and playing (whether the sound plays after the call).

manage_audio.get_audio_info.summary: Read an audio asset: Sound Wave duration, sample rate and channel count; Sound Cue duration, node count and attenuation; Sound Class volume, pitch and parent; Sound Mix modifier count; Attenuation falloff.
terms: how many nodes in a sound cue

manage_audio.get_metasound_graph.summary: Read a MetaSound graph: every node with its input literals, the links by pin name, and the graph inputs and outputs.

manage_audio.list_metasound_nodes.summary: List the MetaSound node classes the engine has, by part of their class name, display name or category, with what each does and, with includePins, its input and output pins: the nodeClassName add_node takes.

manage_audio.measure_loudness.summary: Measure how loud Sound Waves are the way broadcast and streaming measure it: EBU R128 integrated loudness in LUFS from each wave's own samples (K-weighted, so a deep rumble counts less than speech at the same level; gated, so silences and quiet tails do not pull it down), the loudness each plays at through its Volume, and its sample peak; spreadLu says how far apart they play. A peak meter says how high a sound reaches, not how loud it sounds: two waves with the same peak can play 10 LU apart. Mono counts one channel, as EBU R128 does, so a mono wave reads 3 LU under the same sound in stereo. Read only; normalize_loudness sets the Volumes.

manage_audio.normalize_loudness.summary: Make Sound Waves play at one loudness: each wave's EBU R128 integrated loudness is measured from its own samples (as measure_loudness does) and its Volume set so it plays at targetLufs, all in one undo step, each wave saved unless save is false. The samples stay as they are; peakAtVolumeDb says when a raised wave now peaks above full scale before the mix. A silent wave, or one under 400 ms of sound, keeps its Volume (note). Mono counts one channel, as EBU R128 does, so a mono wave reads 3 LU under the same sound in stereo. Refused, changing nothing: ASSET_NOT_FOUND (a path that is not a Sound Wave), ENGINE_CONTENT (an engine wave: duplicate it into /Game first).
