manage_audio.play_sound.summary: Play a sound: 2D, at a location (played or spawned), attached to an actor, or prime it for playback. A 2D sound (looping music too) plays until stop_sound. measure plays it 2D and reports how loud it played (peak and average dB, silent). The sounds already playing are listed by console_command au.DumpActiveSounds.

manage_audio.set_dialogue_context.summary: Add a context to a Dialogue Wave: speakerPath (the DialogueVoice that speaks the line) speaking to targetVoices (the DialogueVoices listening), with soundWavePath (the SoundWave that plays) and localizationKeyFormat (default {ContextHash}). The same speaker and listeners already on the wave is CONTEXT_EXISTS unless replace is true, which swaps that context (replaced). Saved unless save is false (saved).

manage_audio.set_sound_looping.summary: Make Sound Waves loop, or stop looping (looping false): each wave's Looping flag, which loops it wherever it is played by itself (play_sound, an Ambient Sound, a Blueprint's Play Sound), every wave checked first, in one undo step, each saved unless save is false. The reply gives each one's looping before and after. A Sound Cue loops through a Looping node in its graph (edit_sound_cue) and a MetaSound through its own graph, so both are refused. Refused, changing nothing: ASSET_NOT_FOUND (not a Sound Wave), INVALID_ARGUMENT (a Sound Cue or a MetaSound), ENGINE_CONTENT (an engine sound: duplicate it into /Game first).
terms: loop a sound or stop it looping

manage_audio.set_sound_volume.summary: Make sounds louder or quieter: each Sound Wave's Volume (a MetaSound's too) or Sound Cue's Volume Multiplier set to volume (1 as recorded, 0.5 half, 0 silent) or changed by changeDb (6 is about twice as loud in level, -6 half; negative is quieter), every sound checked first, in one undo step, each saved unless save is false. The reply gives each one's volume before and after. To make several play at one loudness by ear, use normalize_loudness. Refused, changing nothing: ASSET_NOT_FOUND (not a Sound Wave, MetaSound or Sound Cue), ENGINE_CONTENT (an engine sound: duplicate it into /Game first), INVALID_ARGUMENT (both volume and changeDb; neither is MISSING_REQUIRED_ONEOF).
terms: make a sound louder or quieter
turn the music or a sound up or down

manage_audio.set_subtitles.summary: Give a Sound Wave subtitles: subtitles [{text, time}] replaces its cues (time is the seconds into the sound a cue shows from; each stays until the next one or the end), [] takes them off. The engine shows them at the bottom of the game's screen whenever the wave plays, through a Sound Cue too (not inside a MetaSound, which plays its waves itself), unless the game has subtitles switched off (a warning says so). One undo step, saved unless save is false; the cues come back as the wave holds them. Every cue is checked first, so a bad one changes nothing: ASSET_NOT_FOUND (not a Sound Wave: a Sound Cue plays waves, give those the subtitles), ENGINE_CONTENT (an engine wave: duplicate it into /Game first), INVALID_ARGUMENT (a cue with no text, or a time outside the sound).
terms: show subtitles in the game while a sound plays

manage_audio.stop_sound.summary: Stop, pause or resume playing sounds: the 2D sounds play_sound started (only that sound with soundPath), or with all every sound the editor and a running game play, its music included. Pause holds a sound where it is and resume continues it; the reply counts the sounds changed (0 when none was playing).

manage_character.build_metahuman.summary: Run the MetaHuman assembly pipeline, producing the usable character assets.

manage_character.configure_character.summary: Configure a Character Blueprint's defaults by setting: movement_speeds (walk, crouch, swim, fly, acceleration, braking, friction), jump (launch speed, hold, double jump, air control, gravity), crouch, rotation (orient to movement or face the aim), capsule_component, mesh_component (skeletal mesh, Animation Blueprint, offset), camera_component (a third-person spring arm and camera, made when missing, or with view first_person a camera at the eyes) or nav_movement (AI agent size, avoidance). Each compiles and saves the Blueprint, changes only the fields sent and reads the values back; a Blueprint that is not a Character is refused (NOT_A_CHARACTER).
terms: switch to first person or third person
make the player faster or slower
make the character walk or run faster
change the player model or mesh
set the camera to first person or third person
set the camera behind the player or closer to it
move the camera closer to the player or further away

manage_character.create_character_bluepr.summary: Create a Character Blueprint at path/name (path default /Game) from parentClass (Character or a subclass, default Character), with skeletalMeshPath set on its inherited Mesh, and save it. An asset already at that path is refused (CREATION_FAILED), never reused.

manage_character.create_metahuman.summary: Create an empty MetaHuman Character asset at path/name (path default /Game/MetaHumans), or report the one already there (created false). It is not rigged or built yet (rig_metahuman, build_metahuman); coreDataInstalled says whether the Core Data it needs is installed, saved whether it reached disk. Needs UE 5.6 or later with the MetaHumanCharacter plugin (FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE otherwise).

manage_character.export_metahuman.summary: Export a MetaHuman as skeletal meshes, material instances, or DNA assets.

manage_character.get_character_info.summary: Read a character Blueprint's defaults: capsule size, walk speed, jump velocity and count, air control, gravity scale, spring arm and camera settings, and the live player view state in PIE.

manage_character.metahuman_status.summary: Report MetaHuman readiness: plugin present, Core Data installed, and whether a character is rigged and buildable.

manage_character.rig_metahuman.summary: Auto-rig a MetaHuman character so it can be assembled. Runs on an Epic cloud service.

manage_character.set_movement_property.summary: Set one character movement property: walk speed, jump height (set as its launch speed, JumpZVelocity), gravity scale, ground friction, braking deceleration; compiled, saved and read back.

manage_character.setup_movement.summary: Set a Character Blueprint's walk speed (walkSpeed, or runSpeed when walkSpeed is absent) and acceleration on its Character Movement defaults, then compile and save it; a value not sent stays as it is. The reply gives the maxWalkSpeed and maxAcceleration it now has; a Blueprint that is not a Character is refused (NOT_A_CHARACTER).

manage_combat.apply_damage.summary: Deal damage to an actor in the running game, as a hit does (ApplyDamage): its own damage handling decides what happens, so an actor with the health behaviour loses Health and dies at 0. A negative amount heals such an actor.

manage_combat.configure_damage.summary: Hitboxes on a Blueprint, chosen by setting. hitbox adds or updates the HitboxCapsule, HitboxBox or HitboxSphere component (hitboxType, default Capsule) sized by hitboxSize (only the sizes sent change), on hitboxBoneName of its skeletal mesh when given (NO_SKELETAL_MESH without one), and sets the variables bIsHeadshotZone and HitboxDamageMultiplier. hit_detection makes sure a hitbox of hitboxType exists and sets HitboxDamageMultiplier, without sizing it. An unknown hitboxType is refused. These are a component and variables only: no damage happens until the Blueprint applies it on the hitbox overlap or hit event. Compiles and saves (SAVE_FAILED otherwise).

manage_combat.configure_projectile.summary: Configure projectiles: give a weapon a Fire function that shoots a projectile class, or set a projectile movement, collision or homing.

manage_combat.configure_weapon.summary: A weapon Blueprint, chosen by setting. weapon_mesh assigns weaponMeshPath (a static mesh; NOT_FOUND otherwise) to its WeaponMesh component, added when missing. attachments adds an AttachPoint_<slotName> scene component under WeaponMesh for each attachmentSlots entry: on socketName when given (socketFound says whether the mesh has that socket), with allowedTypes added to its component tags. These are components only; equipping an attachment is Blueprint logic. Compiles and saves (SAVE_FAILED otherwise).

manage_combat.create_combat_asset.summary: Create a combat Blueprint named name in path (default /Game), chosen by kind; it is saved, and a path an asset already holds is refused. weapon_blueprint is an Actor with a WeaponMesh component (weaponMeshPath) and BaseDamage, FireRate, Range and Spread variables (defaults 25, 600, 10000, 2), and no firing logic of its own. projectile_blueprint flies (projectileSpeed, default 5000; projectileGravityScale, default 0), stops on what it meets with a collisionRadius sphere (default 5), applies damage (default 20) to it and is destroyed, never hits the actor that fired it, and is gone 5 s after firing when it meets nothing; projectileMeshPath is its mesh. A mesh path that does not load is refused before anything is made. damage_type (damage_type_setup) is a DamageType Blueprint for ApplyDamage to name.
terms: give the player a gun or a weapon

manage_combat.get_combat_info.summary: Read a weapon or projectile Blueprint: parent class, components, mesh, projectile movement and collision flags, and its variables with defaults; info=stats returns the variables plus a stats object of the numeric ones.

manage_effect.activate.summary: Activate (restarting from age 0 unless reset is false), deactivate or reset the Niagara component on a placed actor (actorName), or with assetPath the one playing that system, on actorName or anywhere in the level; the running game's copy while Play runs. The reply says active, false while its system is still compiling or loading. A miss names what was not found: the actor, its Niagara component, or a component playing assetPath (SYSTEM_NOT_FOUND).
terms: stop or start a fire or an effect

manage_effect.add_niagara_data_interface.summary: Add a data interface to a Niagara emitter: static mesh, skeletal mesh, spline, collision query, audio spectrum.

manage_effect.add_niagara_module.summary: Add a module to a Niagara emitter: any module script by path, or a typed module (spawn rate/burst/per-unit, initialize particle, velocity, acceleration, force, color, size, collision, kill, camera offset, particle state, sprite/mesh/ribbon/light renderer, simulation stage, event generator/receiver). It goes where its dependencies hold (a force before Solve Forces and Velocity).

manage_effect.advance_simulation.summary: Advance a placed Niagara system by steps of deltaTime right away, in the level editor as in a running game, to look at it at a chosen age: spawn it with spawn_niagara, advance it, then capture it with control_editor screenshot from a camera location. The reply gives the age reached and whether the system has finished; NOT_ADVANCED means it did not move (finished, paused or not running).

manage_effect.cleanup.summary: Delete every actor in the level being edited whose label starts with filter, ignoring case, whatever its kind: not only effects. An empty filter deletes nothing. One undo step; refused during Play (PIE_ACTIVE). Replies removed and removedActors.

manage_effect.create_dynamic_light.summary: Spawn a point, spot, directional or rect light (lightType, default Point) at location (default the origin), labelled name: into the running game while Play runs, where it is gone when play stops, otherwise into the level being edited. Only intensity and color are set, each only when given, and there is no rotation: a spot or directional light faces +X until control_actor set_transform aims it.

manage_effect.create_effect.summary: Create an effect: a Niagara system or emitter, a ribbon, particle trail, impact or environment effect, volumetric fog, or spawn a preset particle/niagara effect.
terms: a campfire, fireflies, falling leaves or a waterfall
add sparks, fire or smoke to a torch or a chimney
add a fire or a campfire

manage_effect.debug_shape.summary: Draw a temporary debug shape in the editor viewport (debugOp draw, the default: sphere, box, circle, line, point, coordinate, cylinder, cone, capsule, arrow or plane at location, for duration seconds, default 5), or clear every debug shape drawn (clear). Nothing is spawned or saved, and nothing shows in Play In Editor or a packaged game.
terms: debug sphere box line arrow capsule

manage_effect.edit_niagara_system.summary: Edit a Niagara system: add an emitter (an asset, or a copy of another system's), user parameters or parameter bindings, set parameter values or dynamic inputs, emitter properties, GPU simulation, connect pins.
terms: make the fire bigger or the smoke darker

manage_effect.get_niagara_info.summary: Read a Niagara system: each emitter (enabled, CPU or GPU, stack modules, current module input values, an input that reads a parameter or a dynamic input as {linkedTo}, the static switches such as Ribbon Width Mode that gate them, and its renderers with the object path inspect.set_property writes and their material) and its user parameters with their default values; emitterName and moduleNames narrow it to one emitter and the named modules, and actorName reads one placed effect's own values and which of them it overrides. An emitter asset gives its name and CPU or GPU target. info=validate lists errors and warnings, each naming the module, the problem and the fixes the editor offers.

manage_effect.list_debug_shapes.summary: List the debug shape types that can be drawn (sphere, box, line, arrow, capsule and more) and count the debug lines, points and meshes currently drawn in the editor world.

manage_effect.remove_niagara_node.summary: Remove a node (nodeId, its GUID) from a Niagara system's or emitter's spawn or update script graph (scriptType Update, any case; spawn when absent), reconnecting the parameter map around it; a stack boundary or a branched module is refused. The script recompiles in the background and the system is saved unless save is false.

manage_effect.spawn_niagara.summary: Spawn a Niagara system (systemPath, system or assetPath) as a new actor at location, rotation and scale (scale sizes the effect component), into the Play-In-Editor world while a session runs or else the editor level, optionally attached to attachToActor; autoActivate (default true) starts it at once. Not saved.

manage_gas.configure_ability.summary: Configure a gameplay ability: tags, cooldown, costs, activation and instancing policies; add it to an ability set.

manage_gas.configure_asc.summary: The Ability System Component of an Actor Blueprint, chosen by setting. add_component adds one named componentName (default AbilitySystemComponent); one already there, its own or inherited from a native parent, is kept and named (alreadyExists), never doubled. configure sets its replicationMode: Full (every effect to every client, for single player), Mixed (effects to the owner only, cues and tags to all, for player characters) or Minimal (cues and tags only, for AI). A non-Actor Blueprint is INVALID_TARGET and a name another member holds NAME_TAKEN. Compiles and saves (COMPILE_FAILED or SAVE_FAILED otherwise).

manage_gas.configure_attribute_set.summary: An AttributeSet Blueprint (attributeSetPath), chosen by setting. add_attribute adds a Gameplay Attribute (FGameplayAttributeData) named attributeName at defaultValue (default 0), checked on the compiled class before it saves (ATTRIBUTE_NOT_APPLIED otherwise). base_value sets an existing attribute's base and current value to baseValue (required). A Blueprint that is not an AttributeSet, or a property that is not an attribute, is INVALID_TYPE; a name already there is NAME_TAKEN. Attributes added here do not replicate and are not clamped until the set does that itself.

manage_gas.configure_gameplay_effect.summary: Configure a gameplay effect: duration, stacking, tags, modifiers and magnitudes, execution calculations, cues.

manage_gas.create_gas_asset.summary: Create a Gameplay Ability System asset: gameplay ability, gameplay effect, attribute set, gameplay cue notify, execution calculation.

manage_gas.get_gas_info.summary: Read a Gameplay Ability System Blueprint: its kind (ability, effect, attribute set, cue notify), parent class, and an ability's instancing and net execution policy or an effect's duration policy, stacking type, modifier and cue counts.

manage_geometry.array_mesh.summary: Repeat a mesh inside the same mesh: a row (linear, one offset per copy) or a ring round its local Z (radial). count includes the original.

manage_geometry.boolean_mesh.summary: Combine placed dynamic mesh actors, chosen by booleanOp, editing targetActor's mesh in place in world space: union adds toolActor, subtract cuts it out, intersection keeps only the overlap, trim cuts by trimActorName (keepInside keeps the inside), self_union resolves a mesh's own overlaps. keepTool (default true) keeps the tool actor; a result that would be empty or change nothing is refused (EMPTY_RESULT, NO_EFFECT) with the target as it was and the tool kept to move. Triangle counts before and after come back, and the edit is one undo step.
terms: cut a hole in a mesh or a wall

manage_geometry.configure_mesh_collision.summary: Give a placed dynamic mesh actor simple collision, chosen by collisionOp (UE 5.4 and later). generate fits collisionType box, sphere, capsule or convex (the default, one hull); generate_complex splits the mesh into up to maxHullCount convex hulls (default 8, at most 64) for a concave shape; simplify fits up to targetHullCount hulls (default 4, at most 16) to a copy decimated to simplificationFactor of its triangles (default 0.5), leaving the drawn mesh alone. The reply counts shapeCount; an unknown collisionType is refused.

manage_geometry.configure_mesh_lods.summary: LODs for the meshes the geometry tools make. generate (lodOp generate, the default) bakes the dynamic mesh of actorName or targetActor into a new static mesh asset saved at outputPath (default /Game/GeneratedMeshes/<actor>_LOD) with lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each later one half the triangles of the one before) and replies assetPath, lodCount and the LOD 0 triangles; the actor keeps its dynamic mesh. set_settings and set_screen_sizes change the static mesh asset the first static mesh component of the actor draws, so every actor drawing it changes, and save it (saved says whether it was written); an engine mesh is refused with ENGINE_CONTENT (duplicate it into /Game and assign the copy first). set_settings rebuilds LOD lodIndex (default 1; INVALID_LOD_INDEX past the LODs the mesh has, so generate them first) at trianglePercent of the base triangles (default 50, or 100 minus reductionPercent; above 0 and at most 100), recomputing normals or tangents when asked. set_screen_sizes writes screenSizes, LOD 0 first, as the screen size at which each LOD takes over, and turns the automatic screen sizes off; values past the LODs the mesh has are ignored (screenSizesSet counts those written).

manage_geometry.convert_to_nanite.summary: Bake a dynamic mesh actor into a Nanite-enabled static mesh asset at outputPath (a folder gets <actor>_Nanite; default /Game/GeneratedMeshes/<actor>_Nanite), with a material per slot (materials, entry i for material id i; slots left out get the default material) and collision box (default), complex or none; the asset is saved and naniteEnabled is read back from it. A static mesh already at outputPath is replaced in place (replaced true), so everything drawing it follows; another kind of asset there is refused (ASSET_EXISTS). A material that does not load, or more materials than slots, is refused before anything is created.

manage_geometry.convert_to_static_mesh.summary: Bake a dynamic mesh actor into a static mesh asset at outputPath (a folder gets the actor's name; default /Game/GeneratedMeshes/<actor>), with a material per slot (materials, entry i for material id i; slots left out get the default material) and collision box (default), complex or none; the asset is saved and the actor keeps its dynamic mesh. A static mesh already at outputPath is replaced in place (replaced true), so everything drawing it follows; another kind of asset there is refused (ASSET_EXISTS). A material that does not load, or more materials than slots, is refused before anything is created.

manage_geometry.create_primitive.summary: Create a primitive mesh actor: box (a cube), sphere, cylinder, cone, capsule, plane, disc, ring, torus, pipe, arch, ramp, stairs, spiral stairs, a hip roof over any footprint, or one smooth organic mesh from blended shapes (sdf) with soft fillets where they meet. Each is a DynamicMeshActor with no collision: traces and players pass through it, and what stands on it reads "nothing below it", until configure_mesh_collision gives it some. Each is one undo step.
terms: add stairs, a staircase or a ramp

manage_geometry.deform_mesh.summary: Deform a mesh: bend, twist, taper, stretch, spherify, cylindrify, smooth, relax, noise, lattice, displace by texture. Each edits the placed dynamic mesh in one undo step and leaves the level unsaved.

manage_geometry.edit_dynamic_mesh.summary: Edit a procedural/dynamic mesh: create one, append vertices, triangles, a whole polygon cage (append_polygons), parts laid out in rows and grids (append_cuboids), a loft through cross sections (append_loft), pipes, cables and rings along paths (append_tubes) or copies of a detailed static mesh (append_mesh) in one call, delete the triangles of a region (delete_triangles), give triangles material ids by region (set_material_id), bake AO, edge, cavity and height masks for materials to read (bake_vertex_colors), set vertex positions, colors or UVs, split normals, translate, or subtract another mesh.
terms: author a mesh from vertices and faces

manage_geometry.edit_uvs.summary: Give a placed dynamic mesh actor UVs, chosen by uvOp, in uvChannel (default 0, made when missing); each edit is one undo step. auto and unwrap cut seams with XAtlas and pack the islands into 0-1 (a bounds-sized box projection when XAtlas writes nothing); project box-projects, with tileSize the world size one texture repeat covers (else the texture spans each side once); pack_islands repacks the islands already there; transform shifts (uvOffset), scales (uvScale, about the middle of 0-1) and turns (rotation, degrees) the UVs already there.

manage_geometry.get_mesh_info.summary: Read a procedural DynamicMesh actor: vertex count and triangle count, and whether it has normals, UV sets, vertex colors and polygroups.
terms: how many vertices does a mesh have

manage_geometry.get_vertex_position.summary: Read the x, y, z position of one vertex, by vertexIndex, of a procedural DynamicMesh actor.

manage_geometry.mirror.summary: Mirror a dynamic mesh across a plane: the original stays and a reflected copy is added to the same mesh, welded where the two meet.

manage_geometry.model_mesh.summary: Polygon modeling on a mesh: extrude, inset, outset, offset faces, bevel, chamfer, bridge, loft, sweep, revolve, shell, loop cut, edge split, poke faces, group triangles into quads, or extrude/duplicate along a spline. Extrude, inset, outset, offset, bevel, chamfer and poke work on every triangle, on triangleIndices, or on a region picked by box, facing direction, polygroup or material id. Dynamic meshes are always triangles.

manage_geometry.optimize_mesh.summary: Optimize, smooth or repair a mesh: simplify, remesh (uniform or voxel), subdivide (pn tessellation, or Catmull-Clark, Loop and bilinear surfaces from a polygroup cage), morphology (voxel offset: dilate, contract, close to fillet where unioned parts meet, open), merge or weld vertices, remove degenerates, fill holes, flip or recalculate normals, recompute tangents.
terms: round the edges of a cage

manage_geometry.split_mesh.summary: Split a static mesh asset into one static mesh per connected part (or per material slot), each with its own pivot, the materials it uses and a collision choice.

manage_interaction.configure_interactabl.summary: Configure an interactable: door, chest or switch properties, a door that follows a switch, or its interaction trace.
terms: lock or unlock a door or a chest

manage_interaction.create_interactable.summary: Create an interactable: a door or chest that opens when a pawn comes near, a switch or lever a pawn presses (it fires OnSwitchChanged), a trigger actor, an interactable interface, or an interaction component.
terms: door that opens when the player walks up or gets close
a lever that opens a gate
a locked door that needs a key
a lever that turns on the lights
add a puzzle with switches or levers

manage_interaction.get_interaction_info.summary: Read a door, switch, chest, trigger or other interaction Blueprint: its components and editable property defaults. With actorName, an editor-world actor's name and class only.

manage_inventory.configure_crafting.summary: Edit a crafting recipe made by create_inventory_asset, chosen by setting. add_recipe_ingredient adds ingredientItemPath (an existing item), consumed quantity at a time (default 1), as Ingredient_<n>. recipe_requirements writes requiredLevel and requiredStation, only the ones sent. A recipe of a custom class is refused, so set its own fields with inspect.set_property. Saved unless save is false (saved).

manage_inventory.configure_item.summary: Change an item asset, chosen by setting. properties writes each field of properties: a typed property of a custom item class, else a field of the generic item; failedProperties lists any that did not take, and none taking is INVALID_ARGUMENT. icon sets iconPath, an existing texture or material (empty clears it). stacking writes stackable, maxStackSize and uniqueItems, only the ones sent. category files the item under categoryPath, an existing category asset. A missing item or reference is ASSET_NOT_FOUND. Saved unless save is false (saved).

manage_inventory.configure_loot.summary: Edit a loot table made by create_inventory_asset, chosen by setting. add_entry adds itemPath (an existing item) with lootWeight (default 1) and a quantity range (default 1 to 1) as LootEntry_<n>, returning n as entryIndex. remove_entry drops the entry with that entryIndex, or every entry for itemPath (removedCount; no match is NOT_FOUND). quality_tiers replaces the tiers with tiers ({name, dropWeight}) or the five defaults. Data only: the game reads the table, and nothing rolls loot by itself. Saved unless save is false (saved).

manage_inventory.create_inventory_asset.summary: Create an inventory asset, chosen by kind. item_data_asset, item_category, loot_table and crafting_recipe make generic data assets: the configure actions store their fields and get_inventory_info reads them back. They are data only, for gameplay to read; nothing runs on its own. crafting_station makes an Actor Blueprint with a StationMesh and an InteractionBox. name goes in path (defaults /Game/Items, /Game/Items/Categories, /Game/Data/LootTables, /Game/Data/Recipes and /Game/Blueprints/CraftingStations). An asset already there is refused (ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS), never replaced. A recipe needs outputItemPath, an existing item. Saved unless save is false (saved).

manage_inventory.get_inventory_info.summary: Read an inventory asset: an item (properties), loot table (entries with item, weight and quantity range), recipe (ingredients, output item, station, craft time), or a pickup or inventory Blueprint (components, variables).

manage_inventory.set_inventory_replicati.summary: Make a Blueprint's inventory variables (InventorySlots, MaxSlots, CurrentWeight and MaxWeight, whichever it has) replicate under replicationCondition, or stop (replicated, default false). A RepNotify function already on them is kept; a Blueprint with none of them is NOT_FOUND, and modifiedVariables lists what changed. Saved unless save is false (saved).

manage_level.add_sublevel.summary: Add an existing level map to the level open in the editor as a streaming sublevel, loaded and shown in the editor at once. streamingMethod Blueprint (the default) is not loaded when the game starts until something streams it in (stream during Play, or a Load Stream Level node); AlwaysLoaded loads with the open level. A sublevel already there answers alreadyExists with the method it streams with. The level that was current stays current, so new actors are still spawned where they were (currentLevel names it): the editor's own Add makes the new sublevel current, and this puts the previous one back; set_current_level makes the sublevel current. The add is not undoable and leaves the open level unsaved: save it to keep the sublevel, or load the level again with discardUnsaved to drop it (and every other unsaved change). Refusals: PARENT_LEVEL_NOT_LOADED (parentLevel is not the open level), PACKAGE_NOT_FOUND or FILE_NOT_FOUND (no such map; nothing is left behind).

manage_level.build_lighting.summary: Build the open level static lighting (Lightmass) at quality (default Production; Preview, Medium, High), the same build as build_environment.build_lighting. Reflection captures are not rebuilt, a level whose World Settings force no precomputed lighting is refused (PRECOMPUTED_LIGHTING_DISABLED), an unknown quality is UNKNOWN_QUALITY, and a failed build lists its reasons; it takes minutes, cannot be cancelled once started, and saves nothing.

manage_level.create_level.summary: Create a new empty level map, save it and open it in the editor in place of the open one: levelName in the levelPath folder (default /Game/Maps). A level already at that path is opened instead, not replaced (alreadyExists). Open levels with unsaved changes refuse the call (DIRTY_PACKAGES, listed in unsavedPackages; nothing is created) unless saveDirtyPackages saves them. The new level has no light, sky or floor, so it renders black until some are added. useWorldPartition makes it a World Partition level (default off); when that fails the reply warns and worldPartitionEnabled is false.
terms: add a second level or another map

manage_level.create_light.summary: Spawn a light actor in the level being edited: lightType point, directional, spot, rect or sky (or any light class as lightClass), at location (default 0, 0, 300), labelled name, made Movable; intensity, color and properties are applied, and the reply lists what was applied, refused or adjusted. One undo step; the level is left unsaved. During Play it still spawns into the edited level, not the running game.

manage_level.delete.summary: Delete one level map for good: its .umap, built data and external actor and object files, after taking it out of the open level's streaming list. The open level, or one still loaded, is refused (LEVEL_LOADED): open another map first. No undo and no backup; deleted says whether every file went.

manage_level.duplicate_level.summary: Copy a level map to destinationPath (levelOp duplicate, the default), or rename or move it (rename: newName in the same folder, or destinationPath). Both copy the saved files (the .umap, its built data and its external actor and object files), so unsaved changes to an open level are not in the copy: save first. A destination that exists is refused (DESTINATION_EXISTS) unless overwrite is true, which backs it up and restores it if a step fails; one loaded in the editor is refused (DESTINATION_LOADED). Rename then deletes the source files, and refuses a level loaded in the editor, open or as a sublevel (LEVEL_IN_USE, LEVEL_LOADED). Neither opens the result.

manage_level.export_level.summary: Export the open level: as a .t3d text file inside the project folder (exportPath ending .t3d, relative to the project, e.g. Saved/Exports/Demo.t3d), or as a copy saved to another /Game map path. levelPath, when given, must be the open level (LEVEL_NOT_LOADED otherwise); a /Game copy refuses a destination that already holds another level.

manage_level.get_summary.summary: Read a level (path, name, actor count, asset data) or the one open in the editor, and whether it has unsaved changes, with every unsaved level and asset listed.

manage_level.import_level.summary: Copy a level map from one /Game package path to another (sourcePath or packagePath to destinationPath or targetPath): the .umap, its built data and its external actor and object files, backing up and restoring the destination if a step fails. A destination that exists is refused unless overwrite is true, and a .t3d file cannot be imported (NOT_SUPPORTED). The copy is not opened.

manage_level.list_levels.summary: List the open level and its streaming sublevels (each with loaded, visible and streamingState) and every map the asset registry knows (allMaps, which can be long and comes in pages past 100k characters). Read from the editor world even while Play In Editor runs; the persistent level's name is short, a sublevel's is its package path.

manage_level.load.summary: Open a level in the editor in place of the open one (levelPath: a /Game package or object path, or a bare name tried under /Game/Maps), or with streaming:true add it to the open level as a sublevel instead (add_sublevel answers). Open levels with unsaved changes refuse the load (DIRTY_PACKAGES, listed in unsavedPackages) until saveDirtyPackages saves them or discardUnsaved drops them; the level already open is not reloaded (alreadyLoaded, with its unsaved state); a missing map answers FILE_NOT_FOUND with both paths it checked. The reply waits for the level to settle (settledSeconds), so a screenshot right after shows it drawn.

manage_level.move_actors_to_level.summary: Move placed actors into another loaded level of the open world (one of its sublevels, or the open level itself with levelPath persistent), as the Levels panel's Move Selection to Level does: they are cut and pasted into it, the clipboard kept as it was, and soft references to them follow. One undo step; both levels then need saving. All or none: every name and the level are checked first (ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, SUBLEVEL_NOT_FOUND naming the loaded levels, LEVEL_NOT_LOADED, LEVEL_LOCKED), and an actor already in that level is left as it is and listed under alreadyThere.

manage_level.remove_sublevel.summary: Remove a sublevel from the level open in the editor, as the Levels panel's Remove does: its streaming entry goes and its actors leave the editor world, while its map file stays on disk (manage_level delete removes that). Not undoable, as in the editor. A sublevel with unsaved changes is refused (DIRTY_PACKAGES, listing them) unless discardUnsaved is true, a locked one is refused (LEVEL_LOCKED), a Level Instance's level is not a sublevel (NOT_A_SUBLEVEL: delete its actor instead), and a name that is not a sublevel of the open level is SUBLEVEL_NOT_FOUND, listing the ones it has. The open level is left unsaved: save it (manage_level save) for the removal to last.
terms: take a sublevel out of the level

manage_level.run_map_check.summary: Run the editor's own Map Check (Build > Map Check) on the level open in the editor and answer its messages as rows: severity (error, warning, performance or info), message, the actor it names (actor, actorPath) and code, the map error's name (the key of the engine's guidance for it, such as LightingBuildNeeded or StaticMeshNull). Counts by severity come back as errorCount, warningCount, performanceWarningCount and noteCount, with total; at most 200 rows (truncated says when more were found). No Message Log tab opens and nothing in the level changes. NO_WORLD: no level is open.

manage_level.save.summary: Save the open level in place (saveMode save, the default; a levelPath naming another level is refused with LEVEL_NOT_LOADED, an unsaved new level with TRANSIENT_LEVEL) or under a new /Game path (as: savePath, refused with ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS where something already is). It writes the level's own package: sublevels and changed assets are separate packages it leaves unsaved (control_editor save_all writes everything dirty). Not undoable.

manage_level.set_current_level.summary: Choose the loaded level of the open world that the editor spawns and pastes actors into, as the Levels panel does: one of its sublevels, or the open level itself with levelPath persistent. A hidden level is shown (shown). The reply names that level before (previousLevel) and after (currentLevel); undo does not restore the earlier one, so calling this again with previousLevel puts it back. Refusals: PIE_ACTIVE (stop Play first), SUBLEVEL_NOT_FOUND or AMBIGUOUS_LEVEL (naming the loaded levels), NOT_A_SUBLEVEL (a Level Instance's level: edit its Level Instance instead), LEVEL_NOT_LOADED, LEVEL_LOCKED (unlock it in the Levels panel first).

manage_level.set_metadata.summary: Write key/value pairs into the editor metadata of a /Game level (levelPath; NOT_FOUND when no such map, SECURITY_VIOLATION outside /Game): text as given, numbers and booleans as text, objects and arrays as JSON text; null and empty values are skipped, and an empty metadata object is refused. updatedKeys counts the keys written, and the level is left unsaved. The metadata is editor-only and not kept in a packaged game.

manage_level.set_world_settings.summary: Set the loaded level's WorldSettings: GameMode override, kill Z, gravity, time dilation, and world bounds checks.

manage_level.stream.summary: Stream in a sublevel of the open level (streamOp stream, the default) or stream it out (unload). During Play it streams in the running game, as the Load and Unload Stream Level nodes do, and settles before the reply; otherwise the editor, which keeps every sublevel loaded, shows or hides it as the Levels panel does, and unload hides it with a warning. The reply says which world it acted on (play or editor) and whether the level is loaded and visible now. levelPath is the full package path or the part after its last slash; STREAMING_LEVEL_NOT_FOUND means it is not a sublevel yet (add_sublevel), AMBIGUOUS_LEVEL that two sublevels share the name (listed in matches), LEVEL_NOT_LOADED that its map failed to load.

manage_level.unload_level.summary: Stream a sublevel out (alias of unload): unloaded during Play, hidden with a warning in the editor.

manage_level.validate_level.summary: Check that a level asset exists: returns exists, its normalized path, the .umap file path, and whether the package and the file are present.

manage_level_structure.configure_level_s.summary: Configure streaming and partition: level streaming, streaming distance, World Partition, grid size, HLOD layer, data-layer assignment.

manage_level_structure.create_level_stru.summary: Create level structure, chosen by kind: level (a new map asset, optionally opened), sublevel (a new level streamed into the open one), level_instance (an actor loading a saved level, to reuse a room or building), packed_level_actor (a saved level baked into one instanced-mesh Blueprint), data_layer (World Partition), or minimap_volume (the area a World Partition minimap captures).

manage_level_structure.create_volume.summary: Place a volume of volumeClass in the editor level as a box brush: extent is half its size on each axis (each class has its own default), at location (default the origin) and rotation, labelled volumeName (default the class name). Each class reads only its own settings and refuses one it would ignore: pain (bPainCausing, damagePerSec), physics (fluidFriction, terminalVelocity, bWaterVolume), audio and reverb (bEnabled, reverbVolume, fadeTime), cull distance (cullDistances), post-process (bUnbound, blendRadius, blendWeight, priority, postProcessSettings), KillZ (killZHeight); the trigger box, sphere and capsule take boxExtent, sphereRadius, or capsuleRadius and capsuleHalfHeight. actorPath attaches the volume to an actor instead (Trigger, Blocking, KillZ, Physics, CullDistance and PostProcess). save saves the level too (default false).

manage_level_structure.edit_level_bluepr.summary: Edit the level Blueprint of the open level (levelPath names another loaded level; by default the persistent level), chosen by edit. open opens its editor; add_node adds a node by class or alias (an event bound to a placed actor with actorName and eventName, a reference to one, a component getter with memberClass and memberName) and lists its pins; connect_nodes links two pins through the graph schema, which refuses incompatible ones (CONNECTION_REFUSED, with its reason) and adds the conversion node a cast needs; remove_node removes a node by id, name or title; set_pin_default_value sets an input pin. The level stays unsaved unless save is true (saved), and a transient /Temp level is refused.

manage_level_structure.get_level_structu.summary: Read the open level's structure: streaming sub-levels (loaded, visible, actor counts), whether World Partition is on, its data layers, level instances and HLOD layers.

manage_level_structure.get_volumes_info.summary: List the volumes and trigger actors in the level with name, class, location and box extent, and a total count; filter by label or volumeType (a class name part such as Trigger or PostProcess).

manage_level_structure.remove_volume.summary: Delete a volume or trigger actor from the editor level by its label (any case). Saved only with save true, which also writes the level's other unsaved changes and cannot be undone; without it the removal is one undo step and the level stays unsaved.

manage_level_structure.set_volume_proper.summary: Change a volume found by its label (volumeName), chosen by volumeProperty. properties sets what its class carries: a Physics Volume bWaterVolume, fluidFriction, terminalVelocity and priority; a Pain Causing Volume bPainCausing and damagePerSec; an Audio Volume bEnabled, reverbVolume and fadeTime; a Post Process Volume priority, blendWeight and bEnabled. The reply lists propertiesSet and propertiesIgnored (what this class lacks), and is NO_PROPERTIES_APPLIED when nothing applied. extent sets its half-size (default 100 on each axis); bounds moves and sizes it from a min and a max corner. The level is saved only with save true, which also writes its other unsaved changes.

manage_networking.add_legacy_mapping.summary: Bind a key to a legacy (Project Settings, Input) mapping, chosen by mapping: action takes actionName (or name), key and the shift, ctrl, alt and cmd modifiers; axis takes axisName (or name), key and scale (default 1, -1 for the reverse direction). key is the engine key name (SpaceBar, W, LeftMouseButton, Gamepad_LeftX); an unknown one is INVALID_ARGUMENT. A binding already there is kept (alreadyPresent true, added false); a new one is written to the project DefaultInput.ini (defaultConfigUpdated). Projects on Enhanced Input map keys with manage_networking configure_input instead.

manage_networking.add_local_player.summary: Add a local (split-screen) player to the running game for a gamepad controllerId, spawning a player controller for it; the reply gives its playerIndex. Needs Play In Editor (NOT_IN_PLAY); local players end when play stops.

manage_networking.check_authority.summary: Check an actor's network role by actorName: check=has_authority returns hasAuthority and the local net role; check=is_locally_controlled returns whether a pawn is locally controlled and has a local player controller.

manage_networking.configure_game_mode.summary: Change a game mode Blueprint (gameModeBlueprint or blueprintPath), chosen by setting, then compile and save it: default_pawn_class (pawnClass; "None" for no default pawn), player_controller_class, game_state_class, player_state_class and hud_class set the class it spawns for that role (a class that does not load is NOT_FOUND); rules sets bDelayedStart, respawn sets respawnDelay (both on GameMode children only, a GameModeBase child is NOT_SUPPORTED), spectating sets spectatorClass. A class setting never changes which game mode plays: makeDefault true makes this one the project default (DefaultEngine.ini), and the reply says whether the open level plays with it (effectiveInOpenLevel, openLevelGameMode).

manage_networking.configure_input.summary: Enhanced Input: create an input action or mapping context, add or map keys, set triggers and modifiers, enable a context.

manage_networking.configure_player_start.summary: Set the PlayerStartTag of a PlayerStart in the open level: an explicit tag, or TeamN for teamIndex N. The engine only matches the tag against a ?Portal=<tag> travel option; team spawning needs a game mode that reads it. Undoable; the level is left modified, not saved.
terms: make the player spawn here or at a place

manage_networking.configure_prediction.summary: Configure client-side prediction: client, movement, server correction, or add prediction data (a variable replicated only to the owning client).

manage_networking.configure_replication.summary: Configure replication on a Blueprint: property replication and conditions, RepNotify, net role, dormancy, relevancy, priority, update frequency, cull distance, push model, replicated movement, replication graph, net driver.

manage_networking.configure_rpc.summary: Blueprint RPCs, chosen by setting. create makes a function graph named functionName (a free name: NAME_TAKEN otherwise) in an Actor or ActorComponent Blueprint (INVALID_TARGET otherwise) whose calls run where rpcType says: Server, Client or NetMulticast. inputs are its parameters ({name, type}); reliable defaults to true. The function body is the graph of that name, built with manage_blueprint edit_graph, and it is called like any function. The Blueprint compiles and saves, and actorReplicates says whether it replicates, without which no RPC leaves the machine. reliability makes an existing RPC (that function, or a custom event set to replicate) reliable or not; a non-replicating one is NOT_AN_RPC. validation true is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED): only C++ RPCs validate, so check the parameters at the start of the body. changed false means the flag already had that value and nothing was compiled or saved.

manage_networking.configure_session.summary: Configure multiplayer for the project: the default game port for LAN hosting and joining, the online subsystem (Null, Steam, EOS...), and the local split-screen layout. Written to DefaultEngine.ini.

manage_networking.configure_voice.summary: Voice chat: start or stop it now, set the project VoIP settings (online voice on or off, mic gain, noise gate, silence detection, sample rate), or mute a player.

manage_networking.create_framework_class.summary: Create a game framework Blueprint: game mode, game state, game instance, player controller, player state, HUD.

manage_networking.get_game_framework_inf.summary: Read which game mode is in use and its default classes (pawn, player controller, game state, player state, HUD), from a game mode Blueprint or from the live world, the level override or the project default; a role it spawns nothing for (a default pawn set to None) reads "None".

manage_networking.get_input_info.summary: Read an input asset: every key mapping of an Input Mapping Context (details.mappings: key, action, triggers, modifiers) or an Input Action's value type and consume flag.

manage_networking.get_networking_info.summary: Read an actor's or Blueprint's replication settings: replicates, always relevant, only relevant to owner, net update frequency, cull distance, priority and dormancy; for a live actor also its net role, remote role and authority.

manage_networking.get_sessions_info.summary: Read the current play session: local player count, whether PIE is running, the split-screen setting and layout, and each PIE instance's net mode (Standalone, DedicatedServer, ListenServer or Client) and URL.

manage_networking.host_lan_server.summary: Host a LAN listen server (build the travel URL, optionally travel to it), or make a running Play-In-Editor instance join one.

manage_networking.remove_legacy_mapping.summary: Remove the binding of key from a legacy action or axis mapping, chosen by mapping (actionName, axisName or name): every binding of that name and key goes (an action binding only with the same shift, ctrl, alt and cmd), removedCount says how many, and a pair that is not bound is NOT_FOUND with nothing written. The project DefaultInput.ini is written (defaultConfigUpdated).

manage_networking.remove_local_player.summary: Remove a local player from the running game by playerIndex; the first player (index 0) cannot be removed (PRIMARY_PLAYER), and the players after it move down one index. Needs Play In Editor (NOT_IN_PLAY).

manage_networking.remove_mapping.summary: Remove an Enhanced Input mapping; removing an action's keys is how an input action is disabled.

manage_networking.set_owner.summary: Set or clear (empty ownerActorName) the owner of a runtime actor; an owner name that matches no actor is refused.

manage_pcg.add_pcg_node.summary: Add a node to a PCG graph (graphPath), chosen by nodeKind. node takes any PCG settings class by name (settingsClass or nodeType, such as PCGStaticMeshSpawnerSettings or StaticMeshSpawner; CLASS_NOT_FOUND otherwise). The other kinds add a ready node: surface_sampler, spline_sampler, mesh_sampler (meshPath, checked to load), volume_sampler, static_mesh_spawner (meshPath), actor_spawner (actorClass), spline_spawner, density_filter, distance_filter, height_filter (an attribute range filter), slope_filter (Normal To Density), bounds_filter (culls points outside actor bounds), bounds_modifier, the landscape, spline, actor, texture (texturePath) and volume data nodes, transform_points, copy_points, merge_points, project_to_surface and self_pruning. settings sets any property of the new node by name (INVALID_SETTINGS for one it lacks); nodeName titles it and x, y place it. The reply gives nodeId (for connect_pcg_pins), title, nodeType, settingsApplied and saved; saved unless save is false.

manage_pcg.edit_pcg_graph.summary: Build a PCG graph, chosen by edit. create makes a graph asset and create_subgraph one to run inside another (with parentGraphPath it adds the Subgraph node there too); a graph already at the path is refused unless overwrite is true, which hands back that graph unchanged (created false). connect_pins wires an output pin of one node to an input pin of another (labels default to Out and In; PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the labels). set_node_settings changes an existing node (found by nodeId or nodeName) and refuses an edit that changes nothing. set_partition_grid_size sets the world or one component's generation grid and saves the level unless save is false. Graph edits save the graph unless save is false (saved).

manage_pcg.execute_pcg_graph.summary: Generate a PCG graph on a placed PCG component: the one actorName, componentName or componentPath names, or with createComponent a new one on actorName (one it already has is used; createdComponent says which). graphPath becomes the component's graph and generation is scheduled to run over the next frames (force, default true, regenerates an up-to-date component); read PCGComponent.bGenerated with inspect get_property to see it finished (partitioned actors keep it false). GENERATION_NOT_SCHEDULED when it is already generating, has no graph or has invalid bounds; save also saves the level.

manage_tools.disable_category.summary: Disable a category (world, gameplay, utility, or all, which leaves core on): its tools stay in search, but execute refuses them (TOOL_DISABLED). core cannot be disabled.

manage_tools.disable_tools.summary: Disable parent tools by name (tools): their capabilities stay in search, marked unavailable, and execute refuses them (TOOL_DISABLED). manage_tools and inspect cannot be disabled (listed under protected); names that are no parent tool come back under notFound. Each door keeps its own setting until restart.

manage_tools.enable_category.summary: Enable a category of parent tools (core, world, gameplay, utility, or all) and every tool in it; enabled lists the tools that were off.

manage_tools.enable_tools.summary: Enable parent tools by name (tools), reopening their categories, so their capabilities run again; names that are no parent tool come back under notFound. The setting lasts until the server restarts and each door (the stdio server, the editor endpoint) keeps its own.

manage_tools.get_status.summary: Read how many tools are enabled and disabled, the per-category breakdown, and the catalog revision numbers.

manage_tools.get_task_result.summary: Read a call that answered "still running": whether it is queued, running or done, and once done the reply it would have given.

manage_tools.list_categories.summary: List the four tool categories (core, world, gameplay, utility), each with its enabled flag, tool count and enabled tool count.

manage_tools.list_tools.summary: List the 23 parent tools, each with its category and whether it is enabled now (its own flag and its category both on), with enabled and disabled counts. Tool groups only decide what execute runs: the one public tool stays listed and search keeps every capability.

manage_tools.reset.summary: Put every tool and category back: the stdio server turns all of them on, the editor endpoint returns to the state it started with (only core when it loads tools on demand). enabled counts the tools switched back on.

material.add_function_io.summary: Add a pin to a material function (assetPath), chosen by io: input adds a Function Input named inputName of inputType (default Vector3; an unknown type is refused) that callers wire into; output adds a Function Output named inputName that carries out whatever is wired into it, of that type. A name the function already has is NAME_TAKEN. The node lands at x, y (default 0, 0), the function recompiles and is left unsaved; the reply gives its nodeId for connect_nodes.

material.add_material_node.summary: Add a node to a material graph: any expression class by name, or a typed node (parameters, texture sample/coordinate, math, noise, panner, rotator, fresnel, switches, custom HLSL, function call, landscape layer), or build a whole graph (nodes, wires, material properties) in one batch.
terms: make a material scroll or pan

material.compile_material.summary: Recompile a material or material function from its graph (compileOp compile, the default; rebuild runs the same recompile) and wait for every shader. A material that does not compile answers compiled false with compileErrors, since it renders as the default material until fixed; saved says whether it was written (save, default true). A material function is updated without the shader check.

material.configure_layer_blend.summary: Add a Landscape Layer Blend node to a landscape material, listing the paint layers in order (layers; the first previews at full weight), each with its blend: weight, height or alpha. Every call adds a new node, at x, y (default 0, 0); wire its output with connect_nodes (blendNodeId). An unknown blend type is refused. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved).

material.connect_nodes.summary: Wire an output of sourceNodeId (sourcePin: a name, an index or channel letters such as G or RG; default its first output) into targetPin of targetNodeId, replacing whatever fed that input. targetNodeId Main is the material output (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor...), or in a material function its output named targetPin (the first when left out). The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it). NODE_NOT_FOUND names Main when the target id is missing; INVALID_PIN or PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the inputs the node has.

material.create_material.summary: Create a material asset: a standard material, a decal, landscape or post-process material, a material function, or a Material Parameter Collection (values every material reading it shares). A new material has nothing wired in; add_material_node with nodeKind batch gives it a colour, textures and its other inputs in one call.
terms: make the floor or a surface shiny

material.create_material_instance.summary: Create a material instance from a parent material or another instance (a child instance), optionally with its parameter values already set, or several instances (a palette) under one consent.

material.delete_node.summary: Delete nodes from a material or material function graph: nodeId, or nodeIds for several. Every wire to a deleted node is cut, the material outputs it fed included, so what it fed falls back to its default; the material is then recompiled and saved unless save is false. Ids that match nothing come back in notFound, and NOT_FOUND answers only when none matched (read the ids with get_material_info or find_node).

material.disconnect_nodes.summary: Unplug the wire into pinName of nodeId (or with nodeId Main a material output such as BaseColor), keeping both nodes; the input falls back to its default. A pin name that matches none fails listing the inputs; a material function output node with no pinName unplugs every output. The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it).

material.get_material_info.summary: Inspect a material or material function: summary with its parameters and overrides, node lookup, node details/properties/connections, node chains and connected subgraphs.

material.set_material_parameter.summary: Set material parameter values, chosen by parameterKind. On a material instance it overrides a parameter its parent publishes (a name it does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing the published ones); on a base material it sets the parameter node's default, refused while the material is open in its editor (ASSET_EDITOR_OPEN; the editor would write its own copy back on close). scalar takes a number value, vector value {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a], texture texturePath, static_switch value true or false, and a missing value is refused; parameter takes parameterType (scalar, the default, vector or texture) with value, several at once with parameters, or several instances under one consent with assets. The asset is saved unless save is false (saved).

material.set_material_property.summary: Set a property of a material, or override it on a material instance, by materialProperty: blend_mode, domain, shading_model or two_sided. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved), and the reply gives the value written; on an instance the value becomes an override of its parent, as its Material Property Overrides do (instanceOverride), and the domain cannot be overridden (MATERIAL_INSTANCE). An unknown value is INVALID_ENUM, listing the valid ones, and leaves the asset as it was; a material function is UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT), so duplicate it into /Game first.

material.set_node_position.summary: Move a node of a material or material function graph (materialPath or assetPath; nodeId as add_material_node and get_material_info give it) to x and y, keeping every wire. The move is one undo step (the reply's undo block says so); the material recompiles and is left unsaved; the reply gives where the node now sits and warns when it overlaps another.

material.update_custom_expression.summary: Update a custom expression node: its HLSL code, inputs, output type, additional outputs or title. An input that keeps its name keeps its wire. The material is then compiled and saved, and compiled, compileErrors and saved in the reply say how that went (a step of build_material_graph leaves both to the batch).

sequence.cinematic.add_cinematic_track.summary: Add a cinematic track: camera cut, camera shake, transform, property, skeletal animation, material parameter, particle, event, fade, level visibility, shot, or subsequence.
terms: fade the cutscene in or out

sequence.cinematic.configure_cinematic.summary: Cinematic cameras and shots, chosen by setting. camera sets a CineCameraActor's focal length, aperture, sensor size and focus distance and reads back what the camera kept after clamping to its lens (values); rig_rail sets a rail rig's positionOnRail (0 to 1) and rig_crane a crane rig's pitch, yaw and arm length, each placing the rig at the world origin when actorName names none (spawned); shot sets a shot's display name, range or row. camera and the rigs are one undo step, and a call with nothing to set is refused.

sequence.cinematic.create_cinematic_asse.summary: Create a cinematic piece, chosen by kind. master_sequence makes a level sequence (name in path, default /Game/Cinematics, or sequencePath) at frameRate (default 24 fps) playing from startFrame (default 0) for durationFrames (default 240) or to endFrame, and saves it; it starts with no tracks, so add shots with add_shot_track and sub-sequences with add_subsequence. A level sequence already there is kept (alreadyExists); another asset there is ASSET_TYPE_MISMATCH. cine_camera_actor places a Cine Camera Actor named actorName (or label) at location and rotation with the lens, filmback and focus settings given (appliedProperties) and, with path or sequencePath, binds it to that sequence (bindingGuid); during Play it goes into the running game.

sequence.create.summary: Create a level sequence (sequenceOp create, the default): name in the folder path (default /Game), or path naming the asset itself; it is saved (saved), and a level sequence already there is kept and answered with alreadyExists, while another asset there is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS. duplicate copies the sequence at path into the folder destinationPath as newName and saves the copy; rename gives the sequence at path the name newName in its folder (a path starting with / moves it), references following it; the engine saves it and leaves a redirector at the old path when other assets reference it. Only /Game paths are written (SEQUENCE_PATH_NOT_WRITABLE); a source that is not a level sequence is INVALID_SEQUENCE, and a taken destination ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.
terms: add a cutscene at the start of the level
make a cutscene of the castle, the level or a place
make a trailer or a cinematic

sequence.delete.summary: Delete a level sequence (deleteScope sequence, the default: refused with SEQUENCE_IN_USE, naming referencedBy, while a level or asset still uses it; its editors close and the undo history may be cleared), remove one track by name (track, one undo step), or remove keys (keyframe: from the tracks trackName or bindingId picks, on frame or frames, else every key on them; one undo step; replies removedKeys).

sequence.edit_sequence_bindings.summary: Bind actors to a Level Sequence at path, chosen by edit; an asset that is not a Level Sequence is refused. add_actor and add_actors bind placed actors by label as possessables, reusing a binding an actor already has, and answer per actor (results, successful, failed; NO_ACTORS_BOUND when none bound); add_camera places a CameraActor at the world origin and binds it (actorName labels it), or with spawnable true adds a camera the sequence owns that exists only while it plays; add_spawnable adds a spawnable of className; remove_actors drops the bindings of the named actors (NO_ACTORS_REMOVED when none was bound). Each answers the bindingGuid it made or found.

sequence.edit_sequence_tracks.summary: Edit sequence tracks: add a track, section or keyframe; move, trim or ease a section, or change the play rate of an animation clip; lock, mute or solo a track.

sequence.get_metadata.summary: Read the custom metadata tags (string key/value pairs written by set_metadata) stored on a Level Sequence, or look up one key.

sequence.get_properties.summary: Read a sequence: properties, bindings, tracks, the keys on a track, the available track types, list sequences, or open one in Sequencer.

sequence.media.create_media_asset.summary: Create media playback pieces, chosen by kind, each saved: source points at a local video file (under Content or Saved) or per-platform sources, player plays a source (loop, playOnOpen), playlist strings sources and files together, texture shows a player's picture in a material or widget, sound_component gives a placed actor the player's sound. A taken name is refused.

sequence.media.play_media.summary: Play a media player asset (control play, the default): it opens mediaSourcePath, a playlist (playlistPath, playlistIndex) or filePath first when given, closing what it was playing, else plays what it has open, and the reply waits up to 10 s for it to open and start (openStatus, openWaitMs, isPlaying, currentUrl), failing with MEDIA_OPEN_FAILED, MEDIA_OPEN_TIMEOUT or MEDIA_PLAY_TIMEOUT. Or pause it (pause) or seek it (seek). The picture shows only where its media texture is used (a material on a mesh, or a widget), and its sound needs a media sound component.

sequence.mrq.configure_render_job.summary: Configure a Movie Render Queue job: output settings, anti-aliasing, render passes, burn-ins, console variables, and the camera setting (shutter timing, overscan).

sequence.mrq.create_render_job.summary: Movie Render Queue: create a render job, queue it, start rendering, cancel a running render, or remove jobs from the queue.
terms: render the sequence to a video file

sequence.planner.auto_edit.summary: Cut a Level Sequence between its cameras the way an editor would, as its camera cut track: the playback range is split into segments (segmentSeconds, default 0.5), and at each segment's middle every camera is scored by how it shows the subjects as the sequence plays them (each subject hidden behind something or out of frame, the first, the main one, counting double; the main one too small or too large), and every cut by its jump (two cameras within 30 degrees of each other round the main subject) and its crossing of the line between the first two subjects. The cheapest edit whose shots all last minShotSeconds to maxShotSeconds (default 1.5 to 8) is found by dynamic programming over segment, camera and time held, and replaces the camera cut track's sections, cameras bound to the sequence when they are not, in one undo step. dryRun answers the shots without writing. Refused, changing nothing, with NO_CUT (some moment no camera sees the main subject: unseenSeconds lists when), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_SEQUENCE, INVALID_ARGUMENT (fewer than 2 cameras, a range shorter than the shortest shot).

sequence.planner.fly_through.summary: Fly a camera through points of the level and key the flight into a Level Sequence, never nearer to geometry than a clearance: between two points the camera goes straight when nothing is in the way, else round or over what is (a search through free space, cut short wherever a straight line is clear), and the corners are smoothed into one minimum-snap curve (unbroken in speed, acceleration and jerk) at rest at both ends, timed by distance over seconds (default the path length at 3 m/s). It faces lookAt (an actor) the whole way, else the way ahead. Keys every tenth of a second go on a transform track of its own (an earlier one of that camera is replaced: replacedTrack says so), with a camera cut to it over the flight and the playback range grown to hold it, all in one undo step, from the sequence's playback start; the camera is the actor named camera (default FlyCamera), or a CineCameraActor spawned under that label. dryRun answers the corners and the length without writing. Refused, changing nothing, with POINT_IN_SOLID (a point nearer to geometry than clearanceCm; point gives its index), NO_PATH (no way through free space joins two points, or the smoothed curve cannot be kept clear), ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (lookAt), INVALID_SEQUENCE, INVALID_ARGUMENT.
terms: fly the camera through the level
move the camera along a path in a cutscene
add a camera that follows a path

sequence.planner.frame_shot.summary: Place a camera so one or two actors sit where they should on screen: by default one subject on the left third line, two on the left and right third lines (framing gives each its own screen point). It searches the places around the subjects for the best view: every subject clear of what stands between (each sight line to it traced), the camera out of walls and floors, seen a little from above, a lone subject three-quarter on from its front and turned into the frame; the camera never rolls. One subject is sized by shotSize (close: its box spans 90% of the frame; medium: 55%; wide: 25%); two are sized by how far apart their screen points are, and kept about as far from the camera as each other (a two-shot, not one subject looming over the other). Moves the camera actor named camera (default ShotCamera), or spawns a CineCameraActor under that label when no actor has it, and sets its focal length (focalLength; else 85, 50 or 24 mm by shot size, 35 mm for two subjects) and its manual focus on the first subject, all in one undo step. dryRun answers the same without moving or spawning anything. Each subject comes back with its target, where it landed (screen) and how hidden it is. Refused, changing nothing, with ACTOR_NOT_FOUND (a subject is not in the level; missing lists it), NO_CLEAR_SHOT (no place found sees every subject at least half clear with the camera out of solid geometry: the best one tried is in the details), INVALID_ARGUMENT (a subject that draws nothing, framing points that do not fit the subjects, focalLength on a plain camera, a camera actor with no camera component).
terms: aim a camera at two actors

sequence.play.summary: Play, pause or stop a level sequence in the editor; pause with startTime moves the playhead to that time and holds the frame there, so the level shows that moment.

sequence.replay.configure_demo_settings.summary: Set how this editor session records and plays demo replays, chosen by setting. demo stores the default replayName and friendlyName, extra additionalOptions, maxRecordTimeSeconds (up to 86400), checkpointSaveMaxMSPerFrame (up to 1000 ms; also written to the engine config and the demo driver defaults), playbackSpeed, prioritizeActors and loadDefaultMapOnStop; a recording or playback running now takes them at once (appliedToRuntime), and the reply lists everything stored. killcam_duration sets how many seconds start_killcam replays (up to 600). All but the checkpoint budget last until the editor closes.

sequence.replay.play_demo.summary: Record and play back gameplay replays in the running game, chosen by control; outside Play every control is NOT_IN_PIE. start_recording records replayName (else the configured default, else McpReplay_<time>) until stop_recording, which answers the name, and is refused while a replay plays or records (ALREADY_PLAYING, ALREADY_RECORDING). play plays replayName back (refused while recording); pause pauses or resumes it (paused; without it, toggles); seek jumps to timeSeconds, clamped to the replay's length, and answers once playback gets there (REPLAY_SEEK_TIMEOUT after 10 s); set_playback_speed sets speed (at most 16); start_killcam plays the last durationSeconds of the playing replay, or of replayName. pause, seek and set_playback_speed need a replay playing (NOT_PLAYING). Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).

sequence.set_metadata.summary: Write metadata tags to a Level Sequence asset's package (metadata object, or one key with value) and save it; values are kept as text, and only strings, numbers and booleans are written. The reply lists the keys set and the whole stored map; saved says whether the save worked.

sequence.set_properties.summary: Set sequence properties: playback range and frame rate, display rate, tick resolution, playback speed, view range, work range.

sequence.take.configure_take_recorder.summary: Record a take with the Take Recorder (Takes plugin), chosen by setting: sources picks the actors and allowlisted source classes to record and the sequence or preset to record from; recorded_tracks turns recorded properties of actor sources on or off; panel opens the panel and reads its mode, sequence, frame rate and source count; start_recording begins a take once its countdown ends, for duration seconds or until stop_recording; stop_recording finalizes the take and says whether it recorded anything (RECORDING_OUTPUT_EMPTY when not). Setup changes are refused while a take records (RECORDING_ACTIVE), and a refused call leaves the panel and sources as they were.

struct.delete_struct.summary: Delete a Blueprint Struct asset (deleteScope struct, the default: refused with STRUCT_IN_USE, naming referencers, while other assets use it, unless force deletes it anyway and recompiles the loaded Blueprints that used it; NOT_FOUND when there is none) or remove one member (member: by memberName or varGuid; the assets using the struct are refreshed, and it is saved unless save is false).

struct.edit_struct.summary: Create a user-defined struct or edit it: members, defaults, metadata, types, order, rename, duplicate, import, recompile, refresh dependencies, instanced struct properties.

struct.get_struct.summary: Read structs, chosen by info. struct (read, members and export give the same reply) reads a Blueprint or native struct: name, status, validity and every member { guid, name, type, default, tooltip, containerType, metaData }, the members array import_struct takes back; list lists the Blueprint struct assets under path (default /Game/Structs, recursive); usage lists the assets that reference a Blueprint struct (assetPath, className, referencerType Blueprint, Struct, DataAsset or Other), narrowed by a searchScope path prefix; compare diffs two Blueprint structs member by member, paired by member guid so a rename reads as renamedFrom and renamedTo, each diff added, removed or changed with its type and default in each, plus tooltip and metadata mismatches (metadata from UE 5.5); instanced_property reads an FInstancedStruct property of an asset. Nothing is written.

system_control.configure_display.summary: Configure display and rendering variables: resolution, fullscreen, quality, a console variable, FPS counter, profiling overlay.

system_control.configure_performance.summary: Configure performance settings, chosen by setting: scalability levels or a baseline profile (saved, kept across restarts); session-only console settings (frame rate cap, resolution scale, vsync, LOD and mip bias, Nanite, occlusion culling, texture streaming, draw-call batching, GPU timing), each set as the console does and read back, with appliedCVars and notSet in the reply and CVAR_UNAVAILABLE when none took; World Partition streaming and grid; a shader recompile.
terms: make the game run at 60 fps

system_control.configure_rendering.summary: Set or read the project's rendering methods by plain name: global illumination and reflections (lumen, screen_space, none), shadows (virtual, maps), anti-aliasing (tsr, taa, fxaa, msaa, none), hardware ray tracing, mesh distance fields, MegaLights, and the default bloom, auto exposure and motion blur. Each change is saved to DefaultEngine.ini and applied live where its console variable allows; the reply reads every setting back and lists the ones that wait for an editor restart.

system_control.console_command.summary: Run one console command against the editor world, or through the first player while Play In Editor runs, and return what it printed (output) and what the engine logged meanwhile (log), each kept short: the first 30 lines and any Error: or Warning: line after them, at most three lines that open with the same two words, and (+N more lines) where lines were left out; at most 4096 characters. A command the engine does not recognise fails (EXEC_FAILED); one holding ;, |, &&, a backtick or several lines, or a blocked name (quit, exit, py, crash and the like), is refused (COMMAND_BLOCKED). Success means the engine ran it, not that it had the effect wanted.

system_control.create_cpp_class.summary: Create a new C++ class in a project module, as the editor's New C++ Class does: a header and a .cpp from a parent class (Actor, Character, ActorComponent, Object ..., or None for a plain class), then the editor's own compile.

system_control.create_plugin.summary: Make a content-only plugin in this project's Plugins folder (the Plugins browser's Content Only template: a descriptor, a Content folder and the template icon), mount it and enable it in the project at once, so assets can go under its mountedContentPath (/Name/) straight away. template game_feature makes a game feature plugin instead (the Game Feature (Content Only) template): under Plugins/GameFeatures, loaded by the Game Features subsystem rather than at startup, with its GameFeatureData asset made and saved (gameFeatureData), and activated at once (list_game_features shows when it gets there); it needs the GameFeatures plugin (GAME_FEATURES_DISABLED; GAME_FEATURES_UNAVAILABLE in a build of EngineWire without its game features module, such as the Fab one; ENGINE_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED on UE 5.0). A plugin with code is not made (it needs a build). A name taken by any installed plugin, or by a folder, is PLUGIN_EXISTS; a name that is no valid identifier is INVALID_ARGUMENT; nothing is created then.

system_control.create_widget.summary: Make a Widget Blueprint and fill it, or raise an editor notification, chosen by widgetOp. create makes a Widget Blueprint asset (name and savePath, default /Game/UI/Widgets, or widgetPath) from UserWidget or a subclass (widgetType). add_child adds a widget of childClass (TextBlock, Button, Image and so on) under parentName (default the root panel; PARENT_NOT_FOUND for a name that is no panel), named name, with text for one that shows text. show only raises an editor toast with message for duration seconds (default 4): it puts nothing on screen in the game. To show a Widget Blueprint in the game, give a Blueprint Create Widget and Add to Viewport nodes (blueprint.edit_graph), or use blueprint.add_behaviour for a HUD piece.

system_control.delete_output_file.summary: Delete files the MCP wrote (screenshots, captures, EngineWire's own files, mesh exports, thumbnails, environment snapshots), one path or a list of paths; a folder a delete leaves empty goes too, so deleting every file of a plugin remove_plugin moved aside removes its folder. Nothing outside Saved/Screenshots, Saved/Captures, Saved/EngineWire, Saved/Exports, Saved/Thumbnails, Saved/unreal-mcp, tmp/unreal-mcp or temp/unreal-mcp can be reached.

system_control.edit_save_game.summary: Change a SaveGame slot on disk: set saved properties and write it again (a missing slot is created from saveGameClass), or delete the slot.

system_control.enable_plugin.summary: Enable or disable a plugin, or limit it to some build targets: targets ["Editor"] keeps an editor-only plugin out of the packaged game.

system_control.execute_python.summary: Run Python in the editor: inline code (1 MB at most) or a .py file inside the project (a path outside it, or reached through a symlink, is SECURITY_VIOLATION). Needs the Python Editor Script Plugin (PYTHON_NOT_AVAILABLE otherwise) and an explicit consent grant; dialogs answer their default. The reply gives what the script printed (output) and, when it raised, the traceback (error).

system_control.fit_frame_budget.summary: Bring the level viewport's GPU frame time under budgetMs by turning down per-actor knobs at the least change to the picture, kept as one undo step.
