Each knob is switched on in turn and off again straight after, each state measured (the lower quartile of 16 frames' GPU times), so its gain is the difference of two measures a moment apart, and judged by how much of the picture it changes beyond the renderer's own noise against the picture just before it (as describe_view compareWith judges): a movable light casting shadows into the view (its shadows off), and the small meshes in the view beyond 20, 40 or 80 m (not drawn past that distance). The cheapest set whose gains reach the budget is picked, measured together and kept. The reply lists every knob tried (knobs: gainMs, changed as % of the picture, chosen), predictedMs, measuredMs, met, applied, and change (where the picture changed, with the actors drawn there before and after). It measures what the editor draws now, at its scalability and viewport size, from the view location, rotation and fov give, never in Play; at shadow quality Low no dynamic shadows are drawn, so lights are not tried (a warning says so: raise the Shadow group with set_scalability to measure them). A view already within the budget answers at once; when the knobs cannot reach it nothing changes and the reply says how close every knob together comes. dryRun measures and picks without keeping. Answers in about 3-20 s, the editor window held on screen meanwhile. Refusals: EDITOR_STATE_MISMATCH during Play, NO_VIEWPORT, NOTHING_TO_TRY (no knob in this view: move it to where the frame is slow), GPU_TIMING_UNAVAILABLE (turn on enable_gpu_timing), VIEWPORT_CHANGED (the viewport closed, resized or Play started mid-run; nothing changed).
terms: cheapest way to hit the frame time

system_control.get_plugin_info.summary: Read one plugin from its descriptor: name, description, category, version, author, enabled state and its default, type (engine, project, ...), beta and experimental flags, mounted content path, its modules (type, loading phase), the plugins it needs (dependencies) and the installed plugins that need it (dependents, a disabled one marked). assetPath instead finds the plugin whose content holds that asset; one under /Game, /Engine or /Script is no plugin's and is refused PLUGIN_NOT_FOUND, as is a name no installed plugin has.

system_control.get_project_settings.summary: Read project settings: with no section, the engine version, project name and directory, default maps and general settings; with a section or category (rendering, input, physics, audio, packaging...), every config property of it, or one key's value.

system_control.get_trace_status.summary: Read the Unreal Insights trace session status (connected, destination, active channels, connection type, paused); info=analyze reads a .utrace file's existence, size and modified time.

system_control.launch_build.summary: Start the packaged Win64 game of this project for a short smoke run (offscreen by default), on its default map or a given level, close it after the run, and return a jobId to poll with package_status.

system_control.list_game_features.summary: List the game feature plugins the Game Features subsystem knows (plugins under Plugins/GameFeatures that load on demand), each with its state (installed, registered, loaded or active, else the engine's own name for a step on the way, such as Activating, or an error, such as ErrorRegistering) and the state its descriptor asks for at startup (initialState). Needs the GameFeatures plugin: GAME_FEATURES_DISABLED otherwise (GAME_FEATURES_UNAVAILABLE in a build of EngineWire without its game features module, such as the Fab one).

system_control.list_output_files.summary: List the files the MCP itself wrote: screenshots (Saved/Screenshots), captures and contact sheets (Saved/Captures), EngineWire's own files (Saved/EngineWire: recipes, the asset index and captions, level layout images, plugins remove_plugin moved aside), mesh exports (Saved/Exports, export_mesh's default), thumbnails (Saved/Thumbnails) and environment snapshots (Saved/unreal-mcp, tmp/unreal-mcp, temp/unreal-mcp).

system_control.list_plugins.summary: List every plugin discovered by this editor with its enabled state, category, version and mounted content path; enabledOnly and filter (name or category) narrow the list.

system_control.list_recipes.summary: List the project's recipes: name, summary, paramNames, destructive, and verified (the engine version and time of the last run that succeeded) when a run has. query keeps those whose name or summary holds every word of it.

system_control.list_save_games.summary: List the game's SaveGame slots (Saved/SaveGames), or read one slot as the game loads it: its SaveGame class and every saved property value.
terms: load the game or a save slot

system_control.lumen_update_scene.summary: Ask Lumen to recapture its scene (r.Lumen.Scene.Recapture) in the editor world, after big changes to lighting or geometry; nothing checks that Lumen is on, so executed only means the command ran.

system_control.merge_actors.summary: Merge the static meshes of two or more placed actors into one saved static mesh asset named SM_<name>, materials kept as separate slots and lightmap UVs generated. A name that matches no actor, fewer than two static mesh components, or an asset already at the path is refused. replaceSourceActors places the merged mesh where the merge centred it and removes the sources in one undo step (actorName is the new actor); without it the level is left as it is.
terms: merge the walls or the floor into one mesh

system_control.package_project.summary: Start a project package (cook, stage, pak, archive), optionally under its own executable name, and return a jobId to poll; the build runs asynchronously in the editor.

system_control.package_status.summary: Report a job started by package_project or launch_build: running, succeeded or failed, with elapsed time and logs; a launch_build job adds the game log tail and its error count.

system_control.play_sound.summary: Play a sound asset (soundPath: a SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound Source) as a 2D preview in the editor, tied to no place, at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds; with no soundPath it plays the editor's compile-success chime. A looping sound keeps playing until manage_audio stop_sound. A path that loads no sound is ASSET_NOT_FOUND, and an editor with sound off answers NOT_PLAYED.

system_control.profile_performance.summary: Measure performance, chosen by control. benchmark samples every frame for duration seconds (default 10) and answers averageFps, frame times and game, render and GPU thread times; start and stop record a .uestats file under Saved/Profiling for Unreal Insights (no MCP action reads it); memory_report runs memreport (detailed: memreport -full) and answers the .memreport file it wrote (reportPath, reportIsNew); show_stats turns an on-screen stat overlay on or off. A minimized or unfocused editor is throttled and measures slow. To find what makes a frame slow, inspect get_stats with stats frame names the busiest thread and what in view weighs on it.

system_control.read_log.summary: Read the newest editor log lines (kept since editor start), filtered by text, category or minimum severity, or read the build (UnrealBuildTool), Live Coding or previous-run log instead; returns the lines and a match count.

system_control.remove_cpp_class.summary: Remove a C++ class from a project module once nothing uses it: its header and .cpp (<Name>.h and <Name>.cpp, as create_cpp_class names them) are deleted. Refused, nothing deleted, while something uses it (CLASS_IN_USE, the users named): an object of it is loaded (an actor placed in an open level), a Blueprint or a C++ class derives from it, an asset on disk points at it (the packages that use its module are loaded and searched), or another source file of the project includes its header or names it. A header that declares other reflected types too is refused (FILE_HOLDS_MORE), and so is a module more than 50 packages use (TOO_MANY_PACKAGES). The class stays loaded in this editor until the editor target is built with the editor closed and the editor opens again.

system_control.remove_plugin.summary: Take a plugin that no longer loads out of this project: its folder moves to Saved/EngineWire/RemovedPlugins/<name> (delete_output_file deletes its files there for good; moving it back restores it) and the .uproject drops it. A plugin this editor has loaded is refused PLUGIN_LOADED (only a restart unloads one: disable_plugin it, restart the editor, then remove it). Only a plugin in this project's Plugins folder with no code is removed; an engine or marketplace plugin, or one with code (modules or a Source folder), is refused PLUGIN_NOT_REMOVABLE. A refusal changes nothing; MOVE_FAILED (a file in it is open) leaves the project as it was.
terms: remove a plugin from the project

system_control.run_build.summary: Run automation tests and answer with each one's result (passed or not, its errors and warnings), or run UnrealBuildTool for a target.

system_control.run_recipe.summary: Run a recipe saved with save_recipe: args gives each parameter a value (bound as (let name value) before its first line), and the script runs exactly as run_script runs one: every step checked as a direct execute is, its destructive steps covered by this call's one consent, and everything rolled back when a step or an expectation fails. A run that succeeds marks the recipe verified with the engine version. RECIPE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown name, RECIPE_ARGS when args lacks a parameter.

system_control.run_script.summary: Run a script of capability calls in one request, on every UE 5.x, in the S-expression grammar of read_graph_as_code: (let name (capability.id :param value ...)) calls a capability and keeps what it returns (what a direct execute returns: its declared output fields, the rest under details), name.field.0.field reads into it; (for item list ...) goes over a list, (range n) counts 0 to n-1; (if cond ... (else ...)) runs statements, and as a value (if cond a b) picks a when cond is true, b when not, evaluating only the one picked: (let z (if (> n 0) 100 0)); (expect "assertion") checks the editor in execute's expect language (Crate1.location.z in 0..100, Lamp on Table; the text can be made as it runs: (expect (+ c.label " on Floor"))); (return value) ends the script with its result. Expressions: (not a), (and a b), (or a b), (== a b), (!= a b), (< a b), (<= a b), (> a b), (>= a b), (+ a b) (it also joins text: (+ "Crate_" i)), (- a b), (* a b), (/ a b), (list a b), (obj :x 1 :y 2), literals, null and names; a name is bound once in its block. The whole script is checked before anything runs: every call names a capability, with only parameters its contract declares and each one it requires, and every name is bound before use. Each call is then held to everything a direct execute is (its contract, the caller's scope and path limits, the console policy) and runs on its handler inside this one request; a call that answers later is waited for within deadlineMs, so a later call can use what it made. run_script always asks for elevated consent, and each capability the script calls that asks for consent must be named in destructive, which that one consent then covers. A failed call or expectation stops the script and rolls back what it changed, as far as editor undo reaches: a Blueprint compile or a level load clears the undo history (rollback then says what could not be undone), saved files stay saved, and assets it created are listed in cleanupCall. A script cannot call run_script, run_recipe, undo, redo or restore_point, an

system_control.save_recipe.summary: Keep a run_script script in the project as a named recipe with parameters, so a later call (or another agent) runs it as one checked call with run_recipe. The script is checked as run_script checks one, its parameters bound by name (each a variable the script reads); nothing runs at save time. destructive lists the destructive capabilities it calls, as run_script takes them, and run_recipe's consent covers exactly those. A taken name is refused (RECIPE_EXISTS) unless overwrite is true. Stored under Saved/EngineWire/Recipes/<name>.json.

system_control.screenshot.summary: Capture a screenshot as a PNG, returned inline (downscaled to fit 1600x900 unless resolution sets the box) and saved under Saved/Screenshots unless keepFile is false. mode editor_viewport, the default, shoots the level viewport; game_viewport the running game frame without its UMG widgets (path picks the folder; NO_VIEWPORT when no game runs); full_editor_window the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included (window picks another open window by index or title). returnBase64 false returns only the saved path, at full size.

system_control.set_game_feature_active.summary: Activate a game feature plugin (its content loads and its actions run in the game: components added, abilities granted, input mapped) or deactivate it (active false). The reply comes when the subsystem has finished, with the state reached, or after 20 seconds with GAME_FEATURE_PENDING while it is still on its way; one already in the asked state answers changed false. A name the subsystem does not know is GAME_FEATURE_NOT_FOUND; GAME_FEATURES_DISABLED when the project leaves the GameFeatures plugin off (GAME_FEATURES_UNAVAILABLE in a build of EngineWire without its game features module).

system_control.set_project_setting.summary: Set one setting (section and key): applied to the live settings object and saved where the editor itself saves that class, the project Default<Config>.ini for a project setting, the user Saved config for a per-user one (EditorPerProjectUserSettings). configFile names the file written.
terms: make the main menu the first level

system_control.set_project_thumbnail.summary: Set the project's thumbnail, the picture the Epic Games Launcher and the project browser show for it: the level viewport's view (from location, rotation and fov when given; they stay) drawn in game view (no editor icons or gizmos) as a square of size pixels and written to <ProjectDir>/<ProjectName>.png, the file the editor's own Capture Project Thumbnail writes. The reply shows the picture. Refused during Play In Editor (PIE_RUNNING).

system_control.start_session.summary: Unreal Insights: start, stop, pause or resume a trace session, capture a trace, send or write a snapshot, launch the Insights viewer.

system_control.subscribe.summary: Stream the editor log to this connection (subscribe, unsubscribe), or turn a Gameplay Debugger category on or off.

system_control.validate_assets.summary: Check that assets load without error, with dataValidation that they pass the project's and the engine's Data Validation (the editor's Validate Assets), and with materialUsage that their meshes' materials carry the usage flags a cooked game needs: each asset path, or every asset under a folder (recursive by default); returns isValid, per-path results and the checked and invalid counts.

texture.adjust_texture.summary: Edit the pixels of an 8-bit texture in place (assetPath; a 16-bit or HDR source is refused, and a grayscale one becomes BGRA8), chosen by adjust: curves maps the channel through curvePoints ({x, y} pairs from 0 to 1, at least two); levels remaps inBlack to inWhite (0 to 1) with gamma; blur averages over radius (default 2, 1 to 10); sharpen at strength (default 1, up to 5); desaturate by amount (default 1, fully gray); invert flips the colors. channel picks R, G, B or A for curves, levels and invert (otherwise the three color channels). The texture is saved unless save is false (saved), with no undo, so duplicate it first to keep the original; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT).

texture.configure_texture.summary: Change one setting of a 2D texture asset (assetPath), chosen by setting; the texture is saved unless save is false (saved). compression sets compressionSettings by engine name, with or without the TC_ prefix (Normalmap, Masks, Grayscale, HDR, EditorIcon for UI, BC7 ...); texture_group sets textureGroup, with or without TEXTUREGROUP_ (World, Character, UI, Effects ...), so the texture follows that group's LOD and streaming rules; an unknown name in either is refused with the valid names. lod_bias drops lodBias top mips at runtime (1 halves each side, 0 restores full size). virtual_texture sets virtualTextureStreaming (required); materials sampling the texture then need the matching sampler type (Virtual Color and so on, or back) or they stop compiling. streaming_priority sets neverStream (required): true keeps every mip resident; there is no per-texture streaming priority.

texture.create_texture.summary: Create a texture: gradient, noise, pattern, text, normal from height, ambient occlusion baked from a mesh, resized copy, channel pack/extract, or a combination of two textures.

texture.get_texture_info.summary: Read a 2D texture asset: width and height, pixel format, mip count, sRGB, compression setting, LOD bias, and virtual texture and never-stream flags.
